items.title: Mets manager Andy Green sheds interim tag, signs 3-year deal
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The New York Mets removed the interim tag on manager Andy Green and signed him to a three-year contract on Tuesday.
items.body:
The New York Mets removed the interim tag on manager Andy Green and signed him to a three-year contract on Tuesday.
The Mets are 37-38 with six games remaining in the regular season under Green, who took over after Carlos Mendoza was fired on June 26 with a 34-47 mark at the halfway point.
"Andy has connected with and pushed our players to perform, despite the disappointment of the season," owners Steve and Alex Cohen said in a news release. "Over the last several months, he has brought discipline, accountability and positivity to the clubhouse, attributes we were seeking in our next manager."
Mendoza, 46, was 206-199 during his two-plus seasons as manager of the Mets, who are in the cellar of the National League East this year despite a payroll of about $356 million. They endured a 12-game losing streak in April and had lost six straight when Green, who was with the club in a player development role, was named interim manager.
"When I accepted the interim role, I didn't anticipate it becoming permanent, but the more time I spent with our players and staff, the clearer it became that this is where my passion and experience could make the greatest impact," Green, 49, said in the news release.
"That realization led to many conversations with my family, and together we agreed this is the right opportunity at the right time," added Green, who previously served as senior vice president of baseball development.
Green had previous management experience with the San Diego Padres, who went 274-366 (.428) from 2016-19. He also was bench coach of the Chicago Cubs (2020-23).
He was a major league infielder for parts of four seasons with the Arizona Diamondbacks (2004-06) and Mets (four games in 2009).
"Over the course of the season, it became evident that the next manager of the New York Mets was already in place," Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns said in the news release. "Andy has demonstrated strong leadership qualities and a unique ability to forge connections with our emerging core and distinguished veterans. I look forward to continuing our great partnership as we turn toward the 2027 season."
The Mets last made the playoffs in 2024, advancing to the National League Championship Series where they lost to the eventual World Series-champion Los Angeles Dodgers in six games.
--Field Level Media

items.title: IN FOCUS: 'I cannot go back' - Myanmar refugees fear repatriation as country gets cosier with Malaysia, Thailand
items.author: Rashvinjeet S Bedi

IN FOCUS: 'I cannot go back' - Myanmar refugees fear repatriation as country gets cosier with Malaysia, Thailand

Thailand and Malaysia have been a safe haven for hundreds of thousands of Myanmar nationals fleeing conflict, but recent developments have stoked worries among the refugees.

FAST

KUALA LUMPUR/BANGKOK: Nearly 20 years ago, 54-year-old Mohamed Sadek fled Rakhine State in western Myanmar to Malaysia, desperate to escape possible persecution and violence. 
Three years ago, 39-year-old Lele Khine was forced to make the same decision. She fled Myanmar's southernmost region of Tanintharyi, trading everything she knew for the life of a refugee in Thailand. 
Today, they are terrified by the possibility of being sent back. 
As host nations across Southeast Asia shift their policy postures, thousands of displaced Myanmar refugees in Malaysia and Thailand worry their safe havens may be vanishing. 
Following a 2021 military coup, the  Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) has excluded Myanmar from high-level meetings as it has yet to make meaningful progress on the bloc's Five-Point Consensus to end hostilities. 
The consensus calls for an immediate cessation of violence, constructive dialogue among all parties, the appointment of a special envoy to mediate talks, humanitarian assistance and the envoy's access to all parties concerned. 
Analysts say mounting public fatigue on refugees and domestic political expediency were among factors that drove the policy shifts.    
Malaysia has announced plans to return 5,000 Myanmar refugees, with the Home Ministry announcing that the first 1,476 people - whose ethnicities have not been disclosed - are scheduled to depart Malaysia on Sep 29 on board two Myanmar Navy warships and a hospital ship. 
Malaysia Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Sep 16 he would invite Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing for an official visit in return for his government accepting the return of thousands of Rohingya Muslim refugees. 
"Why did I invite him? I invited him because I want to tell him that we can be friends and trade. We can accept Myanmar, but they must accept (its refugees) back," said Anwar.
Thailand, meanwhile, has been leading an effort to normalise relations with Myanmar, both bilaterally and through the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). 
Myanmar leader  Min Aung Hlaing made an official visit  to the country on Aug 6.

Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul (left) and Myanmar's President Min Aung Hlaing review an honour guard during a welcome ceremony at the Government House in Bangkok, Thailand, on Aug 6, 2026. (Photo: AP/Sakchai Lalit)

Days after the visit, Thai authorities raided an undocumented Karen community in Kaeng Krachan National Park, arresting 28 villagers including children and pregnant women and slating 26 people for deportation to Myanmar. 
Thailand has also enacted a new law authorising the swift deportation of foreign nationals who violate domestic regulations – a measure human rights activists warn will leave refugees more vulnerable to forced repatriation.
According to the United Nations refugee agency’s figures from February, Malaysia has a total of 193,824 refugees from Myanmar. They include 126,144 Rohingya, 15,774 Chin, and 33,002 individuals from other ethnic groups. 
Thailand has over 90,000 refugees from Myanmar – mainly Karen, Karenni and Burmese ethnicity – at nine temporary shelters run by the Thai government on the border.
Indonesia – another major refugee-hosting Southeast Asian country – has around 2,800 Myanmar refugees because it is seen as a transit country with limited work opportunities and is more difficult to access geographically. 
Human rights watchers say the situation in Myanmar is still not conducive for the safe return of those who originally fled the country. 
But Malaysia has said the repatriation programme is voluntary, while Myanmar has pledged "safe and dignified" returns for its citizens displaced abroad.
Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has, so far, directed the authorities to  fully exercise their legal powers for offences such as aggressive behaviour, illegal business operations and landholdings, and actions deemed disrespectful to Thai culture.

Rohingya refugee Mohamed Sadek, 54, formerly ran a school for refugee children in Ampang, Kuala Lumpur. (Photo: CNA/Fadza Ishak)

WHY THEY FLED Malaysia and Thailand are top destinations for Myanmar refugees due to their geographic closeness and established support networks, despite the fact that neither country has ratified the United Nations (UN) Refugee Convention or formally recognises refugees. 
The displacement of Myanmar nationals into Thailand and Malaysia spans nearly four decades, unfolding across three primary historical waves driven by military offensives, ethnic violence and political crackdowns. 
Refugees in both countries told CNA the time was not right to return to their homeland.  
Khine fled to southern Thailand in 2023 because of fighting between the military and rebel forces. 
Her husband, 41,  had fled more than a year earlier, and she joined him after he saved enough money to get her across. Together, they worked to bring their three children, aged 9 to 15, to safety.
“We came because of the political crisis in Myanmar. We could hear bombs dropping from the sky. I was very worried about my family,” she said. 
Khine now lives in a coastal area in southern Thailand and works at a seafood processing plant. She worries that Thailand will start cooperating with the Myanmar government and send Myanmarese back, particularly men like her husband who may be forced to join the military.
In 2024, the Myanmar government announced that all men aged 18 to 35, and women aged 18 to 27, had to serve at least two years under military command.
“But it is not safe there for my family. I don’t think peace will ever be achieved if both sides continue to fight,” said Khine. 
Just three months ago, the Myanmar military searched every house in her village for rebel fighters, she said.
That same anxiety is felt hundreds of kilometres away in Kuala Lumpur. 
James Bawi Thang Bik, a Chin refugee living in the Malaysian capital, told CNA the reports of 5,000 refugees in Malaysia facing repatriation came as a profound shock. 
“We hope that things will change and that we can go back to Myanmar one day, but the whole Chin state and Myanmar is a complete war zone. There isn’t any peace in the country,” said Bawi, who has been in Malaysia for almost 15 years. 
He had fled Malaysia to escape conscription to the army, and said youngsters in Myanmar today still face the same risk.

Ye Htet, 29, fled his village in Mon State, Myanmar four years ago because men in the village were forced to become soldiers. (Photo: CNA/Wisnu Agung Prasetyo)

Ye Htet, a 29-year-old from Mon State, said this was the reason he fled Myanmar four years ago. 
"I know people who were forced to become soldiers. I knew that if I stayed, sooner or later they would come for me," said Ye Htet, who now works on a rubber plantation in southern Thailand.
He made the gruelling three-day trek through forests and mountains to reach the Thai border and, when he finally crossed into Thailand, he said he felt safe for the first time in years.
He believed he had escaped the shadow of the war, but those fears have returned as Bangkok deepens its engagement with Naypyidaw.
"I miss my home. I miss my family. No matter what, Thailand is not my country,” he said. 
“But I cannot go back in the foreseeable future. For someone my age, if I return to Myanmar, I will become a soldier for sure,” he added. 
"I don’t want to fight anyone. I don’t want to kill anyone. But if they make me a soldier, I will have no choice. I think I will die."
As for the Rohingya, who have been described as the most persecuted minority in the world, refugees such as Sadek said he was grateful for Malaysia’s provision of a safe haven and hopes the country will not send back people who may face danger on their return.
“Myanmar is my country but it is not safe for us. We came here not to stay here forever, but to make preparations to return one day. Unfortunately, we cannot do that at the moment,” he said. 
“I’m not sure what agreement they made, but I don’t believe Malaysia will send anyone whose life is in danger back to Myanmar,” he said.  
“The Rohingya must be resettled to third countries where they can find a permanent home. Many have been here since the 1980s but are still in limbo,” he said, also questioning whether there was any urgency to resettle the Rohingya. 
Hundreds of thousands of Rohingya fled Myanmar in 2017 following a military crackdown. 
Many fled across the border to Bangladesh, where they recently rallied for safe return to Rakhine state in Myanmar and protested the dire conditions of refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, where some have lived for nine years. 
The Bangladeshi government has reportedly tried to begin repatriation at least twice previously. But none of the refugees were willing to return, citing security concerns in Myanmar, and Dhaka said it would not force anyone to go back.
In August, the Myanmar government said more than 300,000 people living in camps in Bangladesh are former residents of Rakhine state and that it will  accept their return once security conditions improve , wire agencies reported.

Related:

Myanmar leader in Russia on diplomatic push, even as legal risks complicate travel elsewhere

Malaysia foreign minister calls for review of UN refugee agency's presence: Reports

WHY HOST COUNTRIES ARE ACTING NOW Observers attribute the shifting postures of Southeast Asian host countries to mounting public fatigue on refugees, with Thailand and Malaysia feeling the immediate effects of the crisis much more than others.
Teuku Rezasyah, an international relations expert from Indonesia’s President University, said that these countries are dealing with the spillover of refugees and have vested interests in finding solutions.  
“They are growing impatient and, because of that, they start to improvise,” he said.
“Thailand has accommodated them, but the question is what happens if the conflict continues for many more years. One day, this can become a serious domestic problem for Thailand.”
He added that Myanmar understood Thailand's strategic importance, and likely hopes Bangkok could influence the rest of ASEAN to become more accepting of the current regime. 
Thailand is scheduled to assume the ASEAN chairmanship in 2028. 
“From Myanmar's perspective, it potentially has a powerful ally within ASEAN during this period. Thailand could become very important in shaping how ASEAN approaches Myanmar,” he said. 
There could be a diplomatic incentive for Myanmar’s government to take back the refugees, said Khoo Ying Hooi of Universiti Malaya's International and Strategic Studies Department.
“Engagement with Anwar allows Myanmar’s authorities to demonstrate that, despite ASEAN’s restrictions on high-level participation since the 2021 coup, they can still conduct bilateral diplomacy with ASEAN governments,” she said.
The concern is not whether Myanmar is willing to receive the refugees, she said, but how Malaysia can guarantee those being returned will be safe, protected and treated with dignity. 
Besides Thailand, Min Aung Hlaing has made trips to Vietnam and Cambodia recently. 
In an August interview with Thai PBS World, Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said there has been “measurable progress” to justify “calibrated re-engagement” with Myanmar. 
He cited the release of political prisoners and the moving of Myanmar’s democracy icon Aung San Suu Kyi from a prison to a “designated residence”. Aung San Suu Kyi was also allowed to meet a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross.
Sihasak said Thailand has to live with the “reality” in Myanmar, as continued fighting between Myanmar government forces and ethnic armed groups has driven thousands to cross over to Thailand, which is also grappling with cross-border pollution and scam operations originating in Myanmar.
He said there are also concerns among ASEAN countries that an isolated Myanmar risks becoming an arena for major power rivalry.

A Rohingya refugee uses her phone as she and other members of the community gather in front of the office of the UN Refugee Agency in Kuala Lumpur on Jul 27, 2026 after being evicted from their homes. (Photo: Reuters/Hasnoor Hussain)

As for Malaysia, Teuku said its current stance represents a sharp departure from its historic openness toward displaced Muslim populations. 
But  negative sentiments are growing partly due to disinformation and a lack of knowledge about what actually happened to the Rohingya in Myanmar, Teuku said.
“In a difficult economy, this can easily create envy and resentment. It can then be exploited through social media and disinformation,” he said. 
In June, the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia said it had observed growing hostility, discriminatory rhetoric, and online attacks directed at the Rohingya community. 
In late July, locals evicted over 100 Rohingya refugees from their homes in Penang, leaving them no choice but to pitch camp outside the UNHCR office in Kuala Lumpur. 
Local authorities and aid groups later relocated the individuals to temporary housing arranged by NGOs and the UNHCR across Kuala Lumpur, Selangor and Penang. 
This shifting political climate has affected the community's daily life, leading to the closure of several Rohingya learning centers across the country in recent months. 
Sadek noted that a school he operated in Kuala Lumpur for seven years was forced to shut down a few months ago for lacking valid operational permits. 
“We can only respect the Malaysian law,” he said wryly. 

Books sit on a shelf inside a former school for refugee children in Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, on Aug 21, 2026. (Photo: CNA/Fadza Ishak)

Mahi Ramakrishnan, founder of the refugee advocacy group Beyond Borders, believes the  mood of the electorate in the run-up to the country’s next general election, due by February 2028, may be a factor. 
“I really think it’s about the next election following a string of severe defeats in several state polls,” she said, referring to the ruling  Pakatan Harapan’s performance in recent state elections in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan .
Anwar on Sep 16 acknowledged in a podcast the suffering of the Rohingya, but said Malaysia could not accommodate them permanently, Reuters reported.
He said Myanmar has accepted the return of 5,000 refugees, with Kuala Lumpur bearing the repatriation cost, and the expectation was that more would be returned later in stages.    
"To me, that's better diplomacy than just shouting angrily at Myanmar. Who's going to take them? Where do we send them? They don't even have Myanmar citizenship," Anwar said.
"Previously we didn't negotiate because we didn't recognise them," he said of Min Aung Hlaing's government. "We're not simply going to recognise and negotiate for no reason." 

Malaysia Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim (left) passes the ceremonial gavel to Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr (right) at the closing ceremony of the 47th ASEAN Summit on Oct 28, 2025. The Philippines is ASEAN's 2026 chair. (Photo: CNA/Zamzahuri Abas)

Indonesian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Yvonne Mewengkang said Indonesia is closely monitoring the Myanmar leader’s diplomatic tour.
“In principle, Myanmar’s bilateral relations with those countries are a matter within the authority and rights of each country, and this definitely does not automatically affect ASEAN centrality itself,” Yvonne said at a press briefing in Jakarta on Sep 17. She was referring to the bloc’s ability to play a leading role in addressing various issues that affect the region.
Indonesia therefore continues to view ASEAN as having an important role in helping Myanmar find solutions to its challenges. Mewengkang said ASEAN’s five-point consensus “will remain ASEAN’s primary framework for helping Myanmar find a peaceful, inclusive, and sustainable solution”.

items.title: Trump apoia proibição da exportação de diesel conforme preços dos combustíveis atingem níveis recordes
items.author: Gram Slattery, Ryan Patrick Jones, Timothy Gardner
items.creator: Gram Slattery, Ryan Patrick Jones, Timothy Gardner
items.summary: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta terça-feira que apoiava a proibição das exportações de diesel, enquanto candidatos republicanos em algumas das disputas eleitorais mais acirradas de novembro defendiam a medida como forma de conter os preços recordes dos combustíveis.
items.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta terça-feira que apoiava a proibição das exportações de diesel, enquanto candidatos republicanos em algumas das disputas eleitorais mais acirradas de novembro defendiam a medida como forma de conter os preços recordes dos combustíveis.
Os preços do diesel atingiram níveis recordes nos EUA e na Europa, à medida que as guerras no Irã e na Ucrânia reduziram drasticamente as exportações de alguns dos maiores produtores, como Rússia, Arábia Saudita e Emirados Árabes Unidos.
“Eu disse: ‘Não vamos exportar o diesel. Produzimos muito diesel... Eu pedi isso. Eu pedi isso à minha equipe’”, disse Trump a repórteres antes de uma reunião com o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy.
Os altos preços dos combustíveis são um ponto fraco para Trump nas eleições de 3 de novembro, nas quais os republicanos tentam manter a maioria nas duas Casas do Congresso.
O secretário do Tesouro dos EUA, Scott Bessent, falando na mesma reunião, disse que o governo estava analisando se tal proibição seria viável e se uma proibição total ou parcial funcionaria.
Vários candidatos republicanos nas disputas eleitorais mais acirradas para o Congresso em todo o país, como o senador Dan Sullivan, do Alasca, a deputada federal Ashley Hinson, de Iowa, e Mike Rogers, de Michigan, pediram que o governo Trump implementasse a proibição.
“O combustível americano deve ficar aqui com os americanos”, disse Sullivan em comunicado nesta terça-feira. “O custo do diesel está simplesmente alto demais. Estou pedindo uma suspensão temporária das exportações de diesel americano para que possamos reconstruir nossas reservas antes do inverno e colocar as famílias americanas e do Alasca em primeiro lugar.”
A acessibilidade dos alimentos e de outros bens está no topo das preocupações dos eleitores antes das eleições de meio de mandato.
Hinson e Rogers também pediram, na segunda-feira, o fim imediato da guerra no Irã, distanciando-se de Trump.
O Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA instou, na semana passada, a Casa Branca a tomar medidas em relação aos preços do diesel, segundo duas fontes a par do assunto. A secretária de Agricultura, Brooke Rollins, disse na segunda-feira que havia conversado com Trump sobre o assunto, classificando os preços altos como “uma preocupação real”, segundo o Politico.
AUTORIDADES DO SETOR DE ENERGIA ALERTAM PARA OS RISCOS O apoio de Trump à proibição da exportação de diesel o coloca em desacordo com suas próprias autoridades do setor de energia, que alertam que isso poderia elevar os preços dos combustíveis nas regiões costeiras e reduzir o abastecimento para os aliados europeus.
O secretário de Energia, Chris Wright, disse em um evento do Daily Caller na semana passada que uma proibição levaria a um excesso de diesel na Costa do Golfo dos EUA e levaria as refinarias norte-americanas a reduzir as taxas de produção, o que diminuiria rapidamente a produção de gasolina. “Se você começar a impor barreiras aos fluxos, rapidamente reduzirá a produção e terá menos oferta. Precisamos de mais oferta, não de menos”, disse Wright.
Doug Burgum, secretário do Interior dos EUA, disse que é improvável que uma proibição reduza os preços do petróleo e que isso poderia levar a medidas retaliatórias por parte dos países exportadores de energia, dos quais Estados como a Califórnia dependem para parte de seu abastecimento energético.
O setor petrolífero também se opôs à proibição. Todd Staples, presidente da TXOGA, uma associação comercial de petróleo e gás natural do Texas, disse que isso “prejudicaria os empregos no mercado interno, levaria à escassez de combustível no país e colocaria o poder nas mãos da China e da Rússia, forçando nossos aliados a recorrer a esses países para suprir suas necessidades”.
Embora uma proibição à exportação de diesel pudesse, em teoria, reduzir temporariamente os preços na Costa do Golfo dos EUA, ela restringiria ainda mais a oferta na Europa, que sofre com uma escassez estrutural de diesel e depende fortemente das exportações dos EUA.
“Isso pareceria bastante prejudicial para alguns aliados-chave dos EUA”, disse Jim Mitchell, diretor de análises de comercialização de petróleo da consultoria Wood Mackenzie.
Trump disse que ele e Zelenskiy discutiriam os ataques ucranianos a refinarias de petróleo na Rússia.
“É um golpe sério para os russos. É também um golpe sério para o preço do diesel”, disse Trump, que também informou aos repórteres que os dois líderes discutiriam uma solução para pôr fim à guerra da Rússia na Ucrânia.
“Acho que isso vai acontecer”, disse Trump.

items.title: US Treasury secretary could take on AI czar role, source says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent could become President Donald Trump’s new AI czar, a source familiar with the discussions said on Tuesday, as fears grow among lawmakers in Washington about the risks posed by AI technology.
items.body:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent could become President Donald Trump’s new AI czar, a source familiar with the discussions said on Tuesday, as fears grow among lawmakers in Washington about the risks posed by AI technology.
Trump has repeatedly downplayed concerns about AI and argued that additional regulation is unnecessary.
The Treasury had no immediate comment on Bessent's possible new role, which was first reported by Semafor. A second source told Reuters that no decision had been made.
Trump on Saturday said that he plans to appoint an artificial intelligence adviser, [USN:FWN45B02T TEXT:"known as an "AI czar,""] and create an "AI force," though he did not provide details about either initiative or how they would be implemented.
Bessent led talks on Sunday with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York ahead of this week's summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington. The talks focused heavily on AI.
Bessent told reporters after the talks that Washington had proposed an [USN:L1N45B04Y TEXT:"AI safety notification mechanism"] and US-China AI dialogue, with a particular emphasis on national security concerns.
Trump previously tapped Bessent, a former hedge fund manager, to play a lead role in a major revamp of US trade policy, negotiate with Ukraine about critical minerals and temporarily head the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.
He also serves as acting commissioner of the Internal Revenue Service, and his Treasury is leading a push to isolate Iran economically through sanctions and other measures.

items.title: Anthony Scaramucci's "All the Wrong Moves"
items.summary: Former Trump Administration official and Founder of Skybridge, Anthony Scaramucci, is out with a new book "All the Wrong Moves: How Three Catastrophic Decisions Led to the Rise of Trump." He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the lessons he learned from his time on Wall Street to his short-lived time in the White House and extended exposure to the Trump-world. He tries to make the case for what bipartisan money mistakes lead to today's "political crisis" and how we can get out of it. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Video antiguo se comparte erróneamente como protesta en 2026 por un apuñalamiento en Reino Unido
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Un video que muestra a manifestantes lanzando objetos contra policías después de que un hombre británico matara a tres niñas en 2024 se comparte erróneamente en línea como si mostrara disturbios por el apuñalamiento de una niña por parte de un solicitante de asilo.
items.body:
Un video que muestra a manifestantes lanzando objetos contra policías después de que un hombre británico matara a tres niñas en 2024 se comparte erróneamente en línea como si mostrara disturbios por el apuñalamiento de una niña por parte de un solicitante de asilo.
Un ejemplo que difundió el video en Facebook el 30 de agosto dice: “La turba en el Reino Unido después de que otra niña pequeña fuera apuñalada por un solicitante de asilo”.
Sin embargo, el video se publicó en línea el 30 de julio de 2024 y muestra protestas violentas en Southport, en el noroeste de Inglaterra, después de que un hombre nacido en Reino Unido matara a tres niñas en un evento temático de Taylor Swift en la localidad.
Un portavoz de la Policía de Merseyside dijo que las imágenes fueron grabadas durante los disturbios de esa fecha.
Una comparación del clip con imágenes en Google Maps de la calle St Luke's en Southport, que la policía de Merseyside dijo fue escenario de disturbios ese día, muestra los mismos inmuebles y vegetación.
Axel Rudakubana, de 18 años y nacido en Gales, [USN:S8N3HP021 TEXT:"admitió"] posteriormente haber matado a las niñas y apuñalado a otras 10 personas. Fue [USN:L5N3OJ0TU TEXT:"condenado"] a al menos 52 años de prisión.
La violencia estalló en Reino Unido ese año tras [USN:L6N3JM0G0 TEXT:"falsas acusaciones"] difundidas en línea de que el sospechoso era un solicitante de asilo que llegó en barco antes de que se diera a conocer la identidad de Rudakubana.
Reuters no encontró informes creíbles sobre un solicitante de asilo que hubiera apuñalado a una chica al momento de la publicación difundida en redes sociales. Un portavoz de la policía de Merseyside por su parte dijo que no ha atendido ningún caso reciente que pudiera describirse como “un solicitante de asilo apuñalando a una chica”.
VEREDICTO Erróneamente etiquetado. El vídeo muestra disturbios en Southport en 2024 después de que un hombre nacido en Reino Unido matara a tres niñas en un evento temático de Taylor Swift, y no se trata de una protesta reciente por un solicitante de asilo que haya apuñalado a una chica.
Reuters Fact Check ofrece información confiable mediante su canal de WhatsApp para México . Envíenos un mensaje con el contenido en español que desea que verifiquemos.
Este artículo fue realizado por el equipo de Reuters Fact Check. Lea más sobre nuestro trabajo de verificación de afirmaciones en las redes sociales.

items.title: 'Looksmaxxing' influencer Clavicular charged with rape in Massachusetts
items.author: Nate Raymond
items.creator: Nate Raymond
items.summary: The social media "looksmaxxing" influencer known as Clavicular has been charged with raping a 17-year-old girl who told police she became intoxicated at his family's home on Massachusetts' Cape Cod after he invited her to join him on live stream videos.
items.body:
The social media "looksmaxxing" influencer known as Clavicular has been charged with raping a 17-year-old girl who told police she became intoxicated at his family's home on Massachusetts' Cape Cod after he invited her to join him on live stream videos.
Braden Peters, 20, was charged with rape, drugging a person for sexual intercourse, and procuring alcohol for someone under 21, according to a criminal complaint issued on September 8. He is slated to be arraigned in a state court in Orleans, Massachusetts on October 14.
His spokesperson Mitchell Jackson said the accuser had previously filed a lawsuit against Peters. He said the accuser and her attorney went to the police after Peters moved to dismiss the case and "refused to pay money."
"Looksmaxxing" is an online subculture focused on maximizing people's physical attractiveness. Peters has become a face of the trend, garnering a large following on social media platforms like TikTok and becoming known for endorsing a practice of breaking facial bones with a hammer to have them grow back stronger, which medical experts advise against.
According to court documents, Peters' accuser went to the police in Chatham to report him on June 4.
She told police the two had initially messaged each other on Instagram and he later paid her to be in “looksmaxxing” videos he produced.
The accuser, whose name was redacted from the charging documents, said that after about a week of talking, Peters ordered her an Uber to his family's residence in Chatham on May 23, 2025.
According to the police report, the accuser said Peters was aware she was 17 but told her to lie on a live stream he was recording on the platform Twitch and say she was 18 and that vodka he gave her was water.
The girl told police she became increasingly intoxicated. In a clip from Peters’ livestream that police reviewed, the girl at one point said, "wait I’m so drunk" before the two kissed, according to the police report.
She said she later fell asleep in Peters' bed and the next morning woke up to him "having sex with me" without consent.

items.title: Trump apoya una prohibición a la exportación de diésel mientras los precios alcanzan récords
items.author: Gram Slattery, Ryan Patrick Jones, Timothy Gardner
items.creator: Gram Slattery, Ryan Patrick Jones, Timothy Gardner
items.summary: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el martes que apoyaba una prohibición a las exportaciones de diésel, algo que candidatos republicanos para las elecciones legislativas de noviembre reclaman para frenar el alza de los precios del combustible.
items.body:
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el martes que apoyaba una prohibición a las exportaciones de diésel, algo que candidatos republicanos para las elecciones legislativas de noviembre reclaman para frenar el alza de los precios del combustible.
Los precios del gasóleo se han disparado a máximos históricos en Estados Unidos y Europa, ya que los conflictos en Irán y Ucrania han reducido drásticamente las exportaciones de algunos de los mayores productores, como Rusia, Arabia Saudita y los Emiratos Árabes Unidos.
"He dicho que no enviemos el diésel. Producimos mucho diésel (...) Lo he pedido. Se lo he pedido a mi equipo", dijo Trump a periodistas antes de una reunión con el presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski.
Los altos precios del combustible suponen un punto débil para Trump antes de las elecciones del 3 de noviembre, en las que los republicanos intentan mantener la mayoría en ambas cámaras del Congreso.
El secretario del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, Scott Bessent, en su intervención en la misma reunión, dijo que el Gobierno estaba estudiando si la prohibición era viable y si funcionaría una total o parcial.
Varios candidatos republicanos en las contiendas al Congreso más reñidas de todo el país, como el senador Dan Sullivan en Alaska, la diputada Ashley Hinson en Iowa y Mike Rogers en Míchigan, han pedido a la Administración Trump que aplique la prohibición.
"El combustible estadounidense debe quedarse en casa, con los estadounidenses", dijo Sullivan en un comunicado el martes.
"El precio del gasóleo es sencillamente demasiado alto. Pido una suspensión temporal de las exportaciones de gasóleo estadounidense para que podamos reponer nuestras reservas antes del invierno y dar prioridad a las familias estadounidenses y de Alaska", añadió.
La asequibilidad de los alimentos y otros productos es otra de las principales preocupaciones de los votantes.
Hinson y Rogers también pidieron el lunes un rápido fin a la guerra en Irán, distanciándose así de Trump.
El Departamento de Agricultura de Estados Unidos instó la semana pasada a la Casa Blanca a tomar medidas respecto de los precios del gasóleo, según dos fuentes familiarizadas con el asunto.
La secretaria de Agricultura, Brooke Rollins, dijo el lunes que había hablado con Trump sobre el asunto y calificó los altos precios de "una verdadera preocupación", según Politico.
ADVIERTEN DE RIESGOS El respaldo de Trump a la prohibición de exportar gasóleo lo enfrenta a sus propios responsables de energía, quienes advierten de que podría elevar los precios del combustible en las costas y reducir el suministro a los aliados europeos.
El secretario de Energía, Chris Wright, dijo la semana pasada en un acto organizado por The Daily Caller que una prohibición provocaría un exceso de oferta de gasóleo en la costa del golfo de México de Estados Unidos y llevaría a las refinerías estadounidenses a recortar sus tasas de producción, lo que reduciría rápidamente la producción de gasolina.
"Si empiezas a poner barreras a los flujos, muy pronto reducirás la producción y tendrás menos suministro. Necesitamos más suministro, no menos", dijo Wright.
Doug Burgum, secretario del Interior de Estados Unidos, señaló que es poco probable que una prohibición reduzca los precios del petróleo y que podría dar lugar a medidas de represalia por parte de los países exportadores de energía, de los que dependen estados como California para parte de su suministro energético.
Aunque una prohibición de la exportación de diésel podría, en teoría, reducir temporalmente los precios en la costa del Golfo de Estados Unidos, restringiría aún más el suministro en Europa, que sufre una escasez estructural de gasóleo y depende en gran medida de las exportaciones estadounidenses.

items.title: Ottawa opens up 15% Trans Mountain equity stake to Indigenous groups on pipeline path
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: The Canadian government is offering Indigenous groups a collective 15 per cent ownership stake in the Trans Mountain pipeline through a low-cost loan.
items.body: OTTAWA — The Canadian government has offered Indigenous groups a collective 15 per cent ownership stake in the Trans Mountain pipeline, advancing a long-promised plan to give First Nations equity in the federally owned infrastructure connecting Alberta crude to a Vancouver-area export terminal.  In a letter to a First Nation along the pipeline’s path seen by The Canadian Press on Tuesday, a Department of Finance official said the equity investment would be equally distributed among participating groups “through a low-cost government-provided loan.” The Trans Mountain equity offer follows consultations and discussions with 129 First Nations, said John Fragos, spokesperson for Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne. Ottawa is now gauging interest among the Indigenous nations before determining the finer details, including the size of individual stakes and the terms for buying in, he said. “The government’s position on economic reconciliation is long-standing and clear: Indigenous communities must be able to participate in and directly benefit from the projects shaping Canada,” Fragos said in a statement. He added that each Indigenous nation that invests in Trans Mountain is set to receive $2.5 million, intended to compensate for revenue they might have earned had Indigenous ownership been put in place years earlier. “We’re making up for lost time,” he said in a followup call.  Meanwhile, the letter said Ottawa will provide eligible groups with up to $100,000 for participation costs, while separately covering independent advisers to assist with due diligence. Details of the offer will be shared during a series of in-person meetings in Vancouver, Victoria, Kamloops and Edmonton planned for late October, the letter added.  Ottawa bought the existing Trans Mountain pipeline, its expansion project and related assets for $4.5 billion in 2018 after Kinder Morgan investors raised concerns that regulatory uncertainty made the investment too risky. It later committed to exploring Indigenous economic participation in the expansion with the 129 Indigenous communities potentially affected by the project. The expansion began operations in 2024 and increased the Trans Mountain system’s capacity to about 890,000 barrels per day from roughly 300,000 barrels per day.  Finance documents released that year said Ottawa planned to provide Indigenous groups with access to capital to acquire a stake in Trans Mountain. The documents said the Indigenous stake could be held collectively through a special-purpose vehicle, giving participating groups governance rights and a share of cash generated by the pipeline. Until now, however, the government had not publicly specified the size of the ownership stake it was prepared to make available. --- Brett Bundale, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 22, 2026.

items.title: Anthropic, OpenEvidence partner to bring medical AI worldwide
items.author: Nancy Lapid
items.creator: Nancy Lapid
items.summary: Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic and medical knowledge platform OpenEvidence are collaborating to bring AI-powered clinical decision support to physicians in regions without access to the technology, the companies said on Tuesday.
items.body:
Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic and medical knowledge platform OpenEvidence are collaborating to bring AI-powered clinical decision support to physicians in regions without access to the technology, the companies said on Tuesday.
OpenEvidence answers doctors' questions by drawing on peer-reviewed medical research and treatment guidelines. The platform is free to clinicians in the United States and Europe.
The new initiative is a specialized version available to healthcare providers for free in dozens of low- and middle-income countries where limited access to medical literature, specialist expertise and continuing medical education can impair patient care.
Healthcare systems worldwide are exploring whether generative AI can help address shortages of physicians and specialists. Supporters argue that AI tools can help clinicians quickly navigate vast amounts of medical information, while critics caution that systems trained primarily on data from high-income countries may not reflect local practice conditions.
The initiative is being rolled out in about 100 countries, including Uganda, Angola, Sudan, Haiti, and Mongolia, according to a list provided by OpenEvidence.
"Access to medical knowledge shouldn't depend on geography," OpenEvidence founder Daniel Nadler said.
[USN:L6N45814Q TEXT:"Reuters reported"] last week that Anthropic had built a lab to do physical biology work as it pushes its artificial intelligence ambitions into drug science and as fears of AI's reach grip the public, with some executives and lawmakers calling for a slowdown in development.
Anthropic and OpenEvidence did not disclose financial terms of the collaboration.
REGIONAL DIFFERENCES In August alone, US clinicians consulted OpenEvidence 42 million times, according to Nadler. In 2026, several hundred million Americans will have been treated by a doctor who used OpenEvidence to help guide care, he said.
Anthropic's technology will provide back-end support, while OpenEvidence will tailor the system to different regions, taking healthcare infrastructure into account, the companies said.
“The technology itself has advanced so dramatically that the sort of structure needed for (bringing OpenEvidence to low-resource regions) is there, but the market incentives alone would not let it happen without this type of entrepreneurial, philanthropically minded work,” Anthropic president Daniela Amodei said.
Earlier this year, OpenEvidence said it was working with health organizations in Rwanda and Botswana to adapt its tools for settings where disease patterns, diagnostic resources and available treatments differ markedly from those in wealthier countries.
“One hundred percent of what we are building for these places is context adaptive,” Nadler said.
Even where medical facilities don’t have around-the-clock electricity, most physicians do have smartphones, he said, which means access to quality medical information that a decade ago would only be available at leading institutions like the Mayo Clinic.
Dr. Ahmed Bendary, a cardiologist at Benha University in Egypt, said expanding this access outside the United States and Europe "would be a tremendous leap forward, particularly in regions where institutional subscriptions to major medical journals are limited, making evidence-based, point-of-care tools even more vital."

“One hundred percent of what we are building for these places is context adaptive,” Nadler said. 
Even where medical facilities don’t have around-the-clock electricity, most physicians do have smartphones, he said, which means access to quality medical information that a decade ago would only be available at leading institutions like the Mayo Clinic.

items.title: Belgium, Rwanda resume diplomatic relations after DRC conflict dispute
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Belgium and Rwanda have resumed diplomatic relations 18 months after breaking ties due to a dispute over the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
items.body:
Belgium and Rwanda have resumed diplomatic relations 18 months after breaking ties due to a dispute over the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot and Rwanda's foreign ministry both posted the news on X alongside photos of Prevot and his Rwandan counterpart Olivier Nduhungirehe in New York, where the United Nations General Assembly is taking place.
The two countries expelled each other's diplomats in March 2025 as relations deteriorated over the conflict in Rwanda's neighbour.
The AFC/M23 rebels control large parts of North and South Kivu provinces following their early 2025 advance, during which they captured Goma and Bukavu, eastern Congo's two largest cities. The UN and Western governments say the group is backed by Rwanda, which Kigali denies.
Rwanda says it is defending itself against the threat from a Hutu militia, which it says is fighting with the Congolese military. Both DR Congo and Rwanda are former Belgian colonies.
In a joint statement on Tuesday, Belgium and Rwanda said the two foreign ministers held a series of meetings and informal contacts over recent months, addressing a number of differences and misunderstandings "in a constructive spirit".
They also thanked Qatar for facilitating a first meeting in June 2025 and said they planned to reopen their respective embassies soon.
Prevot wrote on X that this was an important step "in a world marked by growing tensions".
"Restoring diplomatic relations between states does not mean abandoning our position, but having structured channels for dialogue, and I will continue to defend the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the DRC," he said.

items.title: Smaller packs, more protein: AB InBev to adapt drinks to shifting tastes
items.author: Emma Rumney
items.creator: Emma Rumney
items.summary: Anheuser-Busch InBev will sell smaller pack sizes, beers with added protein or electrolytes and push further into drinks beyond beer, executives said on Tuesday, as the top brewer looks to grow amid shifting drinking habits, strained incomes and a trend towards health and wellness.
items.body:
Anheuser-Busch InBev (ABI.BR) will sell smaller pack sizes, beers with added protein or electrolytes and push further into drinks beyond beer, executives said on Tuesday, as the top brewer looks to grow amid shifting drinking habits, strained incomes and a trend towards health and wellness.
The world's largest brewer by market value will look to drive higher beer consumption and grow revenue from non-beer products like canned cocktails and energy drinks, executives told investors at a capital markets event.
Brewers including AB InBev, which makes labels like Corona and Stella Artois, have been battling to grow beer volumes and revive weak demand in some large markets like the United States as some consumers cut back, prompted by pressure on their wallets or changing tastes.
AB InBev Chief Marketing Officer Marcel Marcondes said one aim was to grow consumption among infrequent beer drinkers, with budget-conscious consumers in this category presenting the most significant opportunity.
"Data is showing us huge opportunities to make beer more affordable, especially in developing markets," he said, adding AB InBev will address this by increasing both smaller pack sizes and larger ones offering higher quantities for less.
Increasing non-alcoholic beer consumption during casual meals presented another major opportunity, he said, adding AB InBev would drive that via zero-alcohol beers with different flavours, low calories and even protein or electrolytes. The company has launched a version of its Spaten beer with added protein in Brazil.
In the US especially, AB InBev has also been pushing into categories other than beer, including with top-selling canned cocktail label Cutwater and some energy drinks. Executives said it would expand further in these areas, with energy drinks alone potentially adding $25 billion to AB InBev's addressable market.
"In this space, we are the challengers, which gives us huge headroom for growth," CEO Michel Doukeris said.

items.title: 米追加利上げ観測、企業の物価期待抑制が鍵に＝リッチモンド連銀総裁
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Howard Schneider

[ボルチモア　２２日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Howard Schneider

[ボルチモア　２２日　ロイター] - 米リッチモンド地区連銀のバーキン総裁は２２日、米国の経済状況は「堅調さを増している」との認識を示した。個人消費が継続しているほか、人工知能（ＡＩ）投資ブーム以外でも力強さが見られるため、連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）はインフレに焦点を当て続けていると述べた。

バーキン氏は、アナリストの業界団体であるＣＦＡ協会のボルティモア支部で行う講演原稿で「インフレのリスクは最大雇用のリスクを上回っている。それが先週の会合で利上げを実施した理由だ」と説明。２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の利上げは、インフレ率をＦＲＢの目標である２％に戻すのに「役立つ」と述べた。 

その上で「追加利上げが必要になるか、また何回必要になるかについては今後見極めていく」と語った。

バーキン氏の発言は、インフレに対する懸念を広げてきた他のＦＲＢ当局者らの見解に続くものだ。当局者らは、インフレが単にエネルギーや関税措置など、自然に解消されると予想される供給問題だけでなく、経済における強い需要によってますます押し上げられていると感じている。 

また、企業が来年度予算や価格戦略を検討する際には、来年のインフレ見通しが重要な判断材料になると指摘。ＦＲＢによる利上げや追加利上げ観測が企業のインフレ期待を抑制し、物価上昇圧力を和らげる可能性があるとの見方を示した。

経済についても「過熱を主張するつもりはまだないが、経済は堅調さを増しており、弱まってはいない」と指摘。不確実性の時代を経て、企業や機関は投資・支出の判断をためらわなくなっているとの見方を示した。多くの企業は依然として価格決定力を持っていると感じているとも述べた。

総裁は、こうした「一時的な」ショックでさえ「短期間の単発的な出来事にとどまらず」、当初想定されていたよりも根強い物価上昇圧力を生み出していると指摘。

「中東紛争や関税措置の影響を特に強く受けているごく一部の品目が原因で高インフレが起きていると考えたくなる」が、個人消費支出（ＰＣＥ）物価指数の多くの項目は年率３％を超えるペースで上昇していると述べた。

その上で「データセンター以外の分野でも勢いを感じている。防衛部門は活況を呈しており、製造業の関係者からはより楽観的な声が聞かれるようになってきた。銀行関係者からは、新規案件のパイプラインが堅調だと聞いている」と述べた。

労働市場については、「過熱しておらず、特に逼迫しているわけでもない」と指摘。消費者のバランスシートが過度に膨らんでいる証拠はあまり見られず、雇用市場が健全である限り消費者は支出を続けるとの認識を示した。

さらに足元の生産性向上については、その大部分がＡＩを反映しているとは考えていないと述べた。現在の局面については、１９９０年代の景気サイクル半ばの調整に似たものになると考えたいと語った。

金融環境については、ＦＲＢが細心の注意を払っているとしつつ、市場金利がインフレ抑制に必要な水準にとどまると想定することはできないと指摘。「きょうのイールドカーブが、あすのイールドカーブと同じになると当てにすることはできない」と述べた。

バーキン氏は今年の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で投票権を持たない。

items.title: ＮＹ市場サマリー（22日）ナスダック連日最高値、ドル続伸　利回り低下
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ＜為替＞　ドルが続伸して取引を終えた。原油価格の乱高下でインフレ見通しが不透明になる中、序盤に２カ月ぶりの高値を付けた後、不安定な値動きが続いた。    原油価格は序盤、２週間ぶりの安値まで下落していた。イランが、米国が軍事的圧力を緩和し、イランの港湾封鎖を解除すれば、７日以内にホルムズ海峡を再開できると述べたことや、イランと米国が紛争終結に向けた交渉再開の可能性を示唆したことが手掛かりとなった。    しかし、トランプ氏が国連総会での演説で、１１月の中間選挙後にイランとの合意に達すると考えていると述べたことで、原油とドルが上昇。序盤の楽観的なムードは後退した。    ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、市場では米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）による１０月会合での利上げを巡って見方がほぼ二分しており、少なくとも２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の利上げ確率は５５．４％と、前日の５７．６％から低下している。
items.body:
＜為替＞　ドルが続伸して取引を終えた。原油価格の乱高下でインフレ見通しが不透明になる中、序盤に２カ月ぶりの高値を付けた後、不安定な値動きが続いた。    原油価格は序盤、２週間ぶりの安値まで下落していた。イランが、米国が軍事的圧力を緩和し、イランの港湾封鎖を解除すれば、７日以内にホルムズ海峡を再開できると述べたことや、イランと米国が紛争終結に向けた交渉再開の可能性を示唆したことが手掛かりとなった。    しかし、トランプ氏が国連総会での演説で、１１月の中間選挙後にイランとの合意に達すると考えていると述べたことで、原油とドルが上昇。序盤の楽観的なムードは後退した。    ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、市場では米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）による１０月会合での利上げを巡って見方がほぼ二分しており、少なくとも２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の利上げ確率は５５．４％と、前日の５７．６％から低下している。    主要通貨に対するドル指数は０．１７％高の１００．５９。同指数は一時、７月３０日以来の高値となる０．２９％高の１００．７０を付けたものの、０．１１％下落する場面もあった。    ドルは対円では０．０３％高の１５７．４１円と、３営業日続伸となる勢い。日銀が１８日の金融政策決定会合で利上げを決定したにもかかわらず、円は圧力にさらされている。より慎重なペースを主張した政策委員２人の反対票について、市場は追加利上げの実施が難しくなる可能性を示唆していると受け止めている。    ユーロは０．１８％安の１．１４４１ドル。    英ポンドは０．２３％安の１．３３３２ドルと、２営業日続落の見通しとなった。過去７営業日で６回目の下落となる。 

ＮＹ外為市場：[USD/J]

＜債券＞　国債利回りが低下した。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が追加利上げを実施するか見極めようとする動きが続く中、この日はインフレ懸念の緩和につながる原油価格の下落に反応し、１０年債や２年債などの利回りが低下した。

終盤の取引で１０年債利回りは２．２ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の４．９４１％。先週は５．０４１％と、２００７年以来の高水準を付けていた。

トランプ米大統領はこの日に国連総会で行った一般討論演説で、１１月上旬の中間選挙後に米国がイランと合意に達するとの見方を表明。その後、記者団に対し、米政府当局者がこの日にイラン代表団と約３時間にわたり「極めて良好な」協議を行ったと明らかにした。

これに関連してイラン国営メディアは、イランのアラグチ外相がこの日にニューヨークで米国のウィットコフ和平交渉担当特使と会談し、戦略的要衝であるホルムズ海峡の通航再開に向けたイランの条件を米国に伝えたと報道。 米国時間の原油先物は下落し、北海ブレント先物は約１％安の１バレル＝９９．２５ドルで取引を終えた。

原油価格は対イラン軍事攻撃を受け急騰しており、インフレ加速と金利上昇に対する懸念が強まる要因になっていた。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は１５─１６日に開いた連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で、インフレ抑制を目的に２０２３年７月以来初めて利上げを決定。ＦＯＭＣに合わせて公表された金利・経済見通しでは、年内に少なくともあと１回の利上げが実施される可能性が示唆された。

ＣＭＥフェドウオッチによると、１０月２７─２８日の次回ＦＯＭＣで追加利上げが決定される確率は約５５％。

終盤の取引で、ＦＲＢの金融政策見通しに敏感な２年債利回りは２．５ｂｐ低下の４．７２８％。一時は４．７８７９％と、約２年ぶりの高水準を付けていた。

２年債と１０年債の利回り格差は２１．１ｂｐ。

３０年債利回りは１．５ｂｐ低下の５．２８１％。 

米金融・債券市場：[US/BJ]

ＮＹ市場サマリー（22日）ナスダック連日最高値、ドル続伸　利回り低下
6:13 配信

＜為替＞　ドルが続伸して取引を終えた。原油価格の乱高下でインフレ見通しが不透明になる中、序盤に２カ月ぶりの高値を付けた後、不安定な値動きが続いた。    原油価格は序盤、２週間ぶりの安値まで下落していた。イランが、米国が軍事的圧力を緩和し、イランの港湾封鎖を解除すれば、７日以内にホルムズ海峡を再開できると述べたことや、イランと米国が紛争終結に向けた交渉再開の可能性を示唆したことが手掛かりとなった。    しかし、トランプ氏が国連総会での演説で、１１月の中間選挙後にイランとの合意に達すると考えていると述べたことで、原油とドルが上昇。序盤の楽観的なムードは後退した。    ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、市場では米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）による１０月会合での利上げを巡って見方がほぼ二分しており、少なくとも２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の利上げ確率は５５．４％と、前日の５７．６％から低下している。    主要通貨に対するドル指数は０．１７％高の１００．５９。同指数は一時、７月３０日以来の高値となる０．２９％高の１００．７０を付けたものの、０．１１％下落する場面もあった。    ドルは対円では０．０３％高の１５７．４１円と、３営業日続伸となる勢い。日銀が１８日の金融政策決定会合で利上げを決定したにもかかわらず、円は圧力にさらされている。より慎重なペースを主張した政策委員２人の反対票について、市場は追加利上げの実施が難しくなる可能性を示唆していると受け止めている。    ユーロは０．１８％安の１．１４４１ドル。    英ポンドは０．２３％安の１．３３３２ドルと、２営業日続落の見通しとなった。過去７営業日で６回目の下落となる。 

ＮＹ外為市場：[USD/J]

＜債券＞　国債利回りが低下した。米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が追加利上げを実施するか見極めようとする動きが続く中、この日はインフレ懸念の緩和につながる原油価格の下落に反応し、１０年債や２年債などの利回りが低下した。

終盤の取引で１０年債利回りは２．２ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の４．９４１％。先週は５．０４１％と、２００７年以来の高水準を付けていた。

トランプ米大統領はこの日に国連総会で行った一般討論演説で、１１月上旬の中間選挙後に米国がイランと合意に達するとの見方を表明。その後、記者団に対し、米政府当局者がこの日にイラン代表団と約３時間にわたり「極めて良好な」協議を行ったと明らかにした。

これに関連してイラン国営メディアは、イランのアラグチ外相がこの日にニューヨークで米国のウィットコフ和平交渉担当特使と会談し、戦略的要衝であるホルムズ海峡の通航再開に向けたイランの条件を米国に伝えたと報道。 米国時間の原油先物は下落し、北海ブレント先物は約１％安の１バレル＝９９．２５ドルで取引を終えた。

原油価格は対イラン軍事攻撃を受け急騰しており、インフレ加速と金利上昇に対する懸念が強まる要因になっていた。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は１５─１６日に開いた連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で、インフレ抑制を目的に２０２３年７月以来初めて利上げを決定。ＦＯＭＣに合わせて公表された金利・経済見通しでは、年内に少なくともあと１回の利上げが実施される可能性が示唆された。

ＣＭＥフェドウオッチによると、１０月２７─２８日の次回ＦＯＭＣで追加利上げが決定される確率は約５５％。

終盤の取引で、ＦＲＢの金融政策見通しに敏感な２年債利回りは２．５ｂｐ低下の４．７２８％。一時は４．７８７９％と、約２年ぶりの高水準を付けていた。

２年債と１０年債の利回り格差は２１．１ｂｐ。

items.title: Oil price becoming increasingly important for ECB, Bundesbank chief says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Oil prices are an increasingly important indicator for ECB policymakers in setting interest rates but other factors also play a crucial role, Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said on Tuesday after markets raised rate-hike bets on expensive energy.
items.body:
Oil prices are an increasingly important indicator for ECB policymakers in setting interest rates but other factors also play a crucial role, Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said on Tuesday after markets raised rate-hike bets on expensive energy.
The ECB has already lifted its key rate twice this summer but investors see another three or four moves in the next year as both oil and gas prices are now at its "severe" scenario and inflation could peak at around 4%, twice the bank's target.
ECB President [USN:L1N45A0DM TEXT:"Christine Lagarde"] and Vice President [USN:L8N4591NP TEXT:"Boris Vujcic"] have both pushed back on those bets, arguing that rates do not move in lockstep with oil prices. Their remarks suggested the bank may wait until December to pull the trigger next.
"It's definitely not the only indicator but it's become a more relevant indicator over the last four years, this is for sure," Nagel told an event hosted by London's Society of Professional Economists.
"It is obvious that we in governing council have to look at it and we have to take it into account when we take our decisions," he said about oil prices.
Still, he kept open the door to more rate hikes. He said rates, now at 2.5%, are in a territory that neither restrict economic growth nor stimulate it.
"I cannot exclude that if we are confronted with higher energy prices like this, that we have to go into the mild restrictive territory of monetary policy," he said.
But he played down some worries about second-round inflation effects, arguing that the labour market was far softer than in 2022, when an energy-price-led inflation fuelled increasing wage demands, leading to a wage-price spiral.
He also said there were no significant second-round effects in the data.
For now, the ECB needed to maintain its approach of making decisions meeting by meeting, Nagel said.
This means that policy needs to be somewhere between "constructive ambiguity," or intentional policy vagueness, and setting "forward guidance" or making explicit commitments about future policy moves, Nagel said.

[ロンドン　２２日　ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）理事会メンバーのナーゲル独連銀総裁は２２日、エネルギー価格の高騰でインフレ率が目標を上回って推移していることを受け、ＥＣＢが金融政策を巡る判断を行うに当たり原油価格が一段と重要な指標になっているとの認識を示した。

ナーゲル氏はロンドンで開かれたイベントで、「（政策判断のための）唯一の指標では決してないものの、原油価格の重要性は過去４年間で確実に高まっている」と指摘。「ＥＣＢ理事会が原油価格に注視し、政策決定を行う際に考慮しなければならないのは明らかだ」と語った。

労働市場の動向については、それほど懸念していないと述べた。

items.title: Jets sign QB Will Levis to practice squad
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The New York Jets signed former Tennessee Titans starting quarterback Will Levis to the practice squad on Tuesday.
items.body:
The New York Jets signed former Tennessee Titans starting quarterback Will Levis to the practice squad on Tuesday.
In the corresponding move, the Jets released quarterback Bailey Zappe from the practice squad. Starter Geno Smith and rookie Cade Klubnik are the quarterbacks on New York's active roster.
The Titans released Levis, 27, at the end of the preseason on Aug. 30 and he went unclaimed on waivers.
Levis started 21 games for the Titans after being drafted No. 33 in 2023, completing 61% of his passes for 3,899 yards, 21 touchdowns and 16 interceptions. He had a 5-16 record as a starter and spent last season recovering from right shoulder surgery after being unseated as the starter by 2025 No. 1 overall pick Cam Ward.
Tennessee, which moved up eight spots to draft Levis with the first pick in the second round, signed Mitchell Trubisky to a two-year contract in March and gave the veteran most of the work behind Ward during training camp.
Zappe, 27, has played in 15 games (nine starts) and completed 62.1% of his passes for 2,223 yards, 12 TDs and 14 interceptions.
The New England Patriots selected Zappe in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL Draft.
In other moves, the Jets signed linebacker Troy Reeder to the 53-man active roster and signed linebacker Jaden Keller to the practice squad.
Reeder, 32, was elevated from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers and played 25 snaps on special teams. He has played in 107 regular-season games (38 starts) for the Los Angeles Rams (2019-21, 2023-25), Los Angeles Chargers (2022) and Jets.
Keller, 23, an undrafted rookie out of Virginia Tech who signed with New York in May, was released from the practice squad on Sept. 15.
--Field Level Media

items.title: 米国株式市場＝ナスダック連日最高値、ＡＩ関連株高で 　米中首脳会談に注目
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ニューヨーク　２２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ニューヨーク　２２日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場では、ナスダック総合が連日で終値での最高値を更新した。半導体大手マイクロン・テクノロジーや人工知能（ＡＩ）関連銘柄に買いが入り、ナスダック指数を押し上げた。また、原油価格が１バレル＝１００ドル近辺で推移する中、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種８月１３日に付けた過去最高値に迫った。

マイクロンは５％高、サンディスクは約７％高となった。

メタ・プラットフォームズが投入したＡＩアシスタント「ミューズ」の成功が、このところＡＩ関連半導体株への買いを後押ししている。

一方、ミューズが小売業者やオンライン証券会社など消費者向け企業と競合するとの懸念から、消費者向けソフトウエア株などに売りが広がった。

配車アプリ大手ウーバー・テクノロジーズとリフトはともに１％超下落。チャールズ・シュワブは６．１％安、民泊仲介大手エアビーアンドビーは３％安となった

原油先物は下落。トランプ米大統領が２２日の国連総会一般討論演説で、イランとの戦闘終結に向けた合意に至らなければ同国を「壊滅させる」可能性があると警告したことが材料視された。

市場では、２４日に予定されている米中首脳会談に注目が集まっている。

テミス・トレーディングの株式市場構造調査責任者、ジョー・サルッツィ氏は「対立を続けるのではなく、何らかの国際的な枠組みを構築できる可能性について、少なくとも対話を始めることが求められている」と述べた。

Ｓ＆Ｐ主要１１セクターのうち６セクターが下落。ＪＰモルガン・チェースとウェルズ・ファーゴがともに３％超下落する中、金融は１．６８％安となった。通信サービスも０．８％下落した。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００種指数では、値上がり銘柄数と値下がり銘柄数はほぼ拮抗した。

米取引所の合算出来高は１７９億株と、直近２０営業日の平均である１６３億株を上回った。

Sailing-Black Foils focus on future after tough SailGP season

Tokyo 2020 Olympics - Sailing - Men's 49er - Medal Race - Enoshima Yacht Harbour - Tokyo, Japan - August 3, 2021. Peter Burling of New Zealand and Blair Tuke of New Zealand in action. REUTERS/Carlos Barria

FAST

LONDON, Sept 22 : Black Foils co-CEO Blair Tuke said the New Zealand team are building for the future, including protecting the oceans fundamental to their sport, as they near the end of what he said had been a "really tough" SailGP season.
A high-speed crash with France in front of New Zealand's home crowd in February resulted in the team's sailors being shore bound for months and missing four events while SailGP built a replacement for their F50 catamaran, which was beyond repair.  
"It's been a really tough one is probably the only way to put it. We had four months when we didn't sail or race as a team," Tuke told Reuters in a recent interview.
"It's a mix now. We're obviously trying to build for next season and develop, but probably the best way to do that is to try and put your best foot forward and to race well and put yourselves under pressure," the 37-year-old wing trimmer added.

With no prospect of reaching November's grand final in Abu Dhabi, the team are also working on developing new talent.
"The season's out of reach," Tuke said, adding that Black Foils, who now lie 12th on the season leaderboard, were aiming to "win race weekends and build processes and experience that sets us up for the future".
Tuke is a fan of the new group racing format that splits SailGP's now 13-strong fleet in two, partly as a precaution aimed at avoiding clashes like the dramatic one in Auckland.
"It had to happen at some point as SailGP grew and I think following some of the incidents that happened earlier this year it maybe got fast-tracked a little quicker," he said.
'MUCH BIGGER THAN OURSELVES'
Tuke said New York-based MSP Sports Capital's acquisition of a majority stake in the Black Foils gives them a "really exciting opportunity", both on and off the water. 
"We're so focused on becoming a global sports brand that represents New Zealand on the world stage, that pushes what's possible on the performance side," said Tuke, adding that the team is also targeting "something much bigger than ourselves".
Having MSP's backing has 'supercharged' the team's ability to achieve all those things, said Tuke, partly with reference to the Live Ocean Foundation he founded with co-CEO and longtime sailing partner Pete Burling in late 2019.
"The ocean is declining fast and its health is key to our future on this planet," Tuke said of the campaigns which Live Ocean has launched in New Zealand to "bring people round to issues they otherwise wouldn't be made aware of". 
"We've got the platform in sport to do something," he said, adding that he and Burling had wanted to be able to integrate their campaigning into something that they did every day.
For Tuke, establishing the team's Live Ocean partnership was a "non-negotiable" in discussions with SailGP, which runs its own impact league among teams, from the outset.
"I am very committed to making sure we leave this place in a better state than when I came into it," he said. 

Source: Reuters

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Michael S. Derby

[ニューヨーク　２２日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Michael S. Derby

[ニューヨーク　２２日　ロイター] - 米ニューヨーク連銀で金融政策の執行を担うロベルト・ペルリ氏は２２日、連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の金融政策のツールキットは引き続き非常に効果的に機能しているとの認識を示した。

ニューヨーク連銀が主催した米国債市場に関する会合の閉会あいさつでペルリ氏は「われわれは非常に強固な金利コントロールを維持し、準備預金を潤沢な水準の範囲内に保ってきた。財務省短期証券（Ｔビル）買い入れも円滑に進んでいる」と語った。同氏は、ＦＲＢの資産ポートフォリオ「システム・オープン・マーケット・アカウント（ＳＯＭＡ）」を運営している。

同氏はまた、現在停止中の金融システムに流動性を供給するためのＦＲＢによる最近の措置について、あらかじめ決められた方針があるわけではないと説明。市場の流動性を下支えする必要があると判断すれば、ＦＲＢが再びＴビルを買い入れる可能性があることを示唆した。

「準備金管理購入（ＲＭＰ） 」と呼ばれるＴビル買い入れについては、市場の流動性ニーズに応じて調整されるとも言及。Ｔビル買い入れに関して、「買い入れ額をゼロに設定するという最近の決定は、ＲＭＰが昨年１２月に始まって以降、デスクが下してきた他の判断と本質的に異なるものではない」と述べた。  

さらに、ニューヨーク連銀の「準備預金の予測プロセスは頑健で、概して非常に正確だ」とし、「過去４年間の予測誤差は、準備預金供給全体のごくわずかにすぎず、当行の潤沢な準備預金の枠組みにより容易に吸収可能だ」と述べた。

items.title: Apollo private credit fund redemption requests ease in third quarter
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Asset manager Apollo Global Management recorded lower withdrawal requests at its flagship private credit fund in the third-quarter tender offer, suggesting redemption queues are beginning to clear.
items.body:
Asset manager Apollo Global Management (APO.N) recorded lower withdrawal requests at its flagship private credit fund in the third-quarter tender offer, suggesting redemption queues are beginning to clear.
Investors in Apollo Debt Solutions BDC (ADS) sought to withdraw roughly 14.7% of shares in the latest tender offer, compared with 16.8% in the prior quarter, according to a regulatory filing on Tuesday.
The $25.9 billion fund will repurchase 5% of shares, the customary threshold for such vehicles.
The Apollo fund said repurchase requests declined sequentially across both US onshore and offshore investors, and most of them were investors resubmitting unfulfilled requests from prior quarters.
Demand from wealth investors to pull money from private credit funds hit record levels this year on concerns about lending standards and AI disruption risks.
However, redemption pressure has recently begun to ease across major non-traded private credit funds as asset managers work through a backlog of unfulfilled withdrawal requests and sentiment improves after a turbulent period.
Earlier this month, BlackRock (BLK.N) also [USN:L4N4530XC TEXT:"revealed a decline in redemption requests"] at its private credit funds.
Most non-traded private credit funds have enforced the customary 5% limit on redemptions this year, keeping withdrawal requests elevated as investors resubmit their unfulfilled requests in following tender offers.
"Following third-quarter repurchase payments, investors who have sought liquidity during 2026 will have received an estimated 75% of their requested capital," the Apollo fund said.
During the quarter, ADS received $0.2 billion in gross subscriptions through September 1. Quarterly net outflows are expected to be roughly $0.5 billion, or 3% of net asset value.
Since inception, ADS' Class I shares have delivered a net total return of 8.2% as of August 31, outperforming leveraged loan and high-yield markets by 177 and 377 basis points, respectively.
Data from major vehicles run by Ares (ARES.N) and Blue Owl (OWL.N) are expected in coming weeks.

FAST

Sept 22 : The S&P 500 Financial index and the benchmark's bank sector were under pressure on Tuesday as investors worried about competition from artificial intelligence and uncertainty around AI-related initial public offerings, along with moves in the bond market that potentially point to softer conditions ahead. 
The benchmark's broader financial index finished down 2 per cent on Tuesday with money managers Charles Schwab, Ameriprise Financial and Raymond James among the biggest decliners. Schwab fell 6.1 per cent while Ameriprise shares fell 4.4 per cent and Raymond James shares lost more than 3 per cent. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 bank index finished down 3 per cent. 
With Muse, an AI agent from Meta Platforms, recently moving past ChatGPT as the most downloaded free app for iPhones, Macrae Sykes, portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds, said that investors have started to become concerned about potential competition from the app in the wealth management industry.
"There's worries about AI disruption to traditional businesses," said Sykes, who manages investments in the financial industry. "Clearly there's going to be some arguments both around the benefits and the disruption of AI tools and what it all means for the incumbents, but I think today is another sell-without-regard reaction."

Sykes also highlighted moves in the US bond market where the yield curve between short- and long-dated bonds has been flattening, which could eat into bank returns.   
A closely watched part of the Treasury yield curve measuring the gap between yields on two- and 10-year Treasury notes, seen as an indicator of the health of economic expectations, hit its flattest level since March 2025 earlier on Tuesday. It was last at a positive 21 basis points but was as low as 17.90 basis points earlier on Tuesday. As traders have increased their bets on Federal Reserve rate hikes, the curve, which was at 55.5 on August 18, has been flattening gradually.
"There's a tipping point between raising rates reflecting a strong economy and raising rates and having the effect of slowing the economy," said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments, a family investment office in New Vernon, New Jersey.
Gabelli's Sykes also pointed to concerns about the market for initial public offerings after a New York Times report on Monday about delays in initial public offerings for companies tied to the data centers supporting AI. 
SB Energy, a subsidiary of the Japanese conglomerate SoftBank, filed paperwork recently for a US IPO. But the data center developer, which had originally planned an IPO for this month, has postponed the launch of its roadshow to market the offering to investors, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters. SB Energy declined to comment.  
Nuclear services company Holtec last week suspended its planned US IPO.
Still,  Sykes argues that the outlook for bank stocks is strong. 
"The short-term noise does not affect our appreciation for the long-term outlook," he said. "The outlook in general for banks is pretty good. There's a good economy and good employment. The fundamentals are good."  

Source: Reuters

SB Energy, a subsidiary of the Japanese conglomerate SoftBank, filed paperwork recently for a US IPO. But the data center developer, which had originally planned an IPO for this month, has postponed the launch of its roadshow to market the offering to investors, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters. SB Energy declined to comment.  
Nuclear services company Holtec last week suspended its planned US IPO.
Still,  Sykes argues that the outlook for bank stocks is strong. 
"The short-term noise does not affect our appreciation for the long-term outlook," he said. "The outlook in general for banks is pretty good. There's a good economy and good employment. The fundamentals are good."  

Source: Reuters

items.title: WPP finance chief Joanne Wilson to become Diageo CFO, Sky News reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: WPP CFO Joanne Wilson is set to leave Britain's biggest advertising group to become finance chief of Guinness-maker Diageo , Sky News reported on Tuesday.
items.body:
WPP (WPP.L) CFO Joanne Wilson is set to leave Britain's biggest advertising group to become finance chief of Guinness-maker Diageo (DGE.L) , Sky News reported on Tuesday.
Diageo was finalising Wilson's appointment and could announce the move as early as Wednesday, the report said.
Diageo declined to comment, while WPP did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours.
The move comes as Diageo undergoes a broad overhaul under CEO Dave Lewis, who last month [USN:L4N4430TT TEXT:"unveiled"] a $1 billion cost-cutting plan, saying the world's largest spirits maker must adapt to a prolonged period of weak growth.
Lewis is reshaping the company's management and board, while implementing a restructuring programme that has already led to the departure of several senior executives and reductions in headcount.
Wilson would replace Nik Jhangiani, who is expected to leave the spirits maker, according to Sky News.
Jhangiani, who [USN:L4N3H651J TEXT:"joined"] Diageo as CFO in May 2024 and later became interim CEO, [USN:L1N3TE0FB TEXT:"won praise"] from investors for his communication style and leadership, with some shareholders backing him as a candidate for the chief executive role.
The move would also reunite Wilson with Lewis, a former colleague from her time at Tesco (TSCO.L) .
Meanwhile, Wilson's departure from WPP comes as the British advertising group navigates a leadership transition and seeks to improve its performance after a period of weaker growth relative to some industry peers.

items.title: Jefe BID busca 2.500 millones de dólares para Venezuela; consejeros se resisten: fuentes
items.author: Rodrigo Campos, Cassandra Garrison
items.creator: Rodrigo Campos, Cassandra Garrison
items.summary: El presidente del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) ha estado trabajando para obtener la aprobación de un préstamo de 2.500 millones de dólares para Venezuela, pero se ha enfrentado a la oposición de algunos miembros del consejo de administración de la entidad, dijeron a Reuters dos fuentes con conocimiento del asunto.
items.body:
El presidente del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) ha estado trabajando para obtener la aprobación de un préstamo de 2.500 millones de dólares para Venezuela, pero se ha enfrentado a la oposición de algunos miembros del consejo de administración de la entidad, dijeron a Reuters dos fuentes con conocimiento del asunto.
El presidente del BID, Ilan Goldfajn, ha enfrentado inquietudes de la junta sobre la posibilidad de otorgar un crédito a Caracas sin la habitual labor paralela de otros prestamistas multilaterales, a pesar de que la junta reconoce los beneficios de retomar la relación con Venezuela, señaló una de las fuentes.
El BID dejó de otorgar nuevos préstamos al país sudamericano en mayo de 2018 después de que este se retrasó en los pagos.
Estos esfuerzos ponen de manifiesto los desafíos que enfrenta Venezuela para resolver sus problemas de deuda. El país exportador de petróleo atraviesa una crisis de liquidez y macroeconómica que combina, entre otros factores, ingresos petroleros mucho menores y un déficit fiscal creciente.
Se prevé que la reestructuración de su deuda —que según algunas estimaciones podría superar los 200.000 millones de dólares— sea compleja y lenta.
Una operación del BID por 2.500 millones de dólares sería significativa como financiación para una etapa inicial de recuperación, pero representa una cifra insignificante frente al problema estructural del balance financiero de Venezuela. La concreción de dicho préstamo requeriría superar varios obstáculos.
Actualmente, el BID no puede otorgar préstamos a Venezuela debido a su política sobre atrasos en pagos públicos, dado que Caracas adeuda más de 2.000 millones de dólares en capital e intereses vencidos al organismo regional.
No obstante, dichos atrasos podrían saldarse mediante un préstamo puente de un tercero, un procedimiento habitual para reintegrar a un país en el sistema financiero internacional, indicó una de las fuentes.
El BID declinó hacer comentarios y el gobierno venezolano no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios.
El préstamo propuesto se enmarcaría en un mecanismo de Préstamo Especial para el Desarrollo (SDL, por sus siglas en inglés), el cual, en el caso de Venezuela, tendría un límite de 500 millones de dólares conforme a las normas del BID, dijeron las fuentes.
Un préstamo de 2.500 millones de dólares a Caracas requeriría una excepción respecto al monto máximo permitido, así como una segunda excepción por la ausencia de un programa vigente con el Fondo Monetario Internacional, requisito este último para los préstamos SDL, según la normativa del banco.
Goldfajn [USN:L6N45818S TEXT:"declaró"] a Reuters el lunes que el BID trabaja en una "nota de acercamiento" con Venezuela, un plan a corto plazo que suele preceder a la concesión de nuevos préstamos.
Cualquier propuesta de préstamo a Venezuela requeriría, en última instancia, la aprobación del Directorio Ejecutivo del BID —integrado por 14 miembros—, donde Estados Unidos ostenta el 30% del poder de voto, seguido por Argentina y Brasil, con un 11% y 35% cada uno.
El BID cuenta con 48 países miembros, incluidos 26 países prestatarios de América Latina y el Caribe, región donde constituye la principal fuente de financiación multilateral.
En 2025, aprobó nuevos préstamos y garantías por valor de 17.400 millones de dólares, mientras que su cartera de préstamos pendientes alcanzó casi 118.000 millones de dólares, según su informe anual más reciente.

WASHINGTON, Sept 22 : Boeing's drone subsidiary Insitu and aviation Wi-Fi provider Gogo have successfully tested a military drone using satellite communications, the companies said on Tuesday, underscoring growing efforts by governments and defense firms to reduce reliance on Elon Musk's Starlink.
Gogo Special Missions, the military and government arm of Gogo, and Insitu integrated a modified version of Gogo's Galileo HDX antenna onto Insitu's Integrator drone, a mid-sized uncrewed aircraft used by military customers for surveillance and reconnaissance missions.
Drone warfare has become central to military strategy following its widespread use in Russia's war in Ukraine and conflicts across the Middle East. As militaries seek to operate drones at longer ranges, withstand jamming attacks and carry out increasingly complex missions, they are turning to satellite networks such as Starlink rather than relying on line-of-sight radio links.
Gogo and Insitu said their system would provide the Integrator drone with high-speed global internet through Eutelsat OneWeb's low-Earth-orbit satellite network and would not be subject to US International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), easing exports to international customers.

"Adding an ITAR-free, high-speed SATCOM option is an essential capability for our global customers," John Kelly, Insitu's vice president of growth, said in a statement, adding that the technology would extend command-and-control range and allow faster transmission of sensor data from the battlefield.
Gogo and Insitu did not disclose a timeline for deploying the system.
Providing military users with Starlink and Starshield, SpaceX's secure government-focused satellite communications service, has become an important source of revenue for Musk's company. But European governments and some in the Pentagon have voiced concerns about an over-reliance on Starlink, whose constellation of thousands of satellites dwarfs those of its rivals.

Raphael Satter　AJ Vicens
