Since returning to office last year for a second term, Trump has sent waves through the global order, joining Israel to attack Iran, ordering a raid on Venezuela that captured the country's leader, and threatening to seize Greenland.
In a 37-minute speech ahead of a whirlwind diplomatic schedule that included meetings with the leaders of Britain, Ukraine and Japan, Trump laid out his foreign policy vision, arguing that the Iran war had spared the world the threat of a nuclear-armed menace while asserting US dominance in the Western Hemisphere is essential to preventing crises from taking root.
"Our actions in Venezuela are proof that the United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere," Trump said. "While others have spoken of peace, I have made peace."

Related:

Binance faces US scrutiny over possible Iran sanctions violations, source says

Iran, US hint at revival of talks as Trump, Pezeshkian due to attend UN

Outside the UN headquarters, dozens of anti-Iranian-government demonstrators gathered, a few of them holding up signs calling for democracy and decrying dictatorship.
Trump brushed aside suggestions that the midterm elections, in which his Republican Party risks losing control of Congress, could constrain his handling of the war. Some analysts have argued that a Democratic takeover of the legislature would weaken his leverage in the conflict.
"What they don't realize is that I'm not running," Trump said, referring to the leadership in Tehran. “I did that already, and won in a landslide. We won in a giant landslide, and I'll be here for 2-1/2 years.”
DIPLOMATIC WHIRLWIND Taking aim at US neighbours, Trump labelled Mexico "the epicentre of cartel violence," urged its government to "reclaim control of its soil," and said his administration was pursuing "a fundamental change in the situation in Cuba."
Members of the Cuban delegation walked out of the hall as Trump referenced his pressure campaign against the country.
"It's an absolutely failed state, it's failing like never before, and it will fall," said Trump .
Yet Trump 's appearance was less dramatic than in 2025, when he used a combative speech to chastise world leaders, warning that some countries were "going to hell," and complained about UN facilities after being briefly stranded on a malfunctioning escalator and suffering an initial teleprompter failure.
Trump renewed his criticism of the UN, highlighting his efforts to cut its bureaucracy, but offered no fresh attacks or indications that the US would leave any additional UN agencies.

Related:

Trump returns to UN at a moment of anxiety about Iran, AI and the future of world body itself

Commentary: Trump declares victory in Greenland, but the deal exposes a deeper crisis of trust

Trump spoke less than a week after a UN fact-finding mission said it had reasonable grounds to believe US forces committed war crimes in two strikes on Iran, including one that hit a primary school in the southern city of Minab.
He renewed his criticism of international bodies that could serve as a check on US power, singling out the International Criminal Court and declaring that US military personnel would not be subject to its authority.
"We will never allow US service members or anyone else to be investigated or given show trials by an anti-American tribunal with no jurisdiction over us," he said.
Ahead of a UN Security Council meeting on AI and international security on Wednesday, Trump acknowledged the challenges of the new technology but said, "I'm not going to stifle growth of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution."
The speech kicked off a day of high-level diplomacy at the United Nations, where Trump was due to meet more than a dozen world leaders as wars in the Middle East and Ukraine continued to test his foreign policy agenda.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he had "established a good connection" with Trump in their first-ever meeting, where they discussed trade, Ukraine and the status of the Falkland Islands.
At the press-facing start of their talks, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the meeting would demonstrate the strength of the US-Japan alliance amid a "severe security environment, including in Asia," an apparent nod to China. Trump is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington later this week.
On his meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Trump told reporters that the two talked about finding a solution to end Russia's war in Ukraine.

Source: Reuters/fs

items.title: Trump hails Burnham as 'natural business person' after first meeting
items.author: Elizabeth Piper
items.creator: Elizabeth Piper
items.summary: US President Donald Trump hailed Andy Burnham on Tuesday as a "natural business person" at what the new British leader's team described as a smooth first face-to-face meeting.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump hailed Andy Burnham on Tuesday as a "natural business person" at what the new British leader's team described as a smooth first face-to-face meeting.
After days of preparation for the Trump meeting, Burnham emerged relatively unscathed, with the US leader only taking issue with what he called a "terrible deal" to cede sovereignty of the [USN:L6N45D0ZR TEXT:"Chagos Islands,"] home to a US-British air base.
Otherwise, Trump praised Burnham, saying Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade was someone with whom he could do business and a patriot who had put Britain on the up after replacing the former prime minister, Keir Starmer, in July.
"I think right now, based on my relationship with the prime minister, Andy, I think that ... we're doing very well," Trump said after they met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York for around 40 minutes.
"I think he's a natural business person. We've had a lot of discussions, even before this meeting we were talking with each other numerous times on the phone."
'ENCOURAGING MEETING' Burnham, who travelled to New York on Monday to take part in the UN assembly, had said little beforehand about his expectations for the meeting with Trump, saying only that in their two phone calls he had found "a connection" with the US president.
Afterwards, he repeated that earlier conversations had established that connection "and that very much came through today".
"(I) can certainly work with him. It was a very encouraging meeting," Burnham told reporters, saying the two leaders had found "common ground" on dealing with cost-of-living pressures, ending the conflict in the Middle East and reindustrialising nations to spur economic growth, among other issues.
"He was very upbeat about the country's (Britain's) prospects, which, to be honest, was great to hear."
Before arriving in New York, Burnham had sought common ground with Trump on AI, a focus of his comments to the UN on Monday in which he described the technology as having the ability to bring "huge benefits" to the British and global economy.
Trump has said he wants to cherish AI rather than stifle its growth, dismissing fears about it as a hoax and "sick conspiracy". The US leader has said concerns can be addressed through the existing [USN:L6N45E0RD TEXT:"justice system"] without extra regulation — an issue that might cause some friction with Britain.
Yet, while the two leaders seemed to find common ground on a number of issues, there were some pitfalls.
Trump again criticised Britain's move, under Starmer, to cede sovereignty of the Chagos Islands while retaining control of Diego Garcia air base on a 99-year lease.
Trump called the agreement with Mauritius, now on hold, a "terrible" deal. "It's amazing how strategic it is, and I think the prime minister is going to be looking at it," he said.
Burnham later told reporters he had inherited the problem and would work to find a resolution between the different sides. "It was clear that we need to come to that agreement, but I'm confident we can find it working with our US partners," he said.
Burnham also showed a willingness to disagree with Trump if it is in his nation's interest, saying he would "stand firm in the face of any threats" to the right of Falkland Islanders to self-determination and to remain British.
In August, Trump said he was reviewing the United States' neutral position on the remote archipelago in the South Atlantic. Days later Argentine President Javier Milei — who will address the UN on Wednesday — said he would impose sanctions on oil companies drilling in the islands.
And the British leader navigated some other bilateral sticking points. Trump appeared unmoved over Britain's decision to block imports from [USN:L8N45007X TEXT:"Israeli settlements"] in the occupied West Bank, while its decision not to back the US over the Iran war was also skated over.
OPENS WAY FOR BURNHAM TO FOCUS ON AI With the meeting done, Burnham turns his focus for UNGA to AI and his support for the technology, which he hopes will help Britain assume a leading role globally.
At an earlier business roundtable, Burnham said he would make the case for Britain in a speech later on Tuesday to help establish "a single set of global principles and standards" to unlock the potential of AI.
Describing Britain as being stuck in 10 years of political turbulence since voting to leave the European Union in 2016, Burnham told business leaders he wanted to usher in a period of stability and embrace AI, while being clear-eyed on the risks.
"So outside Downing Street, on my first day, I said I want to be the circuit breaker," he told the roundtable, including Tim Cook, executive chairman of Apple, and Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser.
"(To) bring forward a very clear path that everyone can understand, a 10-year plan for Britain ... so that nobody's in any doubt at all about what we're trying to do."

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [２２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[２２日 ロイター] - 米軍は２２日、ドイツ西部のシュパングダーレム米空軍基地所属のＦ１６戦闘機１機が墜落したと発表した。操縦士１人は無事脱出し、治療を受けている。

米軍は声明で、事故原因については調査中で、緊急対応要員が墜落現場に派遣されていると明らかにした。

ドイツの航空管制当局は別の声明で、Ｆ１６戦闘機計４機が訓練演習に参加していたと説明。「うち２機は依然として訓練空域におり、他の２機はシュパングダーレム空軍基地に帰投中だった。この２機のうち１機が着陸進入中に墜落したとみられる」と述べた。残るＦ１６戦闘機はラムシュタイン米空軍基地に着陸したという。

items.title: トランプ一族の金融取引にメスを、共和党上院議員が議会に調査要求
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中間選挙を数週間後に控えた米国で、与党共和党の上院議員がトランプ一家の金融取引を調査するよう求めている。ドナルド・トランプ・ジュニア氏の証言要求を含め、トランプ大統領と明確に一線を画した。

ユタ州選出のカーティス上院議員は、上院司法委員会の指導部への書簡で今回の要求を明らかにした。第2次トランプ政権下で共和党議員が大統領個人に向けた批判としては、これまでで最も強いものとなる。他の共和党上院議員はイランとの戦争やその他の政策を批判してきたが、大統領またはその家族が公職を私的利益のために利用したかどうかについて、現職の共和党上院議員が正式な調査を求めた例はない。

中間選挙は11月3日に迫っている。生活費高騰に対する有権者の不満は強まり、出口の見えない戦争が続く中で、トランプ氏の職務遂行に対する支持率は低下の一途をたどっている。一部の民主党候補からは、大統領の汚職疑惑と、共和党が米国民の経済的苦境に対処していないとの批判を結び付ける動きも見られる。

カーティス議員の書簡は、大統領との関係が「国内外の利害関係者による私的な金銭的利益、優遇措置、あるいはアクセス獲得のため」にどのように利用されているかを調べるよう司法委員会幹部に求めた。具体的には、トランプ・ジュニア氏が暗号資産事業で多額の利益を得ていることや、ロシアのオリガルヒが費用を負担した豪華な結婚式の祝賀行事に言及した。

カーティス議員（66）はまた、バイデン前大統領が公職に就いていた、あるいは選挙に立候補していた時期に、息子のハンター・バイデン氏が外国の利害関係者と重要なビジネス上のつながりを得ていたことを巡る疑惑も取り上げた。

ホワイトハウスとトランプ・ジュニア氏の代理人にコメントを求めたが、現時点で返答は得られていない。ハンター・バイデン氏の作品を扱う画廊も、コメントを求める電子メールに直ちに返答しなかった。

FAST

Sept 22 : Anthropic on Tuesday launched Claude Opus 5.5, a new AI model that it says delivers performance comparable to its top-tier Fable 5.1 while costing 40 per cent less to run than its predecessor.
The release lands amid growing debate over AI risks. CEO Dario Amodei earlier this month called on the global AI community to slow down the pace of releasing new capabilities to address safety concerns.
Anthropic said Opus 5.5 underwent external testing by independent AI safety research groups Frontier Design and METR before launch and includes safeguards previously reserved for its most capable systems.
According to Anthropic, Opus 5.5 outscored rival OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol on a software development benchmark while costing roughly one-third as much to run.

Opus 5.5 is priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, 20 per cent below Opus 5, Anthropic said. The model is available on platforms including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure.
The model also scored better than previous systems in internal safety tests and was about 85 per cent less likely than Opus 5 or Mythos 5.1 to attempt to bypass containment boundaries in a dedicated evaluation, the company said.
Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 will be released in the coming weeks, the company said, bringing many of the same performance, speed and safety improvements. 
Anthropic is also expanding programs that give vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences researchers broader access to the model.

items.title: 米軍、グリーンランド駐留拡大へ　デンマークと3者安保協定署名
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Gram Slattery　Jacob Gronholt-Pedersen

[国連／ブリュッセル　２２日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Gram Slattery　Jacob Gronholt-Pedersen

[国連／ブリュッセル　２２日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領とデンマーク、グリーンランドの首脳は２２日、デンマーク自治領グリーンランドでの米軍の駐留拡大を認める協定に署名した。戦略的要衝で豊富な鉱物資源を有する同島を巡る対立の解消につながる可能性がある。

協定はトランプ氏、デンマークのフレデリクセン首相、グリーンランド自治政府のニールセン首相が国連総会が開かれているニューヨークで署名。ロシアと中国が北極圏で存在感を強める中、トランプ氏はグリーンランドを米国領とするよう求めていたが、今回の協定はそこまで踏み込まなかった。

署名後に公表された協定文によると、米国は弾道ミサイルの脅威に対する防衛網として、グリーンランドに「ゴールデン・ドーム」防衛システムを設置することができる。欧州から北米への最短ルートは北極圏の同島を経由しており、同島には米軍最北端の基地も置かれている。

トランプ氏は署名式に先立って行った国連総会の一般討論演説で、この協定により米国はグリーンランドでの「安全保障およびその他のあらゆるニーズに対する恒久的な支配権」を得るとし、「今後、米国に敵対する国や勢力がグリーンランドに軍事拠点を設けたり、米政府の明示的な書面での承認なしに安全保障上重要な投資を行ったりすることは認めない」と表明。「われわれは直ちに適切な場所で大規模な軍事展開の準備に着手する。極めて大規模な軍事基地を２カ所建設する」と述べた。

フレデリクセン首相は、署名された協定は「永続し得る合意」とし、「北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）の重要性を改めて示すもので、グリーンランドの自決権も尊重されている」と語った。ニールセン首相も「ＮＡＴＯの強固さを維持することが極めて重要だ。北極圏でも同様で、ＮＡＴＯはこの地域で重要な役割を担っている」と述べ、北極圏でＮＡＴＯが果たす役割の重要性を強調した。

ＮＡＴＯのルッテ事務総長は米国、デンマーク、グリーンランドが署名した協定は集団安全保障を強化するものとの認識を示し、北極圏と北大西洋地域の安全保障強化は欧州と北米の双方にとって不可欠だと述べた。

米国はすでに、グリーンランド北西部の遠隔地でピツフィク宇宙軍基地を運営。今回の協定の下で新たに２カ所の軍事拠点が設けられるとみられている。拠点が設置されるのは、冷戦時代に空軍基地が置かれていたNarsarsuaqと、現在デンマーク軍の特殊部隊が使用しているMestersvigとみられている。

協定文によると、今回の合意は米国の駐留の法的根拠となってきた１９５１年の防衛協定を改定するもので、トランプ氏はグリーンランドの完全取得を目指す従来の構想から方針転換した格好となる。米国は冷戦期にグリーンランドに１７カ所の施設を設置し、１万人を超える要員を駐留させていた。今回の協定の下で行われるグリーンランドでの米軍インフラの大幅な拡充は冷戦期以降では初の大規模な拡張となる。

items.title: 米国債の価格差縮小、ヘッジファンドが好む「ベーシス取引」に陰り
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米国債市場で人気の「ベーシス取引」の規模が、ここ2年余りで最小となった。ウォール街のストラテジストは、ヘッジファンドが収益機会として利用できる債券市場の価格のゆがみが減っていることが要因とみている。

ベーシス取引は、米国債先物と、その原資産である現物国債とのわずかな価格差から利益を狙う取引で、多額の資金を借り入れて取引規模を膨らませる。米国債への需要を生み出し、32兆ドル（約5000兆円）規模の市場に流動性を供給する役割を果たしている。

この価格差が縮小する中、ベーシス取引の勢いは弱まっており、市場は重要な流動性供給源の一つを失う恐れがある。流動性の急激な低下は、過去に金融市場の混乱を引き起こしたことがあるものの、モルガン・スタンレーやシティグループなどのストラテジストは、ベーシス取引がなくなる状況には程遠く、勢いの変化は単に相対価値を利用した取引機会が減っているに過ぎないとの見方を示した。

シティの米金利戦略責任者、ジェーソン・ウィリアムズ氏は「価格のゆがみとボラティリティーが過去数年間で大幅に低下したため、ベーシス取引のポジションは縮小している。これはリスクを示すというより、取引機会の減少は、米国債への基礎的な需要が想定以上に強い可能性を示唆している」と分析する。

モルガン・スタンレーの推計によると、レバレッジ投資家による米国債ベーシス取引の想定元本総額は、年初の1兆2600億ドルから約9000億ドルに減少した。

モルガン・スタンレーのイーライ・カーター氏率いるチームは、短期の米国債に連動する先物では裁定取引の機会が縮小し、リターンの魅力が低下したことがベーシス取引の減少につながっていると指摘した。一方、長期の国債のベーシス取引は引き続き人気があるという。ストラテジストらは、取引減少に伴う市場のストレスを示す兆候はないとみている。

米国債市場は規模の拡大につれ、市場の円滑な機能に必要な流動性の供給をヘッジファンドに依存する度合いを高めてきた。近年、ヘッジファンドが好んで用いてきた戦略がベーシス取引で、通常は現物国債を買う一方、対応する先物を売る。

FAST

NEW YORK, Sept 22 : Meta has been testing a “human concierge” for its new personal AI assistant, Muse, which entails having human contractors quietly handle some of the phone calls placed via the digital agent, according to internal company posts seen by Reuters.
The Facebook and Instagram owner told employees about the test last week, shortly after the company publicly launched a phone-calling feature for Muse.
The Muse agent, which has topped US app download charts in the two weeks since its debut, is designed to autonomously perform tasks like sending emails, shopping and booking travel on a person's behalf.
With the phone-calling feature, a Muse user can tell the agent to dial phone numbers for US businesses and talk with people on the other end to handle errands like booking haircuts, checking whether a store has an item in stock or getting quotes from different contractors.

Some employees have raised privacy concerns about humans handling those calls, warning that the approach could result in sensitive information being shared unintentionally with contractors in call centers, the internal posts showed.
"It's baffling to me why we think this feature is worth the risk," one employee wrote in an internal post. "We are one bug away from unnecessary information being leaked to human callers."
Another employee, who had asked Muse to call an internet and cable provider to negotiate his bill, said a transcript showed the human contractor had made a racist reference during the call.
In response, a vice president in Meta's Superintelligence Labs unit acknowledged that "it was a miss" to start testing contractor-placed calls without proper disclosures and said the company had "rolled back this feature" for now.
Meta was still "hillclimbing AI calling," she added in her post, noting that some tests indicated having humans make the calls could get their success rate up to the 95 per cent to 98 per cent range, instead of the "lower percentage of AI calling."
She also apologized to the employee who reported the mention of race during a Muse call and promised that the "human agent" involved would not work on any Meta projects going forward.
HUMAN LABOR BEHIND AI PROMISES 
The Muse test offers a window into how tech companies sometimes rely on human labor behind the scenes to deliver on the promises of autonomous AI, as they bump up against reluctance to engage from those on the receiving end of robocalls.
It harks back to an earlier experiment Meta conducted a decade ago, when the company, then known as Facebook, trialed a digital assistant called "M" in its Messenger service. Media reports later estimated that around 70 per cent of the agent's tasks were actually carried out by humans.
Asked about the Muse "human concierge" plan, a Meta spokesperson said the response from employees had been "overwhelmingly positive" and that the purpose of the test was to "get feedback so we can implement safety and privacy protections and improve features before we release them publicly."
"We're working with merchants to continue improving this potential calling feature, and will only roll it out when it's ready and with the proper disclosures," said the spokesperson, Daniel Roberts.
Meta's Muse agent has had more than 2.5 million downloads since its release, according to data provided by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower.
The company's stock has soared more than 20 per cent since the launch, adding more than $200 billion in market capitalization to touch its highest level in more than seven months as of last close.
Shares edged down 0.6 per cent on Tuesday, however.
UNDERCUTTING A KEY SELLING POINT
Meta heavily emphasized the AI assistant's safety protections during its launch, telling would-be users that each agent would have its own secure “virtual machine,” or a dedicated computer in the cloud designed to keep people’s sessions isolated, and would keep sensitive information like passwords in separate secure storage.
Employees critiquing the human concierge plan inside Meta cited those security measures in their feedback, warning that it risked undercutting a key selling point for the agent.
Meta began having employees test out the phone-calling capability in August and gradually started rolling it out to Muse users in the days after the app’s debut, the internal posts showed.
Some users have reported problems with those calls, however, including one employee who said he tried calling his insurance company and "they keep hanging up on Muse when they hear it is AI."
Meta enabled the human concierge feature, also referred to as “human agent calls,” for half of its employees last week to overcome those issues, according to the internal posts.
“Muse is now able to hand requests to a trained agent, who places the call and works it through,” the post announcing the feature to employees said.
Employees who did not want to be included could join an opt-out group, according to the post.

Source: Reuters

items.title: AIの急速な進歩に国連事務総長が警鐘、トランプ氏は抑制に反発
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 国連のグテレス事務総長は22日、歯止めなく強まる企業の力や「キラーロボット」が横行するディストピア的な未来を回避すべく、AIへの規制を強化するよう訴えた。その一方で、トランプ米大統領は、AIがもたらすリスクには米国の既存の制度で対応できるとの考えを示した。

グテレス氏は、国連総会での任期最後となる演説を行い、最先端AIモデルの急速な進歩が国家の力を弱める恐れがあると警告した。グテレス氏だけでなく、英国やフランス、カナダの首脳や主要AI研究機関からもAIを巡って警戒感が示されている。

グテレス氏はAIの新たな安全対策を巡る国際的な合意を呼びかけ、「われわれは、権力が政府から一握りの民間企業や個人へと大きく移りつつあるのを目の当たりにしている」と指摘。「AIは驚異的なスピードで進歩しており、その影響の全容を理解するわれわれの能力を上回る勢いで突き進んでいる」と述べた。

これに対しトランプ氏は、国連総会での演説で「米国は、AIを管理するためのグローバリスト的な枠組みを構築しようとするいかなる試みも全面的に拒否する」と表明。「産業革命を上回る規模になるAIの発展を、私は抑え込むつもりはない」と述べた。

国連トップを10年にわたり務めてきたグテレス氏は、戦争や「武器として利用される」飢餓、加速する気候変動、人権や法の支配への尊重の後退に揺れる世界の厳しい将来像を描いた。特にAIとデータセンターを巡る開発競争が、劇的な変化の時代を左右する大きな力になっていると指摘した。米国と中国を念頭に、AIを安全に開発するためのガードレール（安全策）が必要だと訴えた。

グテレス氏は「最も高度なAI能力を持つ国の政府は、対話を促し、透明性や信頼、協力を確保する枠組みを構築するうえで、人類に対して最も大きな責任を負っている」と語った。

トランプ氏はAIを巡る議論で主要国首脳とは一線を画している。同氏は「慎重でなければならない」とした上で、「必要ならば法執行機関が抑制に動くだろう。だが、われわれは超知能の発展をあくまで後押ししていく。抑え込むのではなく、推進していく」と述べた。

items.title: グテレス国連事務総長、最後の総会演説　ＡＩ規制と国連改革訴え
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Antoni Slodkowski

[国連 ２２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Antoni Slodkowski

[国連 ２２日 ロイター] - 国連のグテレス事務総長は２２日、国連総会での最後の演説で、人工知能（ＡＩ）の規制、戦争の終結、気候変動への取り組み、深刻化する世界的課題への対応に苦慮している国連機関の抜本的な改革を訴えた。グテレス氏の２期目の５年の任期は１２月３１日に満了する。

同氏は演説で、ＡＩリスクに対する世界的な監視を改めて呼び掛け。「この技術革命を主導する国々は、新たな安全上のリスクに関する情報を共有し、試験と評価で協力し、われわれ全員を守る共通のセーフガードに向けて取り組まねばならない」と述べた。

また、各国指導者に対し、「ＡＩの責任ある進展のための条件と、リスクに対処するために必要な追加のセーフガードを推進すること」、そして「信頼性と独立性を備えた監視に支えられた、多国間のＡＩリスク管理の枠組みに向けて取り組むこと」を要請した。

グテレス氏は長らくＡＩのグローバルガバナンスを推進してきた。国連は２０２３年、ＡＩに関する諮問機関を設立。メンバーにはＩＴ企業幹部、政府高官のほか、米国、ロシア、日本などの学識経験者が名を連ねている。

中東情勢を巡っては、「緊張緩和と対話」を呼び掛けた。「共にこの議場から明確なメッセージを送ろう。戦闘を止めなければならない。人道支援を届けなければならない。そして、国際法に従って航行の権利と自由を完全に回復させなければならない」とグテレス氏は述べた。

さらに、環境問題では、汚染者負担の原則を徹底すべきとも改めて訴えた。これは同氏が国連トップとして１０年間にわたり掲げてきた主張である。

グテレス氏はまた、国連組織内の機能不全にも言及した。約１３０人の各国首脳がニューヨークに集まったものの、中国の習近平国家主席をはじめ、南アフリカ、インド、ドイツの指導者らは出席を見送った。

さらに、トランプ米大統領らからは、国連システムが肥大化して機能していないとの批判が上がっているほか、米が複数の国連機関から脱退し拠出金も大幅に削減している。こうした中、グテレス氏は「集団行動のためのわれわれの仕組みは、ますます強い圧力にさらされている」と述べ、国際機関は「大部分がすでに過ぎ去った時代の権力の現実と利害を、依然として反映している」と指摘した。

今回の演説は、大国が国連を迂回（うかい）する動きを強め、米政府が拠出金を大幅に削減する中でも、グテレス氏が国連を紛争の仲介者、新興技術のガバナンスの場として位置付けようとしてきた１０年間の任期の総決算となった。

「１月１日、私はもはや事務総長ではないが、これだけは確信してほしい。私がどこにいようと、何をしていようと、平和は可能であるという信念を掲げ続ける」と強調した。「私は国連憲章の価値のために立ち上がり続け、決して、決して諦めない。ありがとう」と締めくくった。

Nasdaq sets record high, oil dips on improved crude flows

NEW YORK, Sept 22 : The tech-heavy Nasdaq hit a record closing high on Tuesday, while oil prices and Treasury yields dipped in choppy trading as crude flows through the Middle East improved.
The Nasdaq was boosted by Micron Technology and other AI-related stocks as AI demand showed no signs of abating and corporate earnings stayed resilient.
"We maintain our constructive outlook on the AI trade, supported by rising adoption and monetization, as well as growing capital spending," said Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, chief investment officer Americas and global head of equities at UBS’ Chief Investment Office.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.45 per cent while the S&P 500 was flat and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.36 per cent.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe rose 0.11 per cent. The pan-European STOXX 600 index gained 0.13 per cent.
Lower oil prices added to risk appetite after a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran can reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States eases military pressure and lifts its blockade on Iranian ports.
Prices had briefly risen after US President Donald Trump said that a peace deal with Iran was likely after the midterm elections, which are scheduled for November. That is further away than many investors hoped.
"Naturally, he would be aiming for a deal before the midterms in order to preserve Republican control but it doesn't look like he thinks that's possible," said Adam Button, chief currency analyst at investingLive.
Oil fell again on increasing flows of Saudi crude with the restart of the East-West pipeline and ship movements through the Strait of Hormuz, through which 20 per cent of global supply moved before the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February.
US crude was last down 0.6 per cent at $94.59 a barrel and Brent fell to $98.30 per barrel, down 2.03 per cent on the day.
RATE HIKES ON THE WAY 
US 10-year Treasury yields fell 1 basis point on the day to 4.953 per cent, retreating in line with oil.
They remain elevated, however, as investors price in another round of rate hikes from major central banks as inflation remains sticky.
The dollar gained 0.12 per cent on the euro to $1.1448 and was little changed on the day at 157.37 Japanese yen.
The Bank of Japan raised rates last week to a 31-year high, but two dissenting votes and a lack of explicit hawkish guidance disappointed investors, which has left the yen vulnerable and kept traders on alert for signs of official intervention. 
"FX intervention remains a blunt tool to prop up currencies, and without a forceful monetary policy response it will be difficult for Japanese authorities to rein in the selloff in the yen," said Matthew Ryan, head of market strategy at Ebury.
The Federal Reserve raised rates last week and warned its fight against inflation was not over, keeping the door open to further tightening.
TRUMP-XI MEETING AWAITED
Attention is also turning to a meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping later this week, with investors watching for any indications that the leaders of the world's two largest economies can prevent a further deterioration in relations.
Xi arrives in Washington on Wednesday for the first time in more than a decade, helping fuel optimism that a trade truce between the two countries will be extended and there could be cooperation over AI.
"For markets, the big question is what’s going to happen when the current one-year trade truce expires in November, and whilst the general tone remains positive, there still isn’t an agreement yet," Deutsche Bank strategist Jim Reid said.  
(Reporting Karen Brettell, Amanda Cooper and Ankur Banerjee; Editing by Andrew Cawthorne, Alexander Smith and Jamie Freed)

items.title: Trump says freedom will come to Cuba in UN speech
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: President Donald Trump said Cuba was a failed state and freedom would be coming to the island nation in a UN address on Tuesday that increased tensions with the Communist-run government.
items.body:
President Donald Trump said Cuba was a failed state and freedom would be coming to the island nation in a UN address on Tuesday that increased tensions with the Communist-run government.
Washington has openly stated its goal is to change Cuba's government, and a US-imposed oil blockade since earlier this year has put the country under severe strain as it contends with fuel shortages and blackouts exacerbated by failing infrastructure.
"My administration is also seeking a fundamental change in the situation in Cuba, where the communist regime is under great pressure — the biggest pressure they've ever been under. It's an absolutely failed state, it's failing like never before, and it will fall," Trump said in his speech to the UN General Assembly.
"Communism will never be coming to America, but freedom will be coming to Cuba."
The Cuban delegation walked out of the UN General Assembly hall during Trump's remarks.
Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel said later in a post on social media website X that Cuba will defend its sovereignty, and accused Trump of painting the country as a threat to justify its harsh treatment.
The US has maintained a trade embargo on Cuba for more than 60 years and Trump's administration has been [USN:O8N42O02O TEXT:"stepping up pressure"], after using the military in January to remove Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.
Trump has called Cuba a failed nation in the past, including in June, when he said the US had some very good plans for Cuba and will take care of the country.
Cuba has been a US antagonist for decades, since Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution. Trump is strongly supported by hardline Cuban-Americans in Florida, who have pushed for US-instigated regime change for decades.

items.title: 湾岸諸国、トランプ米大統領にイランとの戦闘激化避けるよう要請へ
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 湾岸アラブ諸国は22日、トランプ米大統領との会談で、イランとの戦闘をこれ以上激化させないよう求める見通しだ。事情に詳しい複数の関係者が明らかにした。

サウジアラビア、アラブ首長国連邦（UAE）、カタールなど6カ国で構成する湾岸協力会議（GCC）の当局者は、ニューヨークで開かれる国連総会に合わせたトランプ氏との会談を前に、協議を重ねている。関係者らは、機微に触れる内容だとして匿名を条件に語った。

GCC諸国は戦争の終結を強く望んでいる。イランはこれまで、数千に上るミサイルや無人機で湾岸各国の領土や船舶を攻撃してきた。また、ホルムズ海峡の通航混乱が長引いていることを主な要因に、域内経済も縮小または大幅に減速している。

ただ、イランへの対応を巡っては、湾岸諸国の足並みがそろっていない。イランはエネルギー輸送の要衝であるホルムズ海峡で、船舶の通航を管理する権利が自国にあると主張しており、これを巡っても各国の見方は分かれている。それでも各国は、米国とイスラエルが2月下旬に始めた戦争の終結に向け、トランプ氏との会談を足掛かりにしたい考えだ。

トランプ氏の方針は定まっていない。開戦からまもなく7カ月となる中、イランへの追加爆撃を示唆する一方、合意を目指す考えも示してきた。トランプ氏は週末、FOXニュースに対し、今週ニューヨークでイランのペゼシュキアン大統領と会談する可能性があると語った。ただ、会談が実現する兆しは今のところない。

「私は大きな決断を下さなければならない」と、トランプ氏は22日、ニューヨークで開かれた国連総会の一般討論演説で述べた。同氏は「イランが国を立て直し、かつてないほど偉大な国を築けるような合意が成立するのか。それとも、私がイランを一気に壊滅させるのか」と続けた。

トランプ氏はさらに、11月3日の米中間選挙後には、イランが「合意に応じる」との見方を示した。

イランは以前から、原油の輸出や重要物資の輸入を阻む米国の海上封鎖が解除されない限り、協議を再開しないとしている。海上封鎖の影響もあり、イランのインフレ率は90%近くまで加速し、闇市場では通貨リアルが急落した。それでも、イラン指導部が態度を軟化させる兆しはない。

items.title: トランプ氏、米政府文書で「ＡＩ」に代わり「超知能」使用へ　国連演説
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [国連　２２日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[国連　２２日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２２日、米政府の文書では今後、人工知能（ＡＩ）に代わり「超知能（スーパーインテリジェンス）」という表現を使用する方針を明らかにした。ＡＩに関する警告は「デマ」だとする従来の主張も改めて繰り返した。 

トランプ氏は国連総会での演説で「今後、米国の全ての文書、そしてできれば世界中の文書においても、『人工（アーティフィシャル）』という表現の代わりに、はるかに正確な『超（スーパー）』という用語を使用するよう変更される。つまり『超知能』だ」と述べた。

その上で「産業革命を超える規模となるものの成長を、私は抑え込むつもりはない」との考えを示した。

items.title: Venezuelan man shot by ICE agent hospitalized for paralysis treatment, returned to detention, lawyer says
items.author: Brad Brooks, Julia Harte
items.creator: Brad Brooks, Julia Harte
items.summary: A Venezuelan man shot by a federal immigration agent in Austin, Texas, was treated at a hospital on Tuesday for paralysis on his left side after he had spent a night in ICE detention with a bullet lodged in his back, according to his lawyer.
items.body:
A Venezuelan man shot by a federal immigration agent in Austin, Texas, was treated at a hospital on Tuesday for paralysis on his left side after he had spent a night in ICE detention with a bullet lodged in his back, according to his lawyer.
Wilber Rafael Garces Perez was then returned to the detention facility 130 miles southwest of Austin later on Tuesday, his attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, said.
Lincoln-Goldfinch said in a written reply to Reuters' questions on Tuesday afternoon that Perez was back at an ICE detention center about 130 miles southwest of Austin.
During a news conference on Monday, Lincoln-Goldfinch introduced a man who phoned in as Perez, who said he had been transferred to the detention facility on Sunday after a few hours in the hospital following the shooting. On the Monday call, Perez, 28, said that he was still bleeding and was not receiving adequate medical care.
"I'm not doing well because of the gunshot I received," he said in Spanish. He added that he had to sleep on the floor at the detention center but did not explain.
The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, denied in a Tuesday statement that Perez was forced to sleep on the floor and also said that he had been receiving pain medications and other medical treatment while at the detention center.
The Austin Police Department on Tuesday released body-cam footage that showed its officers responding to the incident. In one video, Perez is seen inside his car as two ICE officers stand nearby. He tells police that his shoulder hurts, and he is told to exit the vehicle and is then placed in handcuffs. A police officer then uses shears to cut away his shirt, revealing a single gunshot wound to his upper back.
Perez said he had been out working as a DoorDash food delivery driver on Sunday when his car was sideswiped by the agents, who he said did not identify themselves or turn on any sort of lights or siren.
Perez said that an agent shot him while he was still in his car and that there had been no foot chase. Austin police said on Sunday that he had run from agents.
The Travis County District Attorney's Office on Tuesday requested that DHS halt removal proceedings against Perez while the investigation into his shooting continued, saying his ability to participate as a material witness would be "severely hindered" if he were deported.

items.title: Trump says US Justice Department could rein in AI companies if needed
items.author: Courtney Rozen, Gram Slattery
items.creator: Courtney Rozen, Gram Slattery
items.summary: President Donald Trump reiterated his opposition to new regulations on AI technology, telling global leaders at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday that US law enforcement agencies would rein in the sector if needed.
items.body:
President Donald Trump reiterated his opposition to new regulations on AI technology, telling global leaders at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday that US law enforcement agencies would rein in the sector if needed.
"We're going to watch it closely through the Department of Justice," Trump said, referring to AI technology and the top US law enforcement agency.
Public alarm about the potential danger posed by artificial intelliegence is growing, after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned and said, "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade."
Trump in recent weeks has dismissed alarms about AI, arguing that such claims are a "hoax."
"I'm not going to stifle growth of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution," he said.
Trump also said US government documents would use the term "super intelligence" going forward instead of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Trump renames AI 'super intelligence' as world leaders jostle over dangers
items.author: CNA
items.summary: US President Trump rejected calls for international supervision of AI, calling them a "globalist scheme" to control the new technology.

Trump renames AI 'super intelligence' as world leaders jostle over dangers

US President Trump rejected calls for international supervision of AI, calling them a "globalist scheme" to control the new technology.

US President Donald Trump addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), in New York City, US, September 22, 2026. REUTERS/Kylie Cooper

FAST

UNITED NATIONS: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday (Sep 22) announced that the US government would rename artificial intelligence "super intelligence" in official communications, as world leaders jostled over how to address the dangers of the fast-advancing technology.
AI has become a major topic at the UN General Assembly after incidents of the technology falling out of the control of humans and warnings by company insiders drew global alarm and calls for better government supervision of the industry.
Speaking to the assembly, Trump stood by his firm opposition to regulating AI, while arguing the word "artificial" undersold the technology and voicing hope the rest of the world would adopt the new term.
Super Intelligence "sounds much better" and "it's much more accurate", he said.

The rebrand is the latest in a series of renamings pursued by the Trump administration, which changed the Gulf of Mexico to the "Gulf of America" via executive order last year and, in August, renamed Lake Ontario "Lake America" amid a trade dispute with Canada.
The US leader also compared the warnings of AI safety advocates to warnings about climate change, whose human causes are affirmed by the overwhelming consensus of the scientific community.
"The United States totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control ... artificial intelligence," he said.
"Every major new technology brings challenges, and superintelligence is no exception," he added.
"The very same people who said we'll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming ... are now saying that AI is going to kill us all, that robots are going to attack us, and that everything is going to be a total disaster."
Ahead of the UN assembly, leaders of more than 20 mostly European countries urged binding safety measures for advanced AI, warning that the technology's development could outpace the ability to control it.
AI superpowers China and the United States did not endorse the idea.

Related:

UN chief calls for AI curbs and end to wars in his last assembly address

US-China AI rivalry: Can Trump and Xi agree on rules for the artificial intelligence race?

Trump returns to UN at a moment of anxiety about Iran, AI and the future of world body itself

"VASSALS" Speaking on the sidelines of the UN meeting, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he planned to use Britain's role as host of the Group of 20 next year to push for a "single set of global principles and standards" around AI, according to Bloomberg.
French President Emmanuel Macron proposed building AI technology independent from the great powers.
"I don't want anyone to become the vassal of one of the great powers," Macron told the UN General Assembly, apparently in reference to China and the US.
"Our investment capabilities must be pooled to build a cutting-edge open-source AI model, which we will share. We should not depend on somebody else."
The US-based AI giants themselves are increasingly asking for global coordination on AI safety, with OpenAI's Sam Altman set to address the UN Security Council on Wednesday.
Anthropic chief Dario Amodei and Hugging Face co-founder Clement Delangue will also participate remotely, a French official said Tuesday.
France, which holds the Security Council presidency this month, initiated the meeting and believes AI's threat to international peace and security has not been sufficiently discussed at the UN.
UN chief Antonio Guterres, meanwhile, called for the US and China to start a dialogue on the technology's future akin to US-Soviet engagement at the height of the Cold War.
"Governments with the greatest AI capabilities have the greatest responsibilities to humanity, to establish channels for dialogue," Guterres said in his address to the assembly.
"At a pivotal moment during the Cold War, strategic rivals came to recognise the need to manage shared existential risks."
China and the US are currently discussing creating a communication channel for AI concerns in anticipation of a Washington summit meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday.

Source: AFP/fs

items.title: 米有名VC、AI人材育成アカデミー設立へ―大学に代わる選択肢目指す
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米有力ベンチャーキャピタル（VC）のアンドリーセン・ホロウィッツは22日、AI製品を開発する若手人材を発掘・育成する新たなプログラムを立ち上げる計画を明らかにした。

同社が同日のブログ投稿で発表した。プログラムの名称はホロウィッツ・アンドリーセン・アカデミーで、参加は無料。住居やコンピューターなどの開発環境、旅費なども提供する。本来なら名門大学に進学する可能性のある学生に、大学に代わる選択肢を提供することを目的としている。主に、高校を卒業したばかりの若者や大学中退者を対象にする。

アンドリーセン・ホロウィッツによると、経験豊富な起業家から指導を受けながら自らのプロジェクトに取り組み、「シリコンバレーのスピードで学ぶ」ことを目指す若者を求めているという。

同アカデミーの設立に向け、アンドリーセン・ホロウィッツが4200万ドル（約66億円）を拠出する。このほか、フェイスブックの元最高技術責任者（CTO）アダム・ディアンジェロ氏や、パランティア・テクノロジーズのシャム・シャンカーCTOを含む個人投資家も出資する。

第1期は2027年秋にサンフランシスコで始まり、約50人を受け入れる予定。期間は1年間。翌年からは2年間のプログラムを提供することを目指している。

原題：Andreessen Horowitz Launches AI School as a College Alternative（抜粋）

items.title: ピムコ、米長期債のアンダーウエートを縮小－利回り5%超で妙味高まる
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米パシフィック・インベストメント・マネジメント（PIMCO）は、米長期債利回りが5%を上回ったことを受け、長期債のアンダーウエートを縮小していると、ダニエル・アイバシン最高投資責任者（CIO）が明らかにした。

世界的な債券売りで長期金利が約20年ぶりの高水準近辺で推移する中、同社は米国債に対してより中立的な姿勢を取っている。具体的には、残存5－7年の米国債に対する強気姿勢と、長期債に対する弱気姿勢の双方を縮小している。

「中期的な投資期間で見れば、十分な投資妙味がある」とアイバシン氏はインタビューで指摘。現在の環境では「分散と忍耐が必要だ」と語った。

イラン戦争に伴う原油高でインフレ懸念が強まる中、市場が債券に弱気になるのは当然だとアイバシン氏は指摘。年内は戦争とホルムズ海峡の通航再開を巡る動きが利回りを左右するとみている。

一方、より長期視点の投資家にとって、5%を超える利回りは魅力的な水準だと同氏は述べた。インフレ抑制に向けてFRBが追加利上げを続ける可能性が高い状況ではなおさらだという。

これはピムコにとって米国債戦略の転換となる。同社は米財政への懸念からここ数年、米長期債に弱気だった。6月時点でも、中期ゾーンを選好していた。

アイバシン氏は「財政問題の多くはすでに織り込まれている。これは米国だけの現象ではない」と指摘。「財政状況そのものに強い安心感を持っているわけではないが、現在のような利回り水準や実質利回りを踏まえると、投資妙味は高まっていると考えている」と述べた。

運用資産2320億ドル（約36兆5000億円）の「PIMCOインカム・ファンド」は年初来0.3%のマイナスとなっているものの、ブルームバーグがまとめたデータによると、広範な市場を追う同業ファンドの77%を上回る成績となっている。1年、3年、5年の各期間では、同業の90%超を上回っている。

米国の借り入れ拡大やAI投資向けの起債増加も、債券投資家にとって魅力的な投資機会を生んでいる、とアイバシン氏は指摘。「政府や企業がより多くの資金を借り入れる必要がある時には、われわれはより高い金利を要求できる」と述べた。

FAST

Sept 22 : Lassen Volcanic National Park offers a wondrous landscape of hot springs and other geothermal features in the Cascade mountains of California, fueled by molten rock deep below the surface. In one of these hot springs, scientists have discovered a microbe that surely is one of the toughest found anywhere on Earth.
This previously unknown species of amoeba — a type of single-celled organism known for its ability to change shapes freely — was found to survive and thrive at temperatures that would kill all other known complex life.
The species, named Incendiamoeba cascadensis, was able to perform cellular division, called mitosis, at up to 145.4 degrees Fahrenheit (63 degrees Celsius) and stay active at up to 147.2 F (64 C), continuing to find food and explore its environment. When exposed to heat up to 158 F (70 C), the amoeba was able to recover after being returned to lower temperatures.
Its heat tolerance is a record for any eukaryote, the expansive category of organisms on Earth covering people and the entire animal kingdom, plants, fungi and a vast array of microbes called protists including amoebae. Eukaryotes are considered complex life because their cells contain a membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-enclosed subcellular structures called organelles lacking in simpler organisms like bacteria.

"These temperatures surpass what was previously thought possible for any eukaryote and reopens questions about the limits of complex life," said biologist Beryl Rappaport of Syracuse University in Syracuse, New York, lead author of the research published on Tuesday in the journal Cell.
Its scientific name honors its heat tolerance, meaning "fire amoeba from the Cascades."
Amoebas are highly successful organisms, owing to their structural flexibility, numerous survival mechanisms and evolutionary adaptability. They can continuously change shape, often crawling by extending structures called pseudopods, or "false feet," and have prospered for hundreds of millions of years across a vast range of environments.
Until now, a few species of red algae, including Cyanidioschyzon merolae, and fungi, including Thermomyces lanuginosus, had held the heat-tolerance record for eukaryotes, at around 140 F (60 C).
There are some microbes that are not eukaryotes such as bacteria and archaea, as well as viruses — all lacking defined nuclei and all possessing smaller genomes. An archaeon called Methanopyrus kandleri holds the heat-tolerance record for all life on Earth, enduring temperatures of 252 F (122 C) — well above the boiling point for water — around hydrothermal vents in the deep ocean.
A MICROSCOPIC PREDATOR
The researchers discovered Incendiamoeba in a tributary off Hot Springs Creek, a thermal stream close to Lassen's Drakesbad area, according to Syracuse University biologist and study senior author Angela Oliverio. It was one of the few pH-neutral geothermal sites at Lassen, meaning neither acidic nor alkaline, and Incendiamoeba flourished in that setting.
The ability to withstand high temperatures has benefited Incendiamoeba. It is the top predator in its hot springs environment, feeding on heat-loving bacteria.
"One potential advantage for Incendiamoeba cascadensis to have this degree of heat tolerance is that it can avoid competition for food or other resources with other species by being the only organism of its kind in its environment. Because no organisms that feed on amoebae, like microscopic animals, have been found at these temperatures, it also avoids predators," Rappaport said.
The researchers documented how this amoeba protects itself at high temperatures by changing shape and forming a protective outer layer, and detected increased gene activity relating to DNA repair and the cell's internal shipping system under these conditions.
The discovery underscores the resilience of Earth's organisms.
"I think the most significant implications of this research is that it challenges our understanding of how and where eukaryotic life can persist. That has implications for understanding evolutionary biology in terms of fundamental constraints on complex cells and how they can evolve, and it expands the search for life on Earth and elsewhere in the universe," Oliverio said.
"I find it to be incredibly hopeful every time we expand our understanding of the myriad of ways in which life can persist in seemingly inhospitable environments," Oliverio said.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Fed's Collins says she supported rate hike, warns of elevated inflation risks
items.author: Michael Derby
items.creator: Michael Derby
items.summary: Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins wrote on Tuesday that she supported the US central bank's decision last week to raise interest rates in the face of risks that future inflation will be above the 2% target.
items.body:
Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins wrote on Tuesday that she supported the US central bank's decision last week to raise interest rates in the face of risks that future inflation will be above the 2% target.
"I now see an increased likelihood of future scenarios in which inflation remains notably above 2%," Collins wrote on LinkedIn . "With the labor market on a better footing, monetary policy can focus on a timely return to price stability, especially after five and a half years of too-high inflation," she said. "A somewhat more restrictive federal funds rate will help ensure that inflation durably returns to target."
The Fed last week [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"raised"] its interest rate target by a quarter of a percentage point to the 3.75%-4.00% range in an effort to curb price pressures. Policymakers also penciled in another rate increase before the year is out, although Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, who is averse to providing guidance about future monetary policy, did not affirm that Fed projection.
Collins, who is not a voting member of the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee this year, did not say in her posting if she wants rates to go up again.
The current outlook for the Fed is particularly challenging because much of the upward drift in price pressures is from supply shocks, such as the US-Israeli war with Iran, that are hard to counter with tighter monetary policy. The persistence of inflation above the 2% target, however, has pushed Fed officials to move away from looking through what would have once been viewed as transient hits to inflation.

items.title: ＦＲＢの割引窓口、市場の流動性を下支え＝ジェファーソン副議長
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [２２日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[２２日　ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のジェファーソン副議長は２２日、ＦＲＢの緊急融資制度に関する近年の改善により、金融機関が同制度を利用しやすくなり、市場の流動性、金融安定、金融政策の実施を支えているとの見方を示した。 

ジェファーソン氏はニューヨーク連銀で開催の米財務省証券市場に関する会議の講演原稿で「銀行に信頼できる流動性の供給源を提供することにより、割引窓口（ディスカウント・ウィンドウ）貸出制度は米国債の強制売却リスクを低減し、市場がストレスにさらされている時期にショックを吸収する役割を果たしている」と述べた。

ＦＲＢはこの貸出制度についてここ数年、複数の改良を行ってきたとし、その中には、現在ディスカウント・ウィンドウによる融資の６０％を処理し、銀行が電話ではなく電子的手段で地区連銀と連絡を取ることを可能にしたセルフサービス・ポータルの導入も含まれていると説明した。その上で、銀行側からは、このシステムにより中央銀行からの借り入れがより容易、迅速かつ効率的になったとの声が上がっていると述べた。

さらに、「こうした改善は、銀行が健全な状態にある時に割引窓口の利用をためらう要因となる摩擦を軽減し、銀行システム全体への信頼を強化するのに役立つと考えている」と指摘。日中の遅い時間帯でも米国債を担保として差し入れ、その日のうちにＦＲＢから融資を受けられる仕組みは、銀行自身にとってだけでなく、金融の安定全体を維持する上でも極めて重要だとの考えを示した。

同氏は、講演原稿で景気や金融政策の見通しには言及しなかった。

items.body:
ＦＲＢの割引窓口、市場の流動性を下支え＝ジェファーソン副議長
9/22 23:52 配信

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のジェファーソン副議長。仏パリで５月撮影。REUTERS/Tom Nicholson

[２２日　ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のジェファーソン副議長は２２日、ＦＲＢの緊急融資制度に関する近年の改善により、金融機関が同制度を利用しやすくなり、市場の流動性、金融安定、金融政策の実施を支えているとの見方を示した。 

ジェファーソン氏はニューヨーク連銀で開催の米財務省証券市場に関する会議の講演原稿で「銀行に信頼できる流動性の供給源を提供することにより、割引窓口（ディスカウント・ウィンドウ）貸出制度は米国債の強制売却リスクを低減し、市場がストレスにさらされている時期にショックを吸収する役割を果たしている」と述べた。

ＦＲＢはこの貸出制度についてここ数年、複数の改良を行ってきたとし、その中には、現在ディスカウント・ウィンドウによる融資の６０％を処理し、銀行が電話ではなく電子的手段で地区連銀と連絡を取ることを可能にしたセルフサービス・ポータルの導入も含まれていると説明した。その上で、銀行側からは、このシステムにより中央銀行からの借り入れがより容易、迅速かつ効率的になったとの声が上がっていると述べた。

さらに、「こうした改善は、銀行が健全な状態にある時に割引窓口の利用をためらう要因となる摩擦を軽減し、銀行システム全体への信頼を強化するのに役立つと考えている」と指摘。日中の遅い時間帯でも米国債を担保として差し入れ、その日のうちにＦＲＢから融資を受けられる仕組みは、銀行自身にとってだけでなく、金融の安定全体を維持する上でも極めて重要だとの考えを示した。

同氏は、講演原稿で景気や金融政策の見通しには言及しなかった。

items.title: Zuckerberg, Bourla among CEOs to attend Trump's state dinner for Xi, sources say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla and Meta Platforms chief Mark Zuckerberg are the latest corporate leaders to confirm plans to attend US President Donald Trump's state dinner at the White House on Thursday for Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to sources familiar with the matter.
items.body:
Pfizer (PFE.N) CEO Albert Bourla and Meta Platforms (META.O) chief Mark Zuckerberg are the latest corporate leaders to confirm plans to attend US President Donald Trump's state dinner at the White House on Thursday for Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to sources familiar with the matter.
Trump will welcome the Chinese leader at the White House this week for their second meeting this year, as the two leaders seek stability in a relationship under pressure over issues ranging from trade to Taiwan and Iran, as well as global worries about artificial intelligence.
Zuckerberg and Bourla will share the room with some of the biggest names in American business and technology.
Guests are expected to include Amazon's (AMZN.O) Jeff Bezos, Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Sundar Pichai, OpenAI's Sam Altman, Apple's (AAPL.O) Tim Cook, Tesla's (TSLA.O) Elon Musk, Nvidia's (NVDA.O) Jensen Huang and Dell Technologies' (DELL.N) Michael Dell.
JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) CEO Jamie Dimon and Citigroup (C.N) CEO Jane Fraser are also expected to attend.

items.title: トランプ氏、イラン「壊滅」警告　外交交渉進展も示唆
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Gram Slattery　Humeyra Pamuk

[国連 ２２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Gram Slattery　Humeyra Pamuk

[国連 ２２日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２２日、戦闘終結に向けた合意に至らなければイランを「壊滅させる」可能性があると警告した。ただ、国連で外交努力が進む中、近く合意が実現する可能性も示唆した。

国連総会の一般討論演説で「私は重大な決断を迫られている。イランが再建し、かつてないほど偉大な国を築くことを可能にする合意を結ぶのか」、もしくは「壊滅させ、二度と人々や国家を殺害し、破壊する機会を与えないようにするのかだ」と述べた。

イラン軍は国連でのトランプ氏の発言を「プロパガンダ」と一蹴し、イランは「より深刻で圧倒的、かつ予測不能な打撃を侵略者に与える完全な用意がある」と表明した。

一方、激しい言葉の応酬の裏では、約７カ月に及ぶ紛争を終結させるための協議が続いている。

トランプ氏は記者団に対し、米政府当局者がこの日にイラン代表団と約３時間にわたる協議を行ったと明らかにし、最終的に何らかの合意に達するとの見方を示した。ウィットコフ中東担当特使と自身の娘婿クシュナー氏がイランとの戦闘終結に向けた合意の可能性を巡り、仲介者らと「極めて生産的な会合を行った」とし、「合意に至る多くのモメンタムがある」と語った。

ウィットコフ氏はＸへの投稿で、米国とイランが仲介者を通じて長時間の協議を行い、仲介者は「終日、双方の間を行き来した」と明らかにした。その上で、仲介者が作業を継続するとし、この日の議論が「建設的で有望なものとなる」ことを期待していると述べた。

トランプ氏はホルムズ海峡の航行再開を望む湾岸諸国の首脳とも会談した。これらの国の多くには大規模な米軍基地があり、紛争開始以降イランの攻撃を繰り返し受けてきた。同氏は会談で「イランを巡る状況は（１１月３日の）米中間選挙直後、あるいはそれ以前に終結する可能性があると考えている。分からない。何が起こるか分からないものだ」と述べた。

こうした中、イランのアラグチ外相はカタールのムハンマド首相と会談した。カタール国営通信が伝えた。

イラン政府高官は、米国が軍事的圧力を緩和し、イランの港湾封鎖を解除すれば、７日以内にホルムズ海峡を再開できるとロイターに述べた。イランは先週、仲介者を通じて最新の提案を米側に伝達したという。

一方、これまでの交渉でイラン側の代表団を率いたガリバフ国会議長は、同国が決して降伏しないと言明。「トランプ氏は自らの力をイラン国民や軍に押し付けることはできないと理解しなければならない」と述べた。

items.title: 中国勢の台頭でＥＵ輸出シェア低下、ドイツ製造業に打撃＝ＥＣＢ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [フランクフルト ２２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[フランクフルト ２２日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）は２２日、中国企業が近年、高付加価値品やハイテク関連の製品で競争力を高める中、「世界的なモノの輸出に占める欧州連合（ＥＵ）のシェアが低下している」とする経済報告を公表した。機械や輸送機器などで顕著となっており、ＥＵ内ではドイツの企業が最も大きな打撃を受けているとした。

中国は、輸出型の欧州企業が存在感を示してきた市場に浸透しつつあるほか、国内生産拡大に伴い、欧州からの製品輸入も減少している。

ＥＣＢによると、ＥＵ主要国の中で、ドイツは輸出品の構成が中国と似通っている一方、イタリアはそれほどではないとした。このほか、アイルランドやギリシャなど経済が小規模な構成国への影響は限定的だという。「自動車や産業用機械など、過去数十年にわたって欧州経済をけん引してきた分野で競争が激化していることが示されている」と説明した。

中国への輸出減少については「ドイツや中欧など、欧州の製造や自動車産業のバリューチェーンに組み込まれている地域で最も顕著だ」と分析した。

items.title: 【米国市況】ナスダック100最高値、半導体株に買い－円は157円台前半
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 22日の米株式市場ではハイテク銘柄中心のナスダック100指数が5営業日続伸し、最高値を更新した。最高値更新は6月以来。半導体銘柄が買われた。イラン戦争終結に向けた外交努力への期待から原油価格が下げたことも、相場を支えた。

ナスダック100指数は0.8%高。フィラデルフィア半導体株指数（SOX）は6営業日続伸した。一方、KBW銀行株指数は下落した。

トランプ米大統領は22日、米当局者がニューヨークでイラン側の代表者と「非常に良い」会談を行ったと明らかにした。トランプ氏がイランを破壊すると改めて警告してから数時間後の会談で、外交による事態打開への期待が再び浮上した。

トランプ氏は、国連総会に合わせて行われた会談が3時間に及び、「非常に生産的」だったとし、近く次回会談を行う方向で調整していると述べた。トランプ氏はその後、スティーブ・ウィトコフ、ジャレッド・クシュナー両特使が会談に参加したと明らかにした。

米政権は中東での戦争終結に向けた取り組みを再び強める姿勢を示しており、トランプ氏は国連総会の一般討論演説で、11月の米中間選挙直後に戦争が終結するとの見方を示した。

セブンズ・リポートのトム・エッセイ氏は、「引き続き地政学情勢が焦点となる。米国とイランの停戦に向けた進展が確認されれば、原油価格と利回りは一段と低下し、株価は上昇するだろう」と述べた。

ネーションワイドのチーフ市場ストラテジスト、マーク・ハケット氏は「ハイテク株への投資と熱気が戻ってきた。その資金をどこかから捻出する必要がある」と指摘。金融株がハイテク株上昇のための「資金供給源」になっていると話した。

インタラクティブ・ブローカーズのチーフストラテジスト、スティーブ・ソスニック氏は、現在の市場では投資家は「相場が上昇すれば、積極的に追随して買う姿勢を示している」と指摘。その上で、投資家はハイテク株から資金を引き揚げることには消極的だと付け加えた。

items.title: S&P500種最高値付近、米イラン外交期待で原油下落－円は157円台前半
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 22日午前の米株式市場ではS&P500種株価指数が小幅上昇し、最高値付近で推移している。米国とイランの戦争終結に向けた外交努力の行方に注目が集まっている。原油価格は下落している。

S&P500種株価指数は約0.1%高。8月に付けた史上最高値に近づいている。北海ブレント先物はアジア時間帯には一時2%超上昇していた。だが、その後は下げに転じ一時1バレル＝98ドルを下回った。サウジアラビアはホルムズ海峡の迂回（うかい）ルートとして使われてきた東西石油パイプラインについて、再稼働に向けた初期段階の作業を進めていると、事情に詳しい関係者が明らかにした。

トランプ米大統領は、条件が整えば、国連総会出席のためニューヨークを訪れているイラン当局者との会談を設定したいとの意向を側近らに伝えた。事情に詳しい米当局者の話として、CNN記者がXに投稿した。

原油の急落を受けて、米国債利回りは一時低下したが、その後は下げを埋める展開。この日は690億ドル規模の2年債入札が実施され、23、24両日にもそれぞれ5年債と7年債の入札が予定されている。

セブンズ・リポートのトム・エッセイ氏は、「きょうも引き続き地政学情勢が焦点となる。米国とイランの停戦に向けた進展が確認されれば、原油価格と利回りは一段と低下し、株価は上昇するだろう」と述べた。

外国為替市場ではドルが方向感を欠く展開。円は対ドルで一時157円78銭まで売られた後、一気に1円近く急伸し156円83銭を付ける場面もあった。市場では日本当局による為替介入への警戒が強まっている。

ストーンXファイナンシャルの通貨トレーダー、呉明賾氏は「この水準で円キャリー取引に踏み切れるのは、勇気のある投資家だけだ」と指摘。円がさらに下落する余地は限られていると付け加えた。

原題：S&P 500 Holds Near Record High as Oil Prices Ease: Markets Wrap（抜粋）

items.title: ＮＹ連銀総裁、金利誘導の枠組み擁護　市場変化に応じ調整も
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Michael S. Derby

[ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Michael S. Derby

[ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] - ニューヨーク地区連銀のウィリアムズ総裁は２２日、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の金融政策運営の枠組みを擁護しつつ、金融市場の変化に合わせて調整・微修正が可能だとの考えを示した。

ウィリアムズ総裁はニューヨーク連銀で開かれた米国債市場に関する会議に向けた冒頭発言原稿で、短期金利を管理するための現行の一連の手段を用いて金融システムに「潤沢な」準備預金を供給する方式について、「金利の管理と中核的な金融市場の円滑な機能の支援において、極めて効果的であることが証明された」と述べた。

同総裁は発言の中で金融政策や金利の見通しについては触れず、会議での発言後に質疑応答を行う予定もない。

ウィリアムズ総裁は、ＦＲＢの金利誘導の枠組みはうまく機能してきたものの、固定的なものではなく、市場環境の変化に応じて適応させられると指摘した。

「市場が時代とともに進化する中、われわれは政策手段が必要な機能を果たすのにふさわしいものであり続けるようにしなければならない」とし、「端的に言えば、金融市場構造の進化は、金融政策をいかに効果的に実施するかの進化につながる」と述べた。

＜バランスシートを巡る議論＞

ウィリアムズ総裁は、ＦＲＢがさまざまな課題を検討する中で、インフレと雇用に関する責務を達成するために短期金利をどう管理するかという仕組みについて発言した。

ウォーシュ議長の下、ＦＲＢはコミュニケーションのあり方、データの評価方法、依然として大規模なバランスシートへの対応について幅広く検討する複数のタスクフォースを設けている。

ウィリアムズ総裁は「中央銀行に準備預金を保有することの機会費用は、ほとんど、または全くないはずだ」とし、「高い機会費用は単に非効率であり、市場機能と安定を妨げる他のゆがみを生み出す」と述べた。

その上でウィリアムズ総裁は、ＦＲＢの戦略は市場環境に対応したものになるとも指摘。「規制や市場構造の変化、あるいはその他の何らかの理由で準備預金の基調的な需要が変化すれば、ＦＲＢは時間をかけて準備預金の供給を変化させ、これに対応する」と述べた。

items.title: Republican senator calls for probe of Trump family business dealings
items.author: Susan Heavey
items.creator: Susan Heavey
items.summary: A Republican US senator on Tuesday called for an investigation into whether President Donald Trump's family is profiting from his time in office, saying any perception that family members are exploiting their position undermines trust in the government.
items.body:
A Republican US senator on Tuesday called for an investigation into whether President Donald Trump's family is profiting from his time in office, saying any perception that family members are exploiting their position undermines trust in the government.
Senator John Curtis wrote a letter to the Senate Judiciary Committee calling for a probe into businesses owned by Trump's eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., and payments by a Russian oligarch for his wedding celebrations in the Bahamas this year. Congressional [USN:L1N4570SP TEXT:"Democrats"] launched an investigation last week into the wedding payments.
Committee chairman Chuck Grassley told reporters he would consider the request seriously but cautioned that deciding on an investigation would take time. A decision was not expected until after the November 3 midterm elections.
The open letter marks the latest example of prominent Republicans attempting to create some distance between themselves and the [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"increasingly unpopular president"], six weeks from midterms in which his party is defending thin majorities in the US Congress.
Republican Senate candidates [USN:L1N45D0Y8 TEXT:"Ashley Hinson and Mike Rogers"] have called for a swift end to the Iran war, an unpopular conflict that has pushed up energy prices and the cost of living, which is Americans' top concern heading into the midterms.
Republican Paul LePage, the former Maine governor seeking a House seat, has criticized Trump's deportation of undocumented immigrants and argued that enforcement should focus on gang members and violent criminals.
"I don't think it's the dam breaking," Republican Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina told reporters when asked about the significance of the candidates' comments. "But they need to have the flexibility to express whatever real concerns they have, because the voters have those concerns."
Unlike Rogers, Hinson and LePage, letter-writer Curtis of Utah is not up for election until 2030. Tillis is due to retire in January.
Reuters/Ipsos polling this week showed Trump's public approval at 32%, its lowest point ever , and support for electing Republicans in the midterms also weakening.
Asked about Republicans in key battleground states calling for an end to the Iran war, US Vice President JD Vance told reporters it was "completely reasonable that Republicans are going to tailor their campaign messages."
'LEGITIMATE QUESTIONS' In the letter, Curtis urged the Senate panel to investigate presidential family relationships and their possible leverage by domestic and foreign entities, including wedding festivities worth hundreds of thousands of dollars for Trump Jr. paid by Russian oligarch [USN:L8N3KK0RL TEXT:"Umar Kremlev"].
Curtis also raised questions about Trump Jr.'s business ventures, including crypto promotion, real estate deals, prediction market platforms and more as his father controls the White House.
"These reports raise legitimate questions about foreign access to members of a sitting president's family and whether such relationships can create actual or perceived expectations of favorable treatment," he wrote. "They also may create expectations of a returned favor that ... could even create national security vulnerabilities."
Trump last week said his son [USN:L1N45A0XF TEXT:"is paying back"] Kremlev but offered no other details.
The Trumps have defended their family business dealings while Trump is in office and denied any conflicts of interest, pointing to a trust managed by Trump Jr. and Eric Trump.
Representatives for Trump Jr. did not respond to a request for comment.
A spokesperson said the Senate committee received the letter but that there was "extremely limited" time to schedule hearings this year.
EQUAL STANDARDS Curtis pointed to previous congressional investigations into Democratic former President Joe Biden's son, Hunter Biden, and said there should be equal standards, regardless of political party.
"The country should not have to accept one standard for the family of a Republican president and another for the family of a Democratic president," Curtis wrote.
Representatives for Hunter Biden could not be immediately reached. The younger Biden, who has worked as an artist, lawyer and investor, has faced years of scrutiny from Republican lawmakers, particularly over his foreign business dealings. He has denied any wrongdoing.
The panel's ranking Democrat, US senator Dick Durbin, in a separate statement backed Curtis' request.

items.title: ロシア・サウジ首脳が電話会談、海峡の安全確保を強調
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [モスクワ ２２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[モスクワ ２２日 ロイター] - ロシアのプーチン大統領は２２日、サウジアラビアのムハンマド皇太子と電話会談を行い、海運の要衝であるバベルマンデブ海峡とホルムズ海峡の航行の安全確保の重要性を強調した。

ロシア大統領府によると、中東情勢について詳細な意見交換が行われ、政治的・外交的解決が唯一現実的な前進の道であるとの認識で一致。イエメンの軍事・政治情勢が悪化する中、敵対行為の迅速な停止が必要との認識が示され、バベルマンデブ海峡とホルムズ海峡を含むこの地域の国際水路で船舶の安全で円滑な航行を確保する重要性が強調された。

items.title: 仏、ホルムズ海峡巡り新たな安保理決議案　米と連携し起草着手＝外交筋
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
John Irish

[国連　２２日　ロイター] -
items.body:
John Irish

[国連　２２日　ロイター] - フランスは、ホルムズ海峡の航行を回復するための国際ミッション設置を目指し、国連安全保障理事会決議案の起草に米国と連携して着手した。複数の外交筋が２２日、明らかにした。 

フランス政府は過去にもこの問題に関する決議案取りまとめを試みたが、失敗に終わっている。今回の動きは、マクロン仏大統領が２１日に国連総会に合わせてトランプ米大統領と会談したことを受けたものとなる。

マクロン氏はニューヨークのトランプタワーでの会談後、「いくつかの選択肢について協議した」とし、「今後数時間のうちに外交的解決策に取り組んでいく。これにより、包括的合意がなくとも、より多くのコンテナ船やタンカーの通航を可能にする方法を見いだせる可能性がある」と語った。 

外交筋によると、フランス政府は近く決議案を安保理に配布したい考えだが、具体的な時期については明らかにしなかった。 

決議案は同海峡の安全保障をイランとのより広範な緊張関係から切り離し、航行の自由とエネルギー供給へのアクセスを維持することが全ての国の共通利益であると強調する内容が中心となるという。 

同筋は「フランスは、ホルムズ海峡における航行の自由を保障する安保理決議について、米国やパートナー諸国と協力していきたいと考えている」と述べた。

items.title: US ties Sudanese army leader's UN visa to ceasefire plan, sources say
items.author: Daphne Psaledakis, Nafisa Eltahir, Antoni Slodkowski, Khalid Abdelaziz
items.creator: Daphne Psaledakis, Nafisa Eltahir, Antoni Slodkowski, Khalid Abdelaziz
items.summary: The United States is withholding a visa for Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ahead of his scheduled UN appearance in a move that Sudanese and other sources say is linked to a US-backed ceasefire proposal that Khartoum has resisted.
items.body:
The United States is withholding a visa for Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ahead of his scheduled UN appearance in a move that Sudanese and other sources say is linked to a US-backed ceasefire proposal that Khartoum has resisted.
The dispute, first reported by Reuters, threatens to deepen tensions between Washington and Sudan's army at a critical moment in [USN:L6N40Y0KB TEXT:"the civil war"], which the United Nations calls the world's largest humanitarian crisis.
A senior Sudanese source said Burhan had postponed his trip to New York but had yet to receive official notice that the visa had been denied.
"We in the Sudanese government express our deep regret because this is a violation of the UN Convention and international law," the source said. "Sudan's government affirms its stance towards peace."
Sudan's UN ambassador appealed to Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to intervene, arguing in a letter that preventing Burhan from attending the General Assembly would violate the UN's obligations toward member states.
US officials have made Burhan's attendance contingent on his agreeing to a 90-day ceasefire proposed by US Senior Advisor for Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos, according to a Sudanese diplomatic source and a Western analyst close to American and Sudanese officials.
The US State Department declined to comment on Burhan's visa.
State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a statement later on Tuesday that neither the Sudanese Armed Forces, the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary nor either of their respective leaders "represent legitimate, constitutional governance for Sudan."
"The United States and President Trump stand ready to work with anyone who is a serious partner for peace in Sudan. In the meantime, we will seek to raise the cost of continued conflict on all belligerents and the networks which fuel the conflict," he said.
The impasse represents a nadir in US-Sudan relations since war broke out in Sudan between the army and the RSF in April 2023, and comes as Burhan was scheduled to address the General Assembly on Thursday.
Another Sudanese source told Reuters that foreign minister Mohieldin Salem would give the address instead.
Sudan's army [USN:L6N43C14C TEXT:"voiced reservations"] about the Boulos-proposed ceasefire in July.
Burhan is unlikely to engage with Boulos' efforts further if the visa is not granted, the analyst and diplomatic sources said.
"Burhan rejects this take-it-or-leave-it approach, any proposal is subject to suggestions and changes," the Sudanese diplomatic source said.
The letter dated September 21, addressed to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and signed by Sudan's UN Ambassador Al-Harith Idriss Al-Harith, asked for the United Nations' "immediate intervention" with US authorities to ensure the issuance of the visa.
"Should this situation persist, it would effectively prevent the Head of State of a Member State of the United Nations from participating in person in the work of the General Assembly," read the letter.
UN 'DEEPLY CONCERNED' In a statement sent to Reuters, UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said the secretary-general is "deeply concerned that a visa has reportedly not yet been issued to the President of the Transitional Sovereign Council of the Sudan," adding that he is engaging with the US on the issue.
Burhan, the head of Sudan's army, has been the country's de facto leader since 2019, though the African Union and Western powers withdrew recognition after a 2021 coup he led with RSF head Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, against the civilian leadership.
Burhan has spoken at the UN General Assembly on Sudan's behalf since the coup.
Dagalo, known as Hemedti, has set up a rival government that has so far struggled to gain legitimacy.
The United States has made efforts to mediate the conflict within a so-called "Quad" format that also includes the United Arab Emirates, Egypt and Saudi Arabia, countries seen as having the most influence in Sudan.
In a piece in US outlet Foreign Policy published on Monday, Burhan said he would refuse external directives about the war and said previous pauses in fighting had only allowed the RSF and its backers to regroup.
Under the agreement for the United States to host the UN headquarters in New York, it is not supposed to deny visas, though it has [USN:L1N459003 TEXT:"denied entry"] to the head of the Palestinian Authority.
Relations between the US and Sudan's army have already been strained in recent weeks over a US proposal to extend an existing arms embargo over Sudan's Darfur region – the RSF's stronghold – to the rest of the country, a move that Burhan's backers say would disproportionately punish the army.
For his part, in a speech sending soldiers off to battle, Dagalo said "it's time for the rifles to speak."
Sudan's civilian prime minister before the coup, Abdalla Hamdok, is in New York this week as part of the General Assembly, along with members of his anti-war coalition.

items.title: 米ボストン連銀総裁、先週の利上げ支持　インフレ高止まりリスクを警戒
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [２２日 ロイター] -
items.body:

コリンズ総裁は交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「リンクトイン」への投稿で、「今や、インフレ率が２％を著しく上回る状態が続くシナリオの可能性が高まっているとみている」と指摘。「労働市場がより良好な基盤の上にある中で、金融政策は、特に５年半にわたって高すぎるインフレが続いた後だけに、物価安定への適時の回帰に集中できる」と述べた。

UN chief calls for AI curbs and end to wars in his last assembly address

United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres' address capped a decade-long tenure in which he sought to position the UN as a mediator in conflicts and a forum for governing emerging technologies, even as major powers increasingly bypassed the organisation.

United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US, Sep 22, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Shannon Stapleton)

UNITED NATIONS: United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres used his final address to the General Assembly on Tuesday (Sep 22) to urge world leaders to regulate artificial intelligence, end wars, focus on climate change and overhaul UN institutions he warned are struggling to confront mounting global challenges.
The former Portuguese prime minister, whose second five-year term ends on Dec 31, reiterated his calls for global oversight of AI risks , just as the UN's 15-member Security Council prepares to host AI leaders for a briefing on the powerful technology.
Guterres also reflected on the gridlock within the organisation, as nearly 130 world leaders gathered in New York, and Chinese President Xi Jinping and others - including leaders from South Africa, India and Germany - skipped the diplomatic meeting.
Delegates responded with sustained applause when Guterres defended a two-state solution for Israelis and Palestinians, demanded that "polluters must pay" for climate change and pressed for reforms to international institutions, causes he has championed throughout his decade leading the United Nations.

The address capped a decade-long tenure in which Guterres sought to position the UN as a mediator in conflicts and a forum for governing emerging technologies, even as major powers increasingly bypassed the organisation and Washington slashed its funding.
"Those countries leading this technological revolution must share information on emerging safety risks, cooperate on testing and evaluation - and work towards common safeguards that protect us all," Guterres told the assembly.
He called on the leaders gathered in New York to "advance the conditions for the responsible pacing of AI and the additional safeguards needed to address risks" and to "work towards a multilateral AI risk management framework, supported by credible and independent oversight".
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that Washington had proposed a new AI safety notification mechanism for US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi to consider at their summit this week. The proposal emerged from talks on establishing a US-China AI dialogue and would cover AI-related incidents with national security implications.

Related:

UN General Assembly: Wars, geopolitical divides, AI and climate change test global cooperation

Guterres enters final UN General Assembly with legacy shaped by a more divided world

A CHAMPION FOR GLOBAL GOVERNANCE OF AI Guterres has long pushed for global governance of AI. In 2023, the UN created a 39-member advisory body on AI, with members including tech company executives, government officials and academics from countries such as the US, Russia and Japan.
The Security Council, which is charged with maintaining international peace and security, met for the first time on the risks of artificial intelligence the same year, when China said the technology should not become a "runaway horse" and Washington warned against its use to censor or repress people.
On the Middle East, where the conflict has widened as Houthi gains along the Red Sea coast threaten shipping routes and tensions persist in the Strait of Hormuz, Guterres called for "de-escalation and dialogue".
"Together, let's send a clear message from this hall: The fighting must stop. Humanitarian aid must flow. And navigational rights and freedoms must be fully restored in accordance with international law," Guterres said.
On the UN system, criticised by Trump and others as bloated and ineffective after Washington withdrew from several UN agencies and slashed funding, Guterres said, "our mechanisms for collective action are under growing strain" and global institutions "continue to reflect the power realities and interests of a largely bygone age".
Guterres used the address to bid farewell to most of the global leaders he has worked with over the last 10 years.
"So, on January 1st, when I am no longer secretary-general, be sure of this. Wherever I will be, whatever I will be doing - I will keep championing the conviction that peace is possible," he said. "I will continue to stand up for the values of the United Nations Charter and I will never, ever give up. Thank you."

Related:

Trump’s a la carte approach to the UN: What’s on the menu – and what’s not

Source: Reuters/aj

Iran, US hint at revival of talks as Trump, Pezeshkian due to attend UN

Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz to Gulf shipping within seven days if the US fulfilled Tehran's demands to ease military pressure and lift the blockade on Iranian ports, says an Iranian official.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian speaks before departing for New York, at Mehrabad Airport in Tehran, Iran, on Sep 22, 2026. (Photo: Iran's Presidential website/West Asia News Agency/Handout via REUTERS)

FAST

DUBAI: Iran and the United States hinted on Tuesday (Sep 22) at the prospect of reviving negotiations to end their conflict, with the presidents of both countries due at the UN General Assembly in New York .
The event would be the first attended by Donald Trump and Masoud Pezeshkian since Trump launched "Operation Epic Fury" against Iran in February, alongside Israel. Trump had said on Sunday he would be open to a meeting with the Iranian president.
A senior Iranian official said there were no plans for the two leaders to meet directly, but that Iran's delegation had full authority to revive talks.
Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz to Gulf shipping within seven days if the US fulfilled Tehran's demands to ease military pressure and lift an American blockade on Iranian ports, the Iranian official said, adding that Iran had conveyed its latest proposal to Washington via mediators last week.
"The US needs to announce that it wants to resolve the issue diplomatically, make that official, and then agree on a timeline for how the process will move forward," the official said. "The UN General Assembly is a golden opportunity for the US to return to diplomacy."
Secretary of State Marco Rubio told NBC's Today show the US was open to speaking with the Iranians, "especially if it has the prospects of leading to something positive and ultimately achieving the goal of what this is all about".
No face-to-face meetings between Iran and the United States are known to have taken place since July, when an agreement on an interim deal to end the war collapsed just weeks after it was signed by Trump and Pezeshkian.
Asked by Fox and Friends about the prospect of a meeting between the presidents, Rubio said of Trump: "He's a businessman who comes from the world of practicality and common sense. And common sense tells you there's no harm in engaging and talking to someone."
REMINDERS OF HARDLINE POSITIONS But Rubio also noted that Pezeshkian is subordinate under Iran's ruling system to Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, "and the supreme leader is a radical Shia cleric and we need to remember that when we talk".
"The central issue here is Iran is run by lunatic clerics," Rubio told Fox. "These people can never have nuclear weapons."
In a reminder of Iran's firm position so far, Parliament Speaker Mohammed Baqer Qalibaf, who headed Iran's negotiating team at previous talks, said on Tuesday that Iran would never surrender: "Trump must understand that he cannot impose his power on the Iranian people and its armed forces."
Trump is due to meet on Tuesday with leaders of the six Gulf Arab states: Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
All are keen to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz but wary of giving their longstanding rival Iran too much power. All apart from Oman also host huge US military bases that have come under repeated Iranian attack throughout the war.

Related:

UN mission finds grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran, and Tehran crimes against humanity

UN General Assembly: Wars, geopolitical divides, AI and climate change test global cooperation

SAUDIS SEEK US SUPPORT AGAINST HOUTHIS The biggest of them, Saudi Arabia, has been drawn deeper into the war this month, with Houthi fighters aligned to Iran advancing in Yemen, routing forces of a Saudi-backed government there and threatening Saudi oil exports through the Red Sea.
There was some relief on oil markets on Tuesday, after sources told Reuters that Saudi Arabia had restarted operations at its East-West Pipeline and could resume exports within hours, albeit at reduced volume, from the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
The pipeline, Saudi Arabia's main alternative route for exports to bypass wartime disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, was shut down after attacks this month that Riyadh blamed on Iranian allies in Iraq.
The Houthis have routed Saudi-supported government forces along the Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at its mouth, and have attacked Saudi Arabia directly with missiles and drones . The fighters are now pushing to seize the strategic heights of the Kahboub Mountains that overlook the Red Sea coast.
The US, which bombed the Houthis for two months last year, has so far rebuffed repeated pleas from Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to rejoin the fight. The New York Times reported that Trump called off US strikes against the Houthis on Sunday at the last minute, after troops had already begun loading bombs onto planes.
Asked why Washington had so far held back from striking the Houthis, Rubio said: "Ultimately, if it comes down to it, the United States will always stand with Saudi Arabia and support them because we have an agreement with them to do so.
"That said, that is a very dangerous and complex conflict that pre-exists ... We have a history with the Houthis as well, and that's something we don't want to see impacted either."
QATARI PROPOSAL ON THE TABLE On the table at the Gulf states' meeting with Trump is a Qatari proposal for a framework to bring Iran and the Arab Gulf states into a common security architecture, regional sources said. One source said Iran was reviewing the proposal.
Speaking at a Qatar Economic Forum in New York on Sunday, Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani said any such arrangement would need to provide security guarantees for the Gulf states and expand economic interdependence with Iran.
"Lasting security cannot be built through repeated cycles of escalations and retaliation, or arrangements that leave any state permanently exposed to insecurity," Sheikh Mohammed said.
