items.title: Fed's Williams says rate-control toolkit is working well
items.author: Michael Derby
items.creator: Michael Derby
items.summary: New York Federal Reserve President John Williams defended the US central bank's monetary policy implementation system on Tuesday, while saying it can be adjusted and tweaked in line with changes in financial markets.
items.body:
New York Federal Reserve President John Williams defended the US central bank's monetary policy implementation system on Tuesday, while saying it can be adjusted and tweaked in line with changes in financial markets.
Supplying "ample" reserves to the financial system with the current suite of tools to manage short-term interest rates "has proven to be highly effective at delivering interest rate control and supporting the smooth functioning of core financial markets," Williams said in prepared opening remarks for a conference on the Treasury market at the New York Fed.
Williams did not address the outlook for monetary policy or interest rates in his remarks and he was not scheduled to take questions following his speech to the conference.
The New York Fed chief said that while the central bank's rate-control framework has worked well, it is not set in stone and can be adapted to changing market conditions.
"As markets evolve over time, we must ensure that policy tools are fit for purpose to carry out their necessary functions," Williams said. "Put simply, the evolution of financial market structure leads to the evolution of how we carry out monetary policy effectively."
DEBATE OVER BALANCE SHEET Williams made his remarks on the mechanics of how the Fed manages short-term interest rates to achieve its inflation and employment mandates as the central bank is reflecting on a range of issues.
The central bank under new Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has a series of task forces looking broadly at how it communicates, evaluates data and deals with its still large balance sheet. Warsh, before taking over as Fed chief in May, routinely criticized the central bank for its large asset holdings and system of providing substantial liquidity to the financial system in the form of reserves.
Before the 2008 financial crisis, the Fed kept liquidity tight in financial markets, but that approach was abandoned.
Fed officials have argued for some time that keeping strong amounts of liquidity in the system helps promote financial stability. They have also said the tools the central bank uses to manage liquidity enable strong control over short-term rates, which is the critical issue in the entire debate.
"There should be little or no opportunity cost to holding reserves at the central bank," Williams said. "A high opportunity cost is simply inefficient and creates other distortions that interfere with market functioning and stability."
Williams, however, noted that the Fed's strategy will be responsive to market conditions.
"If underlying demand for reserves shifts due to changes in regulation, market structure, or any other reason, the Federal Reserve will match that with a shift in the supply of reserves over time," he said.

items.title: 米国人の73％「ＡＩ企業の対策不十分」、悪影響指摘は過去最高＝調査
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Jason Lange

[ワシントン　２２日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Jason Lange

[ワシントン　２２日　ロイター] - ロイター／イプソスが２２日に公表した世論調査によると、米国人の４分の３にあたる約７３％が、人工知能（ＡＩ）が社会に深刻な害を及ぼすのを防ぐための取り組みがＡＩ企業側で十分に進んでいないと懸念していることが分かった。

回答者の３９％がＡＩは社会に悪影響を及ぼしていると答え、前月の３６％から上昇。ロイター／イプソスがこの質問を始めた３月以降で最も高い割合となった。この新しい技術を肯定的に捉えているとの回答は１１％にとどまった。残りの回答者は「分からない」か、質問に答えなかった。

調査ではまた、多くの米国人がＡＩ企業の自主規制能力に信頼を置いていないことも示された。回答者の大半は、安全基準の策定に連邦政府が主要な役割を果たすべきだと回答した。

大手ＡＩ企業が開発の減速や、より厳格な監督・安全基準を求めているとのニュースを追っていると答えた米国人は約６９％に上った。

ＡＩ開発を減速させることは「良いこと」と答えた回答者が５５％だったのに対し、「悪いこと」と答えたのは１３％にとどまった。残りは「分からない」または回答しなかった。

また、回答者の７３％が、米国にとって安全かつ責任あるＡＩ開発を確保することがより重要だと答え、世界のＡＩ開発競争で先頭に立ち続けることがより重要だと答えたのは２３％だった。

調査は２０日までの４日間、オンラインで実施され、全米の成人１２７７人から回答を得た。誤差の範囲はプラスマイナス３ポイント。

Sept 22 : Palo Alto Networks said on Tuesday it would launch a new cybersecurity service for businesses, using advanced AI models from Anthropic and OpenAI to help identify security vulnerabilities across corporate systems.
Hackers are increasingly using AI to find and exploit weaknesses in corporate networks, prompting cybersecurity firms to build defenses that can detect and respond to threats more quickly.
The service, called Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense, will use cyber-focused AI models including Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Cyber, along with open-weight models, the company said.
The offering is designed to continuously test web applications, application programming interfaces and cloud infrastructure, helping customers identify vulnerabilities and possible attack paths as their digital environments change.

items.title: India's Russian oil imports fell in August, seen lower in September, data shows
items.author: Nidhi Verma
items.creator: Nidhi Verma
items.summary: Russia's share in India's oil imports fell in August, while supplies from the Middle East increased as Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) sold oil from the region from outside the Strait of Hormuz, data from trade sources showed.
items.body:
Russia's share in India's oil imports fell in August, while supplies from the Middle East increased as Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) sold oil from the region from outside the Strait of Hormuz, data from trade sources showed.
United Arab Emirates' state-run ADNOC has strengthened its shipping operations, [USN:L1N44B00A TEXT:"shuttling"] oil from its fields inside the Strait of Hormuz for sale from storage and export terminals at Fujairah and Sohar.
In addition to its own crude, ADNOC is also buying oil from neighbouring producers such as [USN:L6N4570UO TEXT:"Iraq"] for resale.
India's Russian oil imports fell 16.5% in August from the previous month to about 2.1 million barrels per day (bpd), the data showed. Russia remained India's top oil supplier, followed by the UAE and Venezuela.
The world's third-biggest oil importer's purchase of Iraqi oil surged by about a quarter to about 171,000 bpd, the data showed.
Imports from the UAE fell 5.4% from July to about 620,000 bpd, while those from Saudi Arabia, which [USN:L4N45A0IK TEXT:"offered"] crude oil from ports [USN:L1N44F014 TEXT:"outside"] the Strait, rose 1.5% to 328,000 bpd.
India boosted purchases of Russian oil after U.S.-Iran tensions led to a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
However, India's Russian oil imports are estimated to decline to 1.9 million bpd in September, according to preliminary data from Kpler.
Indian refiners are tapping spot markets for October and November supplies as they fear they may have to reduce purchases from Moscow to protect India's wider economic interests if U.S. President [USN:L1N45A0ZU TEXT:"Donald Trump"] decides to impose up to a 100% tariff on countries buying Russian oil.
New Delhi, which is negotiating a trade deal with Washington, has said it remains "firmly committed" to ensuring [USN:L1N45904J TEXT:"energy security"] for its people and would continue to source supplies from diverse sellers based on market dynamics.
Overall, India's oil imports fell 8.8% in August to 4.44 million bpd, the data showed.

items.title: Snorkel AI valued at $3.5 billion amid surging demand for complex AI training data
items.author: Krystal Hu
items.creator: Krystal Hu
items.summary: Data startup Snorkel AI has raised $350 million in fresh funding at a $3.5 billion valuation, its CEO Alex Ratner told Reuters, as booming demand from frontier AI labs for increasingly complex training data and simulated environments fuels rapid growth.
items.body:
Data startup Snorkel AI has raised $350 million in fresh funding at a $3.5 billion valuation, its CEO Alex Ratner told Reuters, as booming demand from frontier AI labs for increasingly complex training data and simulated environments fuels rapid growth.
Led by Insight Partners and S32, the funding round included participation from existing investors Addition, Greylock and Wells Fargo, the company said. The deal values the company at nearly three times the $1.3 billion valuation achieved when it last raised $100 million in May 2025.
The San Francisco-based company said its annualized revenue run-rate has crossed $350 million, from roughly $20 million a year earlier, driven by the data-as-a-service business it launched in September 2025.
Founded in 2019 by a team of researchers spinning out of the Stanford AI lab, Snorkel AI initially sold software but has shifted toward supplying finished datasets and reinforcement-learning, or RL, environments directly to customers.
Ratner said demand had grown as AI developers moved beyond simpler labeling work and sought harder, higher-stakes data to train and evaluate increasingly capable systems.
Snorkel now offers what it calls an "agentic data development platform" that pairs human experts with thousands of specialized AI models and agents to create and vet data. Experts devise design scenarios, tasks and grading rubrics, while AI automates much of the labor-intensive quality assurance process, Ratner said, as it partners with AI labs to design ways to acquire high-quality datasets.
The business taps a network of tens of thousands of specialists across fields such as coding, law and medicine. Ratner said Snorkel sells the data products they generate rather than charging for human labor, a model that lets it pay experts more generously while preserving margins.
"Our strong view is that 100% of the data that labs will get value out of will have some human input in the foreseeable future," Ratner said. "But 100% of that data will have to use synthetic and automated approaches to keep up with this complexity."
The company says it works with frontier AI labs, hyperscalers, enterprises and the US federal government. Coding data is one of Snorkel's biggest areas of demand.
Venture funding continues to pour into startups supplying frontier AI labs with human-annotated training data, a market transformed after Meta's $14.3 billion purchase of a 49% stake in Scale AI in June 2025. Rivals including Mercor and Surge AI have also attracted investor interest amid strong revenue growth.
Ratner said the fresh capital would be used to hire researchers and engineers, while expanding the company's enterprise and government operations. The startup also plans to support third-party AI model evaluations and push into new industry verticals and data modalities.
While growth remains the priority, the company said it expects to reach profitability this year.
“Data is becoming more rare, more specialized, more difficult to find," said Andy Harrison, partner at S32 who co-led the funding. “If you want to train the most frontier, complex and capable models, now you need superior data."

items.title: AI 'Terminator’ fears may mask real Chinese threat: McGeever
items.author: Jamie McGeever
items.creator: Jamie McGeever
items.summary: The recent spike in apocalyptic AI warnings from Anthropic, OpenAI and others could reflect genuine fears about this rapidly advancing technology’s threat to humanity, but it may also signal a more prosaic fear about the Chinese threat to US tech firms’ business models. As Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping prepare to meet in Washington this week, the two countries could be entering a new phase in the AI arms race.
items.body:
The recent spike in apocalyptic AI warnings from Anthropic, OpenAI and others could reflect genuine fears about this rapidly advancing technology’s threat to humanity, but it may also signal a more prosaic fear about the Chinese threat to US tech firms’ business models. As Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping prepare to [USN:L8N456219 TEXT:"meet in Washington"] this week, the two countries could be entering a new phase in the AI arms race.
Financial markets have long worried about US tech's mountainous borrowing to [USN:L6N45610J TEXT:"fuel the AI buildout"], but these anxieties have been compounded in recent weeks by a sudden burst of doomsday scenarios floated and promoted by industry insiders.
The [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"recent wave"] of AI “doomerism” kicked off on September 8 when former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon posted on X that "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade." His post has been viewed 173 million times, sparking a wildfire debate about the pace and safety of AI development that has drawn in the most powerful leaders in the industry, wider business world, and government.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on September 12 penned a lengthy essay on the need to moderate the development of AI model capabilities. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX (SPCX.O) founder Elon Musk expressed agreement, broadly calling for the technology to be slowed down or subjected to greater oversight.
The [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"sudden wave of apocalyptic warnings"] seems to have caught everyone off guard – including the Trump administration.
Trump, who has long played down AI security and safety concerns, said he plans to appoint a new [USN:FWN45B02T TEXT:""AI czar""] and to create an "AI force,” though few details are available on either.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also said the two superpowers have agreed to set up a [USN:S0N43U00Y TEXT:"formalized dialogue"] on AI, and senior officials will meet in China later this year.
On the surface, the tech leaders and the president may seem miles apart, but a growing chorus of investors is questioning whether fears about China’s growing AI prowess – and the challenges it could pose to already difficult AI economics – may actually be shared in Silicon Valley and the White House.
‘TERMINATOR’ GARBAGE AI sentiment is increasingly pushing investors into two camps: those who believe the trillions of dollars of investment by US hyperscalers and AI firms will pay off, and those who don't.
The first camp still appears to have the upper hand, as evidenced by the Nasdaq's (.IXIC) rebound this week to its recent all-time high. But those in the second camp are gaining ground. Many now argue that the burst of "concern" shown by AI leaders and insiders about the future of mankind is simply a veiled plea for government help, reflecting the industry’s bleak financial outlook.
"I think these companies are very nervous, they realize that there are no moats around their business whatsoever, and they're trying to manufacture a crisis that will create regulation that they think they can then manipulate to create the moats, to create the duopoly that they want," investor Steve Eisman told CNBC last week, referring to Anthropic and OpenAI. "I think this whole 'Terminator' thing is garbage."
Sounds conspiratorial? Maybe. But the mounting concerns are real.
The mooted OpenAI and Anthropic initial public offerings (IPOs) are getting [USN:L6N45407M TEXT:"pushed back"], even as the record-breaking US capital expenditure (capex) spree continues to accelerate, and debt piles rise.
The US hyperscalers, along with Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Broadcom (AVGO.O) , have more than $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments and guarantees, with more "financing structures under development,“ according to Morgan Stanley.
On top of this is the intricate web of circular financing that raises concerns even among some AI optimists - AI could revolutionize society, but an unwind of these convoluted financing schemes could create a lot of pain for investors along the way.
SPEND MORE TO MAKE MORE The real risk keeping US AI leaders up at night may be less Arnold Schwarzenegger and more Adam Smith.
Cheap large language models (LLMs) from China are proliferating rapidly, putting significant competitive pressure on costlier US offerings. For example, a version of Chinese startup DeepSeek's flagship AI model could be [USN:L8N43Z05S TEXT:"more than 100 times cheaper"] to run than Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 model. Products from other Chinese firms are up to 50 times cheaper than leading US versions, and Chinese LLMs are rapidly closing the performance gap with the more expensive US frontier models, analysts say.
The US AI industry is facing this rising competition by spending and investing on a massive scale. Hyperscalers are expected to invest up to $1.5 trillion in AI next year.
“You have to spend money to make money, or at least the hyperscalers are testing the motto. The AI buildout is expensive, but likely worth it,” says Ryan Sweet at Oxford Economics.
But for that to be the case, the big outlays must be followed by big revenues. Apollo Global Management's Torsten Slok estimates that hyperscalers' operating cash flow needs to more than triple from last year's $600 billion to $2 trillion in 2030 to justify these vast expenditures. That’s a high bar. And it’s one that could become even more difficult to reach if China’s cheaper LLMs see their market share continue to grow.
If these gains don’t materialize, hyperscalers’ capex may be slashed, slowing chipmakers’ revenue growth and Wall Street’s AI-driven rally. This, in turn, could ultimately slow US economic growth.
Few expect any firm understanding on AI to be hashed out at Trump and Xi’s meeting this week, but the statements from both on the technological front could speak volumes about whether US tech firms have more to fear from rogue agents or simple economics.
(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters)

FAST

Sept 22 : Wall Street has turned bullish on Meta Platforms, betting that its new AI agent Muse could open a new revenue stream for the social media giant and reshape the company's AI monetization prospects.
Muse, launched on September 8, is an AI assistant that can send emails, book travel and complete transactions such as selling a car on behalf of a user. The basic version is free, with subscriptions priced at $20 and $100 a month for heavier use.
Since its launch, shares of Meta Platforms have surged more than 20 per cent, outpacing the "Magnificent 7" group of US tech companies during the period. Shares have added over $200 billion in market capitalization to touch their highest level in more than seven months as of last close.
Shares were up 0.5 per cent on Tuesday, after surging more than 11 per cent in the previous session.

"While it is still early, we believe that Muse has the potential to become the most widely used consumer AI application since ChatGPT," J.P.Morgan analysts said in a note, crediting the app's early traction to strong product-market fit, Meta's distribution reach and a free tier that lowers the barrier to trial and repeat use.
The Muse app, available on iOS and Android, but only in the US and Canada regions, has clocked 2.8 million downloads in the first 12 days of launch, according to data from Apptopia.
If compared on similar metrics to the first 12 days of OpenAI's ChatGPT, Muse has 1.8 million downloads versus ChatGPT's 1.3 million.
Early reviews suggest "functionality is resonating with users, particularly agent's ability to execute multi-step tasks and workflows with limited user intervention," BofA Global Research analysts said.
Enthusiasm around Muse sparked a Wall Street tech rally on Monday, lifting Meta shares more than 11 per cent and boosting chipmakers, including AMD and Intel, with AMD crossing the $1 trillion valuation mark for the first time.
"The market has interpreted Muse as a boon for the already significantly bottlenecked CPU market," said Michael O'Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading.
Brokerage Jefferies estimated that if Muse could see 1 billion users by end of 2027 and at least 3 per cent transition to a paid version, it could result in $10.8 billion in annualized revenue. The brokerage raised its price target on Meta's stock to $875.
UBS Global Wealth Management analysts said in a note Meta's Muse provides "early evidence that consumer AI agents could achieve broad adoption, offering new AI monetization opportunities beyond enterprise application."
But the rollout has also faced hiccups. Amazon said on Monday it had not authorized Muse to access its store and asked Meta to remove the e-commerce giant from the experience.
Muse appears to capture and store customer credentials and scrape account data, and does not identify itself when accessing customer accounts, Amazon added.
The company said it expects AI agents to operate transparently and provide an opt-out option.
Of the 64 brokerages that cover Meta's stock, 57 rate it "buy" or higher with a median price target of $760, according to data compiled by LSEG.
"Prior to Muse, investors had completely dismissed the idea that Meta would be able to release a personalized consumer AI agent, favoring (Alphabet) instead," Jefferies analysts led by Brent Thill said.
Meta's Muse comes after a series of setbacks with its Llama 4 models last year, including criticism over the benchmark results reported for early versions.

Source: Reuters

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ワシントン　２２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ワシントン　２２日　ロイター］ - ルビオ米国務長官は、トランプ大統領が２２日にニューヨークで行うウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領との会談について、ウクライナとロシアが互いにエネルギーインフラ攻撃を停止することについて協議すると明らかにした。

ルビオ氏はＦＯＸニュースの番組で「ウクライナのインフラが攻撃の標的とされず、ロシアのエネルギー供給も標的とされないエネルギーインフラ停戦は、素晴らしい案だと考えている。理想的な結果だ」と述べた。

また、米国関連の船舶や米国産石油の供給が、「恐らく意図的ではなく」ウクライナの標的になっていることが懸念事項だと指摘。「この問題には対処する必要がある。このような事態を容認することはできない」と述べた。

items.summary:

ブルームバーグ・ニュースが確認した会合のプログラムによると、アモデイ氏は安保理にオンラインで参加する。

国連のAIパネルで共同議長を務めるヨシュア・ベンジオ氏、ハギングフェイスのクレマン・デラングCEO、アルトマン氏も説明を行う。アルトマン氏の出席については、ロイター通信が以前報じていた。

今回の会合は、世界各国の首脳が集まる国連の年次会合に合わせて開催される。アモデイ氏らテック大手の経営者らは、AIの安全性を巡るリスクを相次いで警告しており、世界的に連携したAI規制の導入を求める声が挙がっている。

items.title: 中国、ディープシークとムーンショットを調査－インフォメーション
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国当局は、米アンソロピックが中国企業による同社のAIモデル「Claude（クロード）」を介した機密データの処理を指摘したことを受け、DeepSeek（ディープシーク）とムーンショットAI（月之暗面）のデータセキュリティーをめぐる調査に乗り出した。テクノロジー系ニュースサイトのジ・インフォメーションが事情に詳しい複数の関係者を引用して報じた。関係者の身元は明らかにしていない。

インフォメーションによると、国家インターネット情報弁公室（CAC）は、両社のオフィスに職員を派遣し、幹部や従業員から事情を聴取し、データセキュリティー上の違反があったかや、その深刻度を調べている。

中国政府は、米企業が所有するAIを介してデータを処理したことで、中国の軍や警察、企業に関する機密データが米国側に流出し、データセキュリティー関連法に違反した可能性を懸念しているという。CACとムーンショット、DeepSeekはインフォメーションのコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。

アンソロピックは今月公表した報告書で、ムーンショットやDeepSeekなどが、利用者に知らせないまま、自社のチャットボットに寄せられた質問をアンソロピックのクロードに送っていたと指摘した。

アンソロピックはさらに、ムーンショットが「蒸留」と呼ばれる手法を用いていたと主張。蒸留は、より高性能なAIモデルから得たデータを使って、性能の低いモデルを改良する手法だ。今回についてアンソロピックは、ムーンショットが同社のシステムから得た回答を、自社独自のソフトウエアの訓練に利用したとみている。

米安全保障当局は、DeepSeekやムーンショットを含む中国の主要AI企業が、蒸留を通じて米企業が持つ独自の知識を組織的に抽出していると指摘している。

原題：China Probes DeepSeek, Moonshot Over Data Security: Information

items.title: Trump threatens to annihilate Iran as diplomats push for deal at UN
items.author: Gram Slattery, Parisa Hafezi, Antoni Slodkowski
items.creator: Gram Slattery, Parisa Hafezi, Antoni Slodkowski
items.summary: US President Donald Trump warned on Tuesday that he could annihilate Iran if there is no deal to end the war, but also suggested an agreement could come soon amid a diplomatic push at the United Nations.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump warned on Tuesday that he could annihilate Iran if there is no deal to end the war, but also suggested an agreement could come soon amid a diplomatic push at the United Nations.
"I have a big decision to make," Trump said in a speech at the UN General Assembly in New York.
"Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before?... Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?"
In a statement on Tuesday, Iran's Armed Forces dismissed Trump's comments at the UN as "propaganda", saying their response is "full readiness to inflict more severe, crushing, and unpredictable blows on the aggressors."
But away from the fiery rhetoric, discussions continued to try to end the nearly seven-month conflict that began with joint US-Israeli strikes and has since killed thousands, driven up oil prices and drawn in neighboring countries.
US envoy Steve Witkoff in a post on X said that the United States and Iran engaged in lengthy talks on Tuesday on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly through mediators "who shuttled between the two sides throughout the day".
The mediators will continue their work, Witkoff added, saying that he hoped Tuesday's discussions would "prove constructive and promising."
Trump also met the leaders of Middle Eastern countries who are keen to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the conduit for a fifth of global oil and gas shipments before the war, but are wary of giving their longstanding rival Iran too much power.
Many also host huge US military bases that have come under repeated Iranian attack throughout the war.
"We think that the situation with Iran could end right after the (November 3) midterm elections, maybe before. I don't know. You never know," Trump said as he met the leaders.
The diplomatic maneuvering comes as Trump faces pressure on multiple fronts — rising energy costs at home, a widening regional conflict abroad, and the midterms six weeks away that could reshape his political standing. Whether talks produce a deal or the war escalates further carries consequences for global oil markets, Gulf security and millions of Iranians.
Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araqchi met with Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani of Qatar, which has spent months trying to de-escalate the conflict, the Qatari state news agency reported.
A senior Iranian official said Tehran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within days if the US eased military pressure and lifted its blockade on Iranian ports.
The senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran had conveyed its latest proposal to Washington through mediators last week and could reopen the strait to Gulf shipping within seven days if its demands were met.
In a reminder of Iran's firm position so far, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, who headed Iran's negotiating team at previous talks, said Iran would never surrender: "Trump must understand that he cannot impose his power on the Iranian people and its armed forces."
WIDENING REGIONAL CONFLICT On the table at the Gulf states' [USN:L1N45D0Z2 TEXT:"meeting with Trump"] is a Qatari proposal for a common security framework involving Iran and the Arab Gulf states, regional sources said. One source said Iran was reviewing the proposal.
Al Thani has said any such arrangement would need to provide security guarantees for the Gulf states and expand economic interdependence with Iran.
Saudi Arabia, the largest of the Gulf states, has been drawn deeper into the war this month as Iran-aligned Houthi fighters have advanced in Yemen, routing forces of the Saudi-backed government and threatening Saudi oil exports through the Red Sea.
The US, which bombed the Houthis for two months last year, has so far rebuffed repeated pleas from Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to rejoin the fight. The New York Times reported that Trump called off US strikes against the Houthis on Sunday at the last minute.
Asked why Washington had held back from striking the Houthis, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the United States would always support Saudi Arabia, adding:
"That said, that is a very dangerous and complex conflict that pre-exists ... We have a history with the Houthis as well, and that's something we don't want to see impacted either."
Oil markets did find some relief on Tuesday after sources told Reuters that Saudi Arabia had restarted operations at its [USN:L1N45E09V TEXT:"East-West Pipeline"] and could resume exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu within hours, albeit at reduced volumes.
The pipeline, Saudi Arabia's main export route bypassing wartime disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, had been shut after attacks this month that Riyadh blamed on Iranian-backed groups in Iraq.

items.title: 肥満症治療薬のノボノルディスク、薄毛治療分野への進出を模索
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 肥満症薬「ウゴービ」のメーカーであるデンマークの製薬会社ノボノルディスクは、消費者に直接販売する医薬品事業を拡大しようと、薄毛治療市場に注目している。

薄毛治療は依存症や更年期障害などとともに、ノボが自社の中核的な科学的専門知識、あるいは最近培われた処方薬を消費者に直接販売するノウハウと接点があるとみている分野の一つだ。

マーティン・ランゲ最高科学責任者（CSO）は22日のブルームバーグ主催のラウンドテーブルで、現在研究が進められている薄毛治療の科学の一部は、ホルモンの働きを調べる内分泌学を基にしており、ノボにはこの分野で長い歴史があると説明した。

ランゲ氏は「われわれの科学的知見を生かし、この分野に進出できる可能性はある」と述べ、「必ずしも最初に取り組む分野ではないが、明らかに可能性はあるだろう」と付け加えた。

急成長する肥満症治療薬市場でイーライリリーに首位の座を奪われたノボだが、肥満や糖尿病以外にも幅広い効果があるとみられるGLP-1受容体作用薬の用途をさらに広げたい考え。主力のウゴービと糖尿病治療薬の「オゼンピック」が2030年代の初めにかけて米国と欧州で特許が切れるのを前に、新たな成長分野を探っている。

同社は今週、投資家向け説明会で事業計画を示したが、具体的な内容に乏しいとして投資家は失望し、株価は急落した。

同社はまた、心臓病や肝疾患、血液疾患の新たな治療法も模索。補完的な買収を検討するとともに、社内の新薬開発パイプラインの迅速化も目指している。

ノボが薄毛治療市場に参入するとしても、時間はかかりそうだ。ランゲ氏は今年終盤または来年初めまでに中期段階の臨床試験に進めると見込まれる8つの疾患のリストを提示したが、薄毛治療は含まれていなかった。

競合の米イーライリリーも、女性医療など肥満症事業を補完し得る分野への進出を模索している。

原題：Ozempic Maker Novo Looks to Target Hair Loss in Consumer Push（抜粋）

Curious case of Pakistani prof Junaid Hafeez—blasphemy, ‘secret’ Facebook group, death penalty

Junaid Hafeez was accused of hosting Qaisra Shahraz, a prominent British-Pakistani novelist, as a guest speaker at Bahauddin Zakariya University and endorsing her allegedly blasphemous remarks.

Debdutta Chakraborty

22 September, 2026 05:17 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Junaid Hafeez went to the United States on a Fulbright scholarship at Jackson State University in Mississippi | Photo: Facebook

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

-->

New Delhi: Pakistan has never really hanged anyone for blasphemy. In author Mohammed Hanif’s words, the country simply fits a noose around a man’s neck each morning and loosens it each night — a mercy just enough to let the country’s conscience sleep. Pakistani professor Junaid Hafeez has been wearing that noose for 13 years.

Pakistanis have used multiple adjectives for him — promising, brilliant, a self-proclaimed romantic who loves books, poetry, and music, and a prisoner of conscience. None of it has helped him be acquitted. He remains in solitary confinement serving a death sentence since 2019. Both inside and outside the jail, his life remains in danger. 

Hafeez, a former visiting lecturer of English literature at Bahauddin Zakariya University in Multan, was arrested in March 2013, and accused of blasphemy for operating a secret Facebook group. 

Show Full Article

Hafeez was also accused of hosting Qaisra Shahraz, a prominent British-Pakistani novelist, as a guest speaker at Bahauddin Zakariya University and endorsing allegedly blasphemous remarks made during the lecture. Shahraz had to flee the country. 

In December 2019, after six years of adjournments and the transfer of judges, a trial court sentenced Hafeez to death. The Lahore High Court is scheduled to hear his case on Tuesday and rights activists are yet again calling for his release. 

In a video shared on X on Monday , activist Sheema Kermani called for a fair trial and his release. During the CJP protests in India, which saw a wave of support from Pakistan, author Mohammed Hanif called Hafeez a “Pakistan’s cockroach ” who has been behind bars, forgotten. 

The trial itself has become one of the most contentious cases in Pakistan’s legal history. Rashid Rehman, the lawyer who first took on Hafeez’s defence, was threatened openly in court by clerics and lawyers before he was shot dead in his office in 2014. In the years after, Hafeez was held in solitary confinement due to repeated attacks by other inmates, and the proceedings have been held behind closed doors, inside a high-security prison in Multan out of public view. 

According to his current lawyer, the case against him never came together. “The prosecution, the witnesses and trial could not prove any of the allegations,” the lawyer told The Guardian after Hafeez’s 2019 verdict. 

He recalled visiting Hafeez the night before the verdict and finding him almost lighthearted and certain, as everyone around him seemed to be, that acquittal was close.

What unfolded, however, the next day was what the lawyer described as “unprecedented”. Rather than presenting concrete evidence, the prosecutor told the judge that Hafeez was “against Islam” and reminded the court that the case was “sensitive”. 

“It was the point I realised they were just using the religious card,” the lawyer added, “which was an immoral and unethical precedent in the court.”

“Pakistan’s blasphemy laws operate as black laws—draconian, anachronistic statutes completely devoid of statutory safeguards and weaponised for personal or ideological vendettas. The case of academic Junaid Hafeez exposes how these edicts systematically dismantle judicial independence,” Pakistani lawyer Shafiq Ahmed told ThePrint.

“By substituting rigorous evidentiary standards with populist intimidation and silencing the defence through targeted terror, these laws strip citizens of their constitutional right to a fair trial. For the legal community, Hafeez’s conviction and his agonizing 13 years behind bars remain a grim indictment of a criminal justice system that routinely capitulates to majoritarian veto,” he added. 

From Jackson to jail
As a student, Hafeez initially studied medicine at Pakistan’s oldest medical college, the King Edward Medical University , in Lahore, but left after his first year to pursue English literature at Bahauddin Zakariya University, where he reportedly broke a decades-old academic record.

In 2009, he went to the United States on a Fulbright scholarship at Jackson State University in Mississippi , where he studied American literature, photography, and theatre. He returned to Pakistan in 2011, and became a visiting lecturer in the English department at his alma mater. He taught literature and invited outside speakers to the campus, including women’s rights activists.

Before his arrest, Islamist student groups had objected to what they described as his liberal teaching. Even finding a lawyer willing to represent Hafeez proved extraordinarily difficult. His father, Hafeez-ul Naseer, in a 2016 Dawn article recalled approaching one lawyer only to see him confronted by a large group of lawyers protesting his decision to take the case. 

Naseer talked about how he would take books for Hafeez to read from his personal collection, which the family said contained more than 6,000 volumes. By the time the trial court sentenced Hafeez to death in December 2019, he had already spent more than six years in prison. 

Also read: Almost all of Imran Khan’s family have been arrested. Three sisters picked up now

The burden of blasphemy in Pakistan
In Pakistan, accusations of blasphemy can carry consequences beyond the courtroom. According to a Human Rights Watch report, over 1,500 blasphemy cases have been lodged since the 1980s. Most turn out to be fabricated.

Human rights organisations have documented cases in which accusations have been accompanied by threats, mob violence, or attacks on those who defend the accused. Two prominent Pakistani figures who advocated changes to the blasphemy laws — former Punjab Governor Salman Taseer and former federal minister Shahbaz Bhatti — after a Christian woman, Aasia Bibi, was wrongfully convicted of blasphemy, were both assassinated in 2011.

That history hangs over Hafeez’s appeal. When an August 2026 Reuters report claimed that blasphemy cases had gone down under Pakistan’s de facto head, Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, many were quick to highlight Hafeez’s case.  

Ahmad Noorani, a Pakistani journalist, described the broader problem in stark terms. In his view, Hafeez’s case cannot be separated from the wider evolution of Pakistani society and the political use of religious sentiment. In the 80s, General Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq rewrote colonial-era blasphemy laws. His amendments tightened the hold of Sunni clerics and named specific offences like desecrating the Quran and insulting the Prophet’s companions. He outlawed Ahmadis from even calling themselves Muslim. The punishment was changed from 2-3 years to life imprisonment or death. 

“What happens when a state is built on religion? The country was founded on a premise that a nation could be built on the basis of religion and a few years later, that premise produced the man suited to carry it to its logical end: Zia-ul-Haq. Everything he did to this society — the fracturing, the unravelling — followed from that founding choice,” said Noorani.

“Hafeez, a well-educated man, a professor, was accused of something he almost certainly didn’t do, but the accusation itself made justice impossible. No lawyer could represent him and remain in the city. Any lawyer who tried was driven out. And when one finally came from elsewhere — Rashid Rehman — he was killed for it. Sit with that. Consider how hollow, how manufactured a case has to be, that the people behind it needed to remove every honest voice from the room before it could proceed,” he added . 

“This is what happens when you build a state on religion or build it on something else entirely and dress it in religion’s colours afterward. The wound doesn’t stay contained to one courtroom. It spreads,” he added.

Qindeel Azeem, a human rights activist who recently spoke to Hafeez’s lawyer, described Hafeez, now in his 40s, as a man who has developed mental health issues after years of imprisonment. His solitary confinement has itself become a form of punishment. His family has aged outside the prison walls. His father, now almost 70, refuses to give up. His mother has largely withdrawn from ordinary life. 

“The real challenge right now is that he appeal in the high courts is heard,” Azeem said.

“There’s a pattern we’ve watched for years — a date gets set, and then charges get quietly altered, or the paperwork ‘isn’t available,’ or the date just moves” .

She is hopeful they will see an acquittal this time. “It’s been years. Hafeez’s lawyer, Saif ul-Malook, is genuinely hopeful, that they’re finally about to hear it. And if they do, there’s a real chance he’s acquitted.”

According to her, what the lower courts want to avoid isn’t a wrongful conviction, it’s the fallout from an acquittal. She pointed to the Aasia Bibi case as the template: “Every time one of these ends in acquittal, right-wing factions of society are unwilling to accept the verdict. Years of indoctrination have resulted in radicalism where there is no differentiation between the innocent and the guilty. It doesn’t matter what the court finds. In the public’s mind, the verdict was already decided the day the accusation was made. That’s the narrative, and everyone in power has learned to tiptoe around it rather than confront it.”

Hafeez and his family meanwhile wait. His trial was relisted for a later date on Tuesday by the Lahore High Court.

As a Pakistani writer, Saki Nama, wrote on Facebook: “Among many other national sins, this one looks the gravest of all.”

(Edited by Aamaan Alam Khan)

items.title: SEBI says Adani firms paid 15 million rupees to settle disclosure violations
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: India's markets regulator said on Tuesday that four Adani companies, including the flagship Adani Enterprises and a former group firm, have paid 15.1 million rupees ($157,966.31) to settle proceedings over alleged disclosure violations.
items.body:
India's markets regulator said on Tuesday that four Adani companies, including the flagship Adani Enterprises (ADEL.NS) and a former group firm, have paid 15.1 million rupees ($157,966.31) to settle proceedings over alleged disclosure violations.
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in its order said Adani Enterprises had allegedly failed to disclose a related-party transaction in its annual report for the year ended March 2013.
The other companies, including AWL Agri Business Ltd (formerly, Adani Wilmar Ltd), were found to have filed certain audit or review reports signed by firms that did not hold a valid peer review certificate at the time.
SEBI had sent show-cause notices to these companies, outlining its allegations, in 2024. They settled without admitting or denying guilt.
These instances were part of 24 cases that the regulator had investigated following allegations by short-seller Hindenburg Research in January 2023 that the Gautam Adani-led group manipulated its share prices through the use of tax havens.
An Adani spokesperson did not immediately respond to Reuters request for comment on whether this settles all pending litigation.
The group has denied these allegations in the past.
The settlement further reduces regulatory uncertainty hanging over the Adani Group following the Hindenburg report.
Over the last year, SEBI has allowed settlements in several investigations arising from the review, including disclosure violations, alleged insider trading and audit-compliance. It separately closed proceedings in a case that examined whether inter-company loans were routed in a way that masked related-party transactions.
However, probes into whether certain offshore investors were used to circumvent Indian rules that require 25% of shares to be held by public shareholders and whether there was manipulation in trading of Adani Group shares are still pending.
($1 = 95.59 Indian rupees)

items.title: After karting fun, Verstappen looks to keep winning feeling going in Baku
items.author: Abhishek Takle
items.creator: Abhishek Takle
items.summary: Red Bull’s four-time champion Max Verstappen, fresh from a last-to-first karting triumph, will be looking to keep that winning feeling going by chalking up a first Formula One victory of the year at this weekend’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
items.body:
Red Bull’s four-time champion Max Verstappen, fresh from a last-to-first karting triumph, will be looking to keep that winning feeling going by chalking up a first Formula One victory of the year at this weekend’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
The Dutchman took just 14 laps and 35 minutes to scythe through a field of 100 competitors at Red Bull’s "Max vs. 100" karting challenge at Britain’s Silverstone last week.
That may have been nothing more than a fun exhibition event for the 71-times grand prix winner, who jokingly pointed out that it was his first win of the season.
But after six podium appearances, four in the last five races, and a second-place finish in Madrid Azerbaijan’s Baku street circuit could set the stage for Verstappen to break his victory duck for the year and become the venue’s first triple winner.
“Madrid was a good result for us and the team has been working hard on taking this positive momentum to make sure we maximise the performance of the car in Baku,” said the 28-year-old.
“We've made some good steps with the car over the last few races and we have some good memories here,” he added.
The Baku street track, a 6-km-long mix of flat-out blasts and tight corners, has a reputation for unpredictable races.
Seven different drivers have won the nine races at the venue, with Verstappen and former Mexican team mate Sergio Perez the only two to have won there more than once.
With safety cars a regular feature of the race, Verstappen’s victory hopes may well rest on Red Bull’s ability to take on the might of Mercedes. The team’s runaway championship leader Kimi Antonelli heads into the weekend gunning for a third straight win and ninth of the season.
The 20-year-old Italian, who won his home race at Monza from the back of the grid and followed that up with victory in the Spanish Grand Prix at the Madring, is 81 points clear of Briton George Russell, his team mate and closest title rival, after 14 rounds.
Russell and third-placed Ferrari rival Lewis Hamilton have both ruled themselves out of realistic title contention.
ANTONELLI CLOSING ON TITLE A win in Baku would only tighten Antonelli’s grip on the championship and move his prospect of becoming the first Italian to win a Formula One title since Alberto Ascari in 1953 further into the realm of when rather than if.
McLaren’s reigning champion Lando Norris, meanwhile, will be fired up to make up for the win that got away from him.The Briton had been leading comfortably from pole in Madrid and seemed on course for his third win from four races when an ill-timed virtual safety car went against him. He eventually had to settle for third.
French racer Isack Hadjar will return to action alongside Verstappen after recovering from a wrist injury that sidelined him for the last three races. Yuki Tsunoda is set to step back into his reserve role.
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the first of a "triple header" of races on consecutive weekends, is being run on Saturday this year with the country marking its Remembrance Day on Sunday.
Organisers are also celebrating a "Decade of Racin" in Baku, with the race joining the Formula One calendar in 2016 as the European Grand Prix. This year’s race will be the 10th around the Baku street track, with the event left off the calendar during the COVID pandemic in 2020.

items.title: DeepSeek, OpenAI and Anthropic to brief UN Security Council on AI this week
items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman plans to brief the meeting, where diplomats also expect participation from senior representatives of Anthropic ...
items.body:
Home / World News / DeepSeek, OpenAI and Anthropic to brief UN Security Council on AI this week

DeepSeek, OpenAI and Anthropic to brief UN Security Council on AI this week OpenAI CEO Sam Altman plans to brief the meeting, where diplomats also expect participation from senior representatives of Anthropic

Representative image for artificial intelligence (Photo: Reuetrs)

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Sep 23 2026 | 12:00 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Chinese AI startup DeepSeek will be among the ??companies briefing the United Nations Security Council this week on the risks posed by artificial intelligence, two sources familiar with the matter said, as world leaders gather in New York ??for the annual UN General Assembly.  
The 15-member Security Council is set to meet on Wednesday to discuss AI and international security, weeks after several AI industry leaders called for a coordinated slowdown of the development of the increasingly powerful AI systems, warning that they could soon improve on their own and slip beyond human control.
  OpenAI CEO Sam Altman plans to brief the meeting, where diplomats also expect participation from senior representatives of Anthropic, Reuters reported last week.
 

  DeepSeek and other Chinese AI firms including Moonshot have been invited to make statements, one of the sources said.
  DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng does not plan to attend, the source said, cautioning that plans remain fluid and could change at the last minute.
Also Read

Security Council must reflect reality of today's world: UN chief Guterres

AI amnesia: Why AI models sometimes forget what users ask them to remember

OpenAI's model solves 100+ maths problems, company forms advisory group

What is Jev? Inside the new AI model built to make software decisions

OpenAI, Anthropic weigh cross-testing deal as AI safety concerns grow

  DeepSeek and Moonshot did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
  The UN Security Council, which is charged with maintaining international peace and security, met for the first time on the risks of artificial intelligence in 2023. At the time, China warned the technology should not become a "runaway horse" and the US warned against its use to censor or repress people.

  UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned world leaders last week that rapidly advancing AI poses risks that cannot be ignored, putting him at odds with US President Donald Trump, who has argued existing safeguards are sufficient and China would benefit ??from the doubt being cast on AI development.
  Chinese state media have dismissed calls for a slowdown in AI development as stemming from a "Cold War playbook," aimed at preserving Washington's dominance in cutting-edge technology and excluding Beijing from the global AI governance system.
  Unlike leaders of US frontier labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic, the heads of China's leading model developers have rarely publicly articulated the possibility that increasingly capable AI systems themselves could deceive humans, evade control or cause catastrophic harm.

  They have also remained largely silent on those risks since the debate intensified in the US this month.
  Senior US and Chinese officials agreed to hold further talks on AI safety, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Monday, after meeting ahead of Trump's scheduled talks with Chinese president Xi Jinping later this week in Washington.

items.title: Global biofuel output to jump nearly 70% by 2030 due to Gulf energy crisis, study finds
items.author: May Angel
items.creator: May Angel
items.summary: Global biofuels output is expected to surge nearly 70% by 2030 from 2025 levels as major producing countries push ahead with raising blending mandates in response to the energy crisis triggered by the Iran war, a study published on Tuesday found.
items.body:
Global biofuels output is expected to surge nearly 70% by 2030 from 2025 levels as major producing countries push ahead with raising blending mandates in response to the energy crisis triggered by the Iran war, a study published on Tuesday found.
The study was co-authored by London-based think tank Chatham House and non-profit certification group the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC).
Biofuels such as ethanol can be produced from a range of organic feedstocks but are typically made from food crops or animal feed. They are commonly blended with gasoline or diesel and become more competitive as fossil fuel prices rise.
The fuels have long been at the centre of debate over whether they help tackle climate change or contribute to food inflation and deforestation. The study's authors warned that the latest surge in demand risks worsening the latter.
"By prioritizing energy security in the short term, some policy responses may be trading off against increased food insecurity in the medium term (and) any additional shock such as extreme weather could severely affect food prices," they said.
Countries including Brazil, China, India, Indonesia and the US, along with the European Union, have proposed or adopted higher biofuel blending mandates since the outbreak of the Iran war.
The authors estimate that if all proposed mandates are fully implemented, the land needed to produce biofuel feedstocks could more than double by 2030 compared with 2023 levels. That would require an additional 36 million hectares, an area roughly the size of Germany.
"The speed at which biofuel mandates are being increased creates significant risks as demand for feedstocks may rise faster than environmental safeguards, certification systems, land-use planning and enforcement mechanisms can be implemented," the authors said.
They said feedstocks grown on degraded land or between crop seasons can help reduce land degradation and even restore land, but that is not typically the case for conventional, or first-generation, biofuels.
First-generation biofuels are made from food and feed crops such as corn and sugarcane. Second-generation, or advanced, biofuels are produced from organic residues and waste materials such as used cooking oil.
"Production of feedstocks for first-generation biofuels tends to have net negative consequences for land degradation, food security and water use," the authors said.
Crude oil prices have risen nearly 40% since the Iran war began in late February, while sugar and corn prices have gained about 20%.

items.title: 原油下落､サウジがパイプライン再開を計画-ホルムズ巡る外交にも期待
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 22日のエネルギー市場では原油が下落。サウジアラビアが主要パイプラインを経由する輸送の再開を模索しているほか、ホルムズ海峡の再開に向けた外交努力が活発化する兆しも見られた。

北海ブレント原油は、一時1バレル＝98ドルを下回った。事情に詳しい関係者によると、サウジアラビアは今週の再稼働を視野にパイプラインの試験を実施しており、紅海沿岸のヤンブー港での積み出しも今週再開する見通しだという。

サウジの東西パイプラインは日量最大700万バレルの輸送能力を持ち、ホルムズ海峡を迂回する主要な輸送ルートとして利用されてきたが、今月ドローン攻撃を受けて停止していた。

また、ホルムズ海峡を巡る共同通信のニュースも手掛かりとなった。共同がイラン政府高官の話を基に報じたところによれば、イランは米国による港湾封鎖が解除されれば、7日以内にホルムズ海峡を再開するとの考えを米国側に示した。

また、イラン革命防衛隊は、国益にかなうのであれば交渉する必要があるとの見解を示したと国営イラン通信（IRNA）が伝えた。

ロンドン時間午前11時38分時点で、ブレント原油は2.5%安の1バレル＝97.81ドル。米ウェスト・テキサス・インターミディエート（WTI）は2.6%下げて93.28ドル。

items.title: Federations question Infantino reform pledge, demand deeper FIFA overhaul
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino's proposal to review the governing body's decision-making processes has failed to ease concerns among several member associations, with football officials in Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden and Wales saying the reforms do not address deeper leadership issues.
items.body:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino's proposal to review the governing body's decision-making processes has failed to ease concerns among several member associations, with football officials in Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden and Wales saying the reforms do not address deeper leadership issues.
In Monday's [USN:L1N45D0SB TEXT:"letter seen by Reuters"] , Infantino wrote to FIFA’s 211 member associations proposing an independent review of FIFA’s decision-making processes, as well as consultations on governance reforms, following a backlash over his failed attempt to sell a 20% stake in FIFA’s commercial operations, including rights associated with the World Cup.
Striking a conciliatory tone, Infantino also said he would propose consultations with confederations, member associations and other stakeholders about strengthening FIFA's decision-making.
The proposal to sell a stake in FIFA's commercial rights was [USN:L1N43X04P TEXT:"abandoned"] in July after strong opposition from continental confederations, with UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF accusing FIFA of pursuing the plan without adequate consultation.
Infantino has since faced a fierce backlash, with the European body expressing its loss of faith in the current president.
Infantino also said in the letter that member associations' positions on proposals or governance matters would not affect their treatment by FIFA, whose development and solidarity programmes would continue under existing rules.
The Swiss is up for reelection in March next year, with his opponents struggling to find a candidate to challenge him. People familiar with the discussions told Reuters this month that Infantino still appeared to have enough support to win another term, prompting critics to focus on curbing the powers of the FIFA presidency.
REFORMS FAIL TO WIN OVER CRITICS Germany's Football Association (DFB) President Bernd Neuendorf, a member of the FIFA Council, dismissed the letter on Tuesday as an attempt to secure another term in office.
"I regard Gianni Infantino's letter as a transparent ploy to secure his re-election next year," Neuendorf said.
"FIFA now seems to have recognised that changes are essential. However, Gianni Infantino is definitely not the right person to lead a reform process. He has squandered all credibility."
The Dutch Football Association (KNVB) echoed those concerns, saying the proposals had not restored trust despite containing some elements it had previously called for.
The KNVB, one of FIFA's founding members, last month proposed hosting an international summit in Amsterdam aimed at overhauling FIFA and has called for Infantino to be replaced by 2027.
"The proposed actions are partly in line with our call for reforms within FIFA. Practice will show whether that is actually the case," a Dutch FA spokesperson was quoted as saying by Dutch news agency ANP.
"At the same time, the proposals cannot be viewed separately from the (public) pressure, and they would not have emerged without the current dynamics."
CALLS FOR NEW LEADERSHIP Swedish Football Association President Simon Astrom welcomed parts of the proposal but said it fell short of the broader reforms required.
"The content of the letter is in line with what we have been calling for over a long period of time," Astrom said.
"These initiatives come late, and several of the measures should have been implemented long ago."
Astrom added that the letter had not altered Sweden's view that FIFA needed new leadership.
Football Association of Wales Chief Executive Noel Mooney also questioned characterisations of the letter as a major reform package.
"It doesn't actually say reform of FIFA itself. It talks about reform around strategic projects and initiatives," Mooney told BBC Radio Wales.
Mooney reiterated his opposition to the abandoned private investment plan, saying FIFA should use its existing financial resources to support member associations rather than seek outside investors.
"You're not looking for somebody to sell off parts of the game. The World Cup does not need private equity," he said.
items.raw_description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino's proposal to review the governing body's decision-making processes has failed to ease concerns among several member associations, with football officials in Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden and Wales saying the reforms do not address deeper leadership issues.

items.title: サウジ、東西パイプライン再稼働へ作業開始－週内の輸出再開目指す
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： サウジアラビアは、ホルムズ海峡の迂回（うかい）ルートとして使われてきた東西石油パイプラインについて、再稼働に向けた初期段階の作業を進めている。事情に詳しい関係者が明らかにした。

サウジは週内にパイプライン経由の輸出再開を目指していると、関係者の1人が匿名を条件に話した。複数の原油トレーダーによれば、パイプラインで運ばれた原油の積み出し港である紅海沿岸のヤンブーには、すでにタンカーが到着する兆候が出ている。

国営石油会社サウジアラムコとサウジのエネルギー省はコメント要請に応じなかった。

パイプラインが再稼働すれば、供給不足に陥っている原油市場に一定の安心感をもたらす。22日の原油相場は一段安となり、北海ブレントは一時1バレル＝98ドルを割り込んだ。パイプライン停止後、サウジは輸出を再びペルシャ湾岸に振り向けており、主要港ラスタヌラではここ数日、数百万バレルが積み出されたとみられている。

東西パイプラインが再開すれば、アラムコはヤンブーからの輸出を再び増やせる。同社はイラン戦争でホルムズ海峡の通航が大きく混乱する中、輸出の大半をヤンブー経由で行ってきた。事情に詳しいトレーダーらによると、アラムコは一部のアジアの製油会社に対し、ヤンブー港で原油を引き取れるようになると非公式に伝えている。

もっとも、リスクはくすぶる。イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派はサウジのインフラへの攻撃を続けている。サウジ南西部の製油所が攻撃を受けたほか、19日には首都リヤドで空襲警報が発令された。リヤドでの警報発令は、イラン戦争が最も激しかった3－4月以来初めて。また、フーシ派はサウジ船舶を対象に海上封鎖を宣言している。

東西パイプラインは10日、イラクから発射されたドローンの攻撃を受けた。その後、アラムコは損傷したポンプ施設を迂回して輸送を部分的に再開する作業を急ぐ一方、約6週間で全面的な能力回復を目指していると、ブルームバーグはこれまで報じた。輸送量をどの程度増やせるかは、損傷した施設の修復ペースに左右される。

items.title: 英国政府、8月までに約1.7兆円の借り入れ超過－来年度予算に逆風増す
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 英国政府の借入額が、4月からの会計年度の最初の5カ月間で773億ポンドに拡大し、予算責任局（OBR）の予想を81億ポンド（約1兆7100億円）上回った。インフレ上昇によって歳出が膨らんだためで、来月に初の予算案発表を控えるヒーリー財務相には打撃だ。

8月単月の借り入れも183億ポンドと、予想の148億ポンドを上回った。

会計年度の最初の5カ月間の税収は、OBRの予測を11億ポンド上回った。しかし、歳出が予測を74億ポンド上回った。このうち、年金を含む社会保障費が24億ポンド、債務利払い費が20億ポンドを占めた。

英政府統計局（ONS）の上級統計官トム・デービス氏は「財政赤字は昨年8月から約2割増加した。政府収入以上に支出が増えたためで、一部にはインフレの影響が出ている」と述べた。

借入額の拡大で、ヒーリー氏が予算案の策定を進める上で直面する課題が改めて明らかになった。同氏は予算案を通じてバーナム首相の経済構想を示すと同時に、政府借り入れが引き続き制御されていることを示し、神経質になっている債券市場を安心させる必要がある。

バーナム首相は、防衛や地方分権から住宅建設、社会福祉に至るまで野心的な計画を打ち出しているが、政策を実施する余地は極めて限られている。イラン戦争を一因とした借り入れコストの上昇により、財政ルールに対して確保していた236億ポンドの余力の半分がすでに失われたと推計されている。

家計がエネルギー料金の大幅な上昇に備える中、生活費を支援する追加策を打ち出すよう、バーナム氏への圧力も強まっている。同氏は、近く発表する予算案が「厳しい」ものになると認めている。

キャピタル・エコノミクスの英国担当副チーフエコノミスト、ルース・グレゴリー氏は、政府借入額の拡大について、歯止めのかからない支出の「惨たんたる状況」を示していると評した。同氏は近く発表される予算案について、「大規模な予算ではなく、小－中規模の増税・歳出措置を盛り込んだ予算となる可能性の方が高く、大幅な増税を避けるために首相の政策構想の多くが抑制されるとみている」と語った。

items.title: サウジ東西パイプライン稼働再開、紅海側で石油輸出22日にも開始
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［シンガポール／ニューデリー　２２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［シンガポール／ニューデリー　２２日　ロイター］ - サウジアラビアは原油を輸送する東西パイプラインの操業を再開した。西部の紅海沿岸のヤンブー港からの輸出は２２日中に再開する可能性がある。事情に詳しい複数の関係筋が明らかにした。

サウジは、ドローン（無人機）攻撃を受けて１３日に東西パイプラインを稼働を停止。ヤンブー港での原油積み出しも止まっていた。

関係筋によると、パイプラインは稼働再開したものの、流量は低水準にとどまっている。サウジアラムコは輸送量を日量４００万バレルに戻そうとしているという。治安筋は、完全再開には数週間かかる可能性があると述べた。

別の関係筋は、パイプラインの再開を受けて、紅海沿岸にあるアラムコの製油所向け原油供給も再開すると説明。２２日中にヤンブーで中国向けの原油タンカー１隻に積み込む予定だと述べた。

サウジの石油輸出再開に備え、商社は船舶間移送のためタンカーをエジプトの地中海沿岸にあるポートサイドやシディ・ケリールへ移動させているとされる。

サウジからの石油輸出再開の見通しとなり、北海ブレント先物は２ドル超下落し、９月８日以来の安値を付けた。［Ｏ／Ｒ］

items.title: Nasdaq reaches record high close, AI stocks rally
items.author: Noel Randewich, Johann Cherian
items.creator: Noel Randewich, Johann Cherian
items.summary: The Nasdaq notched a record high close on Tuesday, lifted by Micron Technology and other AI-related stocks, while the S&P 500 hovered just below a record high as oil prices traded around $100 per barrel.
items.body:
The Nasdaq notched a record high close on Tuesday, lifted by Micron Technology and other AI-related stocks, while the S&P 500 hovered just below a record high as oil prices traded around $100 per barrel.
Chip stocks added to recent gains while consumer-related software shares lost ground. Investors focused on the strong reception of Meta Platforms' AI assistant, which launched this month and can send emails and complete transactions on behalf of a user.
The success of the AI assistant, called Muse, has fueled gains for AI-related chip stocks in recent days. Yet some worried it could compete with retailers, online brokerages and other consumer companies. Amazon (AMZN.O) on Monday blocked the agent from shopping on its platform.
"There are a lot of tech stocks that are down today on Muse-related fears of one sort or another," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management. "People fear that Muse will be used to manage your insurance relationships, book your travel and search for stuff to buy."
Ride-hailing apps Uber Technologies (UBER.N) and Lyft (LYFT.O) lost more than 1% each, while Charles Schwab (SCHW.N) lost 6.1% and Airbnb (ABNB.O) declined 3%.
Micron (MU.O) rallied 5% and Sandisk (SNDK.O) gained almost 7%.
Oil prices were choppy near $100 a barrel, while the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note hovered around 4.94% after US President Donald Trump warned in a speech to the UN General Assembly that he could "annihilate the Islamic Republic" if no deal is reached to end the Middle East conflict.
Investors also awaited a US-China summit on Thursday, with traders speculating the [USN:L6N4560LG TEXT:"trade truce"] with Beijing could be extended and talks could touch on AI regulation.
"What people are looking for is at least the start of a conversation that maybe you can come up with some sort of global framework as opposed to fighting each other ..." said Joe Saluzzi, head of equity market structure research at Themis Trading.
The S&P 500 ended essentially flat at 7,764.64 points.
The Nasdaq gained 0.45% to 27,244.28 points, its second straight record high close.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.36% to 51,863.69 points.
Volume was heavy on US exchanges, with 17.9 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 16.3 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.
Six of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes declined, led lower by financials (.SPSY) , down 1.68%, followed by a 0.8% loss in communication services (.SPLRCL) .
The S&P 500 was less than 0.5% below its August 13 record high close.
JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) and Wells Fargo (WFC.N) both lost more than 3%.
Boston Federal Reserve President [USN:S0N43V06P TEXT:"Susan Collins"] wrote she supported last week’s interest rate increase, citing inflation risks.
New York Fed President [USN:S0N4490DM TEXT:"John Williams"] said the Fed's framework for controlling short-term rates has been effective in supporting financial markets.
Traders see a 53% chance the Fed will increase interest rates by at least 25 basis points in October, the CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed.
The S&P 500 saw about the same number of stocks climb as decline.
The S&P 500 posted nine new highs and 16 new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 48 new highs and 110 new lows.

items.title: Saudi Arabia restarts East-West oil pipeline, sources say
items.author: Trixie Yap, Nidhi Verma, Florence Tan
items.creator: Trixie Yap, Nidhi Verma, Florence Tan
items.summary: Saudi Arabia has restarted operations at its East-West Pipeline and could resume exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu later on Tuesday, three sources briefed on the matter said, as signs mounted of an increase in Middle Eastern oil flows.
items.body:
Saudi Arabia has restarted operations at its East-West Pipeline and could resume exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu later on Tuesday, three sources briefed on the matter said, as signs mounted of an increase in Middle Eastern oil flows.
The resumption of supplies on Tuesday helped to drive selling on global oil markets. Global oil benchmark Brent crude fell by more than $2 a barrel towards $97, its lowest since September 8.
Drone attacks, which Saudi Arabia has blamed on Iraqi militia, [USN:L6N455029 TEXT:"forced the kingdom"] to shut the pipeline on September 11, halting crude loadings at the kingdom's Yanbu port.
Since the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran disrupted oil flows from Saudi Arabia and its Gulf neighbours through the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh has been using the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels per day — around 4% of global supply — to Yanbu.
State oil firm Saudi Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
FULL RESUMPTION COULD TAKE WEEKS, SOURCES SAY The pipeline was pumping at a low rate after its restart, two of the sources said.
Aramco was seeking to get the pumping rate back to 4 million bpd, one of the sources said. The pipeline has a capacity of 7 million bpd.
Reaching a rate of 40% of capacity will take a couple of days and a full restart will take 6 to 8 weeks, a security source said. A separate oil industry source said a return to full pumping rates would take up to six weeks.
[USN:L6N4590YA TEXT:"Three pumping stations"] serving the pipeline were damaged in the drone attack, according to satellite imagery and industry sources. The line is serviced by 11 pumping stations and two separate pressure relief stations, according to industry assessments.
The pipeline will resume crude supply to Aramco refineries located on the Red Sea coast, one of the sources said, adding that one cargo was scheduled to load at Yanbu later on Tuesday. The person said it would be bound for China.
Traders were getting ready for Saudi oil loadings by moving tankers to Egypt's Mediterranean Port Said for ship-to-ship transfers and also to Sidi Kerir, another two trading sources said.
Oil prices have [USN:L1N45E01S TEXT:"also dropped this week"] after Iran said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and because Saudi Arabia has loaded more ships at its Ras Tanura port, raising expectations of increased exports through the Strait.

items.title: From smart glasses to AI pins, privacy fears challenge tech's next big bet
items.author: Aditya Soni, Kenneth Li
items.creator: Aditya Soni, Kenneth Li
items.summary: Companies betting AI devices will usher in a post-smartphone era are fueling privacy fears around the globe that could slow adoption of the emerging technology.
items.body:
Companies betting AI devices will usher in a post-smartphone era are fueling privacy fears around the globe that could slow adoption of the emerging technology.
The backlash against devices that can see, hear and respond to the world around them has been strongest against Meta's (META.O) Ray-Bans, which made smart glasses mainstream by pairing EssilorLuxottica's (ESLX.PA) trendy designs with AI from the social media giant chasing "personal superintelligence."
The glasses have become a lightning rod for growing unease over AI-powered devices, drawing scrutiny from courts weighing privacy lawsuits, users fearing covert recordings and critics warning of a future in which ubiquitous AI eyewear erodes expectations of anonymity and consent. Several UK venues, including one of the country's biggest pub chains, Wetherspoon (JDW.L) , have restricted the use of the frames.
Meta is expected to unveil camera-free smart glasses as early as Wednesday at its Connect conference, according to media reports, highlighting the balancing act facing companies seeking a share of the more than $600 billion smartphone market.
Device makers are trying out a range of form factors to get past those concerns, from glasses and pins to pendants and voice recorders that clip magnetically to a phone, according to Reuters interviews with nearly a dozen technology executives, analysts and legal experts. Some firms are finding faster traction with businesses than consumers.
The outcome of the privacy debate could shape a market that tech firms see as the next major computing platform. If companies fail to win public trust, the same features that make AI-powered wearables useful — always-on cameras, microphones and environmental awareness — risk becoming the barrier to their adoption.
SAMSUNG PLANS PARTNERSHIP APPROACH "The winning form factors will be the ones that make interaction more natural, useful and trusted," said Jay Kim, executive vice president at Samsung's (005930.KS) mobile division, in an interview with Reuters in July. As AI takes on more tasks, he said, users will demand systems that remain secure and under their control.
Samsung plans to enter the smart-glasses market later this year through partnerships with Gentle Monster and Warby Parker (WRBY.N) , but does not view the devices as replacements for smartphones.
For some startups, however, solving the privacy problem may be existential.
ALTMAN'S VISION FOR LOCAL AI PROCESSING Speaking with journalists in December, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman described his vision for an [USN:L1N3XG17E TEXT:"always-on device"] capable of understanding a user's surroundings while knowing when to help and when to stay silent. He argued that such products would ultimately need to process data locally rather than continuously send information to the cloud.
"You want a device that you can trust ... that can have full context and know when to be helpful, when not to," he said. "If a device is going to be listening to your whole life and watching your whole life, most people will not want that running on a cloud server." He added that local AI processing "may take a couple of years longer" depending on how quickly OpenAI can scale its processors.
Experts say the central challenge is that AI devices become more useful as they collect more information about their surroundings. That information can include footage of people who never consented to being recorded.
LAWSUIT ALLEGES COVERT RECORDINGS "It's not always obvious to the consumer what it is they're giving up in terms of privacy to enjoy these new, efficient consumer products that make their lives more productive and more frictionless," said Ryan Clarkson, whose firm represents consumers suing Meta and Luxottica of America over allegedly misleading privacy claims involving their smart glasses.
The lawsuit alleges that human annotators viewed and labeled recordings of people changing clothes, using bathrooms and handling financial information after footage captured by the glasses was uploaded to Meta's servers to train its AI systems.
Those recorded often appeared unaware they were being filmed, Clarkson said. "No reasonable consumer who was promised privacy could ever have concluded these devices would intentionally or inadvertently capture them in their most private moments," he told Reuters.
Luxottica and OpenAI did not immediately respond to requests by Reuters for comment.
Meta said a light that cannot be turned off during filming protects the privacy of people around the user, and that the camera is disabled if the light is covered or tampered with.
The company also said it disagrees with the allegations in the lawsuit and will contest them, adding that reviewing user data to improve products was a common practice across the industry and that Meta filters out identifying information.
STARTUPS OFFER CAMERA-FREE ALTERNATIVES The privacy backlash has led other companies to consider glasses without cameras.
Even Realities, a Shenzhen-based startup founded by former Apple (AAPL.O) engineer Will Wang, who worked on the Apple Watch, introduced its camera-free G1 glasses in 2024. Its latest flagship, the G2, launched in November 2025.
Wang told Reuters in July that consumers increasingly associate smart glasses with covert recording and that cameras should wait until companies can put stronger safeguards in place. The company, whose valuation hit $1 billion in July, expects to end the year with a few hundred thousand users. Consumers account for about 90% of its sales, Wang said.
San Francisco-based Pocket is betting that a phone-mounted recorder that requires users to press a button to capture conversations can ease privacy concerns around audio-only devices by making recording as deliberate and visible as using a phone camera. The company said that about 170,000 Pocket devices were in use eight months after launch, including by workers at firms such as DoorDash (DASH.O) , Michelin and Santander.
Plaud, which sells card-shaped and wearable AI recorders, has also prioritized privacy with Plaud One, a $249.99 Explorer Edition earbud-and-case system that records only when activated and alerts bystanders through lights or an audio announcement. The company has 2.5 million users and more than $100 million in annual recurring revenue.
Privacy concerns sparked by AI devices are not unprecedented, said Jitesh Ubrani, director at research firm IDC, noting that smartphones faced similar unease when cameras and microphones first became ubiquitous.
"As a society, we want to make sure there’s consent and awareness when people are being recorded," Ubrani said. "That’s different from being opposed to recording altogether."
items.raw_description: Companies betting AI devices will usher in a post-smartphone era are fueling privacy fears around the globe that could slow adoption of the emerging technology.

items.summary: "I believe we'll make a deal right after the election because it doesn't make sense for them not to. They're waiting to ??see how I do in the midterm election," Trump said during a speech ...

Home / World News / May make a deal with Iran after mid-term US elections: Trump at UNGA

May make a deal with Iran after mid-term US elections: Trump at UNGA "I believe we'll make a deal right after the election because it doesn't make sense for them not to. They're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election," Trump said during a speech

US President Donald Trump (Photo: PTI)

Reuters 2 min read Last Updated : Sep 23 2026 | 12:11 AM IST

Listen to This Article

President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that Washington and Tehran were moving toward a settlement, while a senior Iranian official said Tehran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within days if the US eased military pressure and lifted its blockade on Iranian ports.  
Trump's remarks came just hours after he repeated a threat at the UN General Assembly to annihilate Iran if it failed to strike a deal.
  Speaking after a meeting with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham at the United Nations in New York, Trump said: "They want to talk to us. They have been talking to us, even today they've been talking to us, and the relationship is developing.
 

  "But we can't let them - and they understand that - we can't let them have a nuclear weapon."
  He gave no details on the talks. No face-to-face meetings between Iran and the United States are known to have taken place since July, when an agreement on an interim deal to end the war collapsed weeks after it was signed.
Also Read

  Earlier, in a combative speech to the UN, Trump gave no sign of readiness to compromise. He called for Iran's complete economic isolation and said he believed a deal would be done after November's midterm elections "because it doesn't make sense for them not to. They're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election."

  Trump faces growing domestic discontent over the unpopular Iran war, rising energy costs and stubbornly elevated inflation.
Iran had earlier signalled a willingness to revive negotiations to end their almost seven-month-old conflict, with the presidents of both countries due at the UN for the annual gathering.
  The senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran had conveyed its latest proposal to Washington through mediators last week and could reopen the Strait of Hormuz to Gulf shipping within seven days if its demands were met.

items.title: 米国債利回り、今後1カ月に低下する可能性－HSBCの新AIモデルが示唆
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）： 英銀HSBCが開発した新たな機械学習モデル「DUSTIN（Directional US Treasury
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 英銀HSBCが開発した新たな機械学習モデル「DUSTIN（Directional US Treasury Indicator）」は、米国債利回りが今後1カ月に低下するとの見方を示している。

トーマス・デブリン氏ら同行のアナリストは、「米国債イールドカーブの短期ゾーンにある3カ月物と2年物で最近売りが進んだことに加え、経済活動を巡る予想外の動きが、今後1カ月の金利低下に対するDUSTINの確信度を高める要因となっている」と20日に公表したリポートで記した。

DUSTINは、米10年債利回りが1カ月後に上昇している確率を予測するモデルで、現在はその確率を28%と見込んでいる。

HSBCによると、このモデルは変化の速いシグナルをより明確に読み取れるよう設計されている。インフレリスクや金融政策を巡る期待の変化、米金融政策当局の信認を巡る問題などが判断材料に含まれる。

アナリストらによれば、過去データを用いた検証でも、このモデルのシグナルはその後の10年債利回りの動きと「明確な関係」を示した。さらに重要なのは、シグナルが1カ月という予測期間を超えて持続する場合があるという。

アナリストらは「DUSTINのシグナルに従った投資戦略を過去のデータで検証したところ、年率リターンは6.7%となり、米10年債を単純に保有した場合の2.3%を上回った」と記した。

原題：HSBC’s New AI Model Points to Lower US Yields One Month From Now
